key_findings: None of the bank-ledger rails can sense a purchase while it happens (IN-SPEND). Plaid checks each institution only 1-4 times per day (Plaid OpenAPI 1.762.0). EU unattended account access is capped at 4 calls per day (a Berlin Group bank spec enforces frequencyPerDay <= 4). India's Account Aggregator fair-use template for purpose 102 (spending/budgeting) allows at most 45 fetches per calendar month. So BRAKE must use ledger data to confirm and correct what alert signals report, and as pre-spend context, never as its real-time trigger.

Plaid is the only turnkey MVP ledger source. Its Link CountryCode enum covers exactly 20 countries: US, CA, GB, IE, ES, NL, FR, DE, IT, PL, DK, NO, SE, EE, LT, LV, PT, BE, AT, FI. It does not cover India, Brazil, Australia or Mexico. Build on /transactions/sync (cursor, count 1-500, added/modified/removed) triggered by the SYNC_UPDATES_AVAILABLE webhook, with a timer-based fallback poll.

Matching a pending record to its later posted record only works natively in Plaid (pending_transaction_id on the posted record). The Australian CDR standard says it gives no guarantee of correlating pending with posted. In Brazil a transactionId can change until the record reaches TRANSACAO_EFETIVADA. UK OBIE marks records Mutable/Immutable. The India AA deposit schema contains posted transactions only. Fusion therefore needs namespaced, mutable-until-final provider ids plus fuzzy pending-to-posted matching.

India's Account Aggregator data can only be consumed by a regulated FIU (RBI NBFC-AA Master Direction, not re-verified this session), so BRAKE needs a regulated FIU partner or its own licence. Under the purpose-102 template: PERIODIC fetches, consent of at most 1 year, at most 13 months of data per request, at most 45 pulls per month, and a 31-day Data Life after which the FIU must purge the data (one template variant is 7 days). This forces a 'derive, then forget raw' architecture.

Sign conventions differ by regime and must be normalized to direction plus a positive amount at the adapter boundary. Plaid: positive = outflow. CDR: negative = outgoing. UK OBIE, Brazil and AA: unsigned amount plus a debit/credit indicator. The AA deposit and credit-card XSDs type amount as xs:float, so parse it as a decimal string.

Recurring-obligation data is the most decision-relevant pre-spend output of these rails. Examples: Plaid /transactions/recurring/get streams (predicted_next_date; status MATURE, EARLY_DETECTION or TOMBSTONED; an add-on needing an access request and ideally 180+ days of history); MX repeating_transactions (predicted_occurs_on); UK /standing-orders, /direct-debits and /scheduled-payments; Brazil LANCAMENTO_FUTURO entries up to 12 months ahead; AA credit-card dueDate and totalDueAmount.

Plaid personal_finance_category carries confidence_level (VERY_HIGH >98%, HIGH >90%, MEDIUM, LOW, UNKNOWN), and counterparties[] carry a type and confidence. Customers that enabled Transactions on or after 3 Dec 2025 receive only taxonomy v2. Every BRAKE CategoryHint must record provider, taxonomy and version.

US Section 1033 data-access rights were not being enforced as of Sept 2026. Evidence: Plaid's OpenAPI says its 1033 reauthorization field is 'not currently used… may enable… if 1033-related expiration begins to be enforced'. BRAKE should not plan on a free, guaranteed regulatory access right, and should expect bank access fees to flow through aggregator pricing.

Licensing route by region: aggregator contract only in the US; AISP registration or the aggregator agent/licence-as-a-service model in UK/EU; a regulated FIU in India; a BCB-authorised receiver in Brazil; ADR status or a CDR representative arrangement in Australia. The pragmatic start is the aggregator-licence model in UK/EU and a regulated FIU partner in India.

Avoid GoCardless Bank Account Data for new builds: its official client libraries are marked 'no longer actively updated or maintained' (last release April 2025). SGFinDex in Singapore is closed to third-party apps (unverified). Direct Akoya/FDX integration is unnecessary when aggregators already cover it.

UK OBIE v4.0.1 has no push events for new transactions; its event-notification spec defines only resource-update events, so UK/EU AIS is poll-based. Its transaction records are rich: MerchantDetails.MerchantCategoryCode, CardInstrument.AuthorisationType, TransactionReference (FPID), CreditorAccount/DebtorAccount, and ISO purpose codes.

Every aggregator integration needs a backend for secrets, tokens, webhooks and AA FIU decryption keys. To respect local-first, BRAKE should run a minimal token-vault-and-relay that pulls deltas, forwards only normalized observations (or encrypted deltas) to the device, keeps only cursors, and enforces per-source retention and real provider-side revocation on disconnect.

key_findings: No card or wallet source in this stream gives a third-party consumer app a universal, consented, real-time feed of all card spending. Fast feeds are limited to one institution (Monzo, Up, Investec), to a merchant subset (Fidel Select tracks only 'purchases at locations in the program'), or to a card BRAKE itself issues. Card data must be a patchwork of adapters governed by the capability registry.

Apple FinanceKit is the only sanctioned iOS feed of bank or card transactions. It covers Apple Card, Apple Cash and Savings in the US (iOS 17.4+) and UK open-banking connected accounts in Wallet (iOS 18.4+). It needs the managed entitlement com.apple.developer.financekit (organization account, Account Holder request, per bundle ID, Finance category, 'financial management tools'). Data stays on device. Recommend 'next' and apply early.

FinanceKit is a POST-SPEND source, not IN-SPEND. The iOS 26 BackgroundDeliveryExtension wakes the app at most hourly ('.hourly = notified within an hour of data updating'). Transaction exposes id (device-scoped, stable across status changes), status (authorized/pending/booked/rejected/memo), transactionType (17 cases including transfer, refund, directDebit) and merchantCategoryCode, which helps directly with the transfer-vs-spending problem.

Apple Wallet Orders and the iOS 26 Mail-based automatic order tracking are write-only for third-party apps (FinanceKit has saveOrder(signedArchive:) but no read API). Item-level purchase context on iOS must come from email or receipts, not Wallet.

True IN-SPEND decisioning requires an issuer authorization hook. Adyen relayed authorisation must be answered within two seconds, after which Adyen applies your fallback logic. Stripe Issuing uses the issuing_authorization.request webhook, Lithic uses HMAC-signed Auth Stream Access, and Marqeta uses Gateway JIT with Commando Mode fallback. A BRAKE-issued card only sees spend on that card and brings sponsor-bank, KYC, Reg E or e-money obligations. Recommend 'later', as an opt-in commitment-card product with fail-open defaults.

Investec Programmable Banking Card Code (South Africa) lets users run their own JavaScript beforeTransaction(authorization) returning true or false on their own bank card. It is a working reference design for a user-owned in-spend rule hook without BRAKE being an issuer (niche reach; recommend 'research').

Neobank personal APIs give seconds-latency POST-SPEND webhooks but are not licensed for public apps. Monzo states its API 'is not suitable for building public applications', limits use to a 'small set of users you explicitly allow', retries webhooks up to 5 times and limits history to 90 days after the first 5 minutes. Up issues Personal Access Tokens only (beta). Revolut retail data is available only to regulated TPPs via its Open Banking API (same 5-minute / 90-day rule). Use these for internal dogfooding; reach users through regulated open banking or FinanceKit.

Card-linked offer infrastructure (Fidel Select, Visa/Mastercard CLO, Cardlytics) is merchant-subset coverage with spend-promoting economics that conflict with BRAKE's mission. Do not rely on it for coverage or take offer revenue. If it is used at all, use it only for user-chosen protective merchant watch-lists, and mark it coverage_scope=merchant_subset so silence is never read as no spending.

Wallet histories (PayPal, Venmo, Cash App, Paytm, PhonePe, Amazon Pay, GCash, GrabPay, M-Pesa) have no verified consumer-consented third-party data APIs. PayPal Transaction Search needs the partner network and lags up to 3 hours. These wallets must be sensed through notifications, SMS (M-Pesa transaction codes, UPI RRN), emails and the matching funding-bank or card debit, with a strong transfer/shared-expense prior for P2P apps.

App-store purchase data is strictly first-party. StoreKit, the App Store Server API, showManageSubscriptions(in:) and Play Billing expose only the calling app's purchases. Subscription intelligence must rely on Apple/Google receipt emails (renewal dates enable PRE-SPEND renewal nudges) plus bank or card descriptor matches.

Open Finance Brasil's credit-card API (reaching Nubank customers via authorised participants) exposes payeeMCC, billId, instalment fields (chargeIdentificator/chargeNumber), a 12-month history and a 7-day transactions-current window. BRAKE's TransactionCandidate schema should model instalment groups and bill-cycle membership now, so one purchase is not counted as N impulse buys.

The adapter layer needs a separate synchronous DecisionHook interface for issuer and Card Code authorizations (hard deadline of about 2 s, precomputed rules only, no model calls, fail-open, audited), distinct from the asynchronous, idempotent SignalSource observation adapters. Webhook adapters must verify HMAC signatures (Up X-Up-Authenticity-Signature, Fidel x-fidel-signature plus timestamp) and dedupe retries.

key_findings: NotificationListenerService should be BRAKE's Android MVP sensor. It sees bank, card, UPI and wallet push alerts, and bank SMS/RCS through the messaging app's MessagingStyle notification, within seconds of the alert and with no SMS permission. Access is a user-granted special access; no Play declaration form specific to NLS was found (unverified for 2026).

Android 15+ redacts OTP-bearing notifications for untrusted listeners: the title becomes the app label, the text becomes 'Sensitive notification content hidden', action titles are blanked and BigText/Messaging bodies are replaced. 'Trust' needs RECEIVE_SENSITIVE_NOTIFICATIONS (signature|preinstalled|knownSigner|role) or a companion-device association, neither of which BRAKE can legitimately obtain. Card-authentication OTP messages are therefore not a usable IN-SPEND signal.

Android 17 withholds OTP-containing SMS from non-exempt SMS-reading apps for 3 hours. This applies to WebOTP/Retriever formats for all apps and to standard SMS for apps targeting API 37; SMS_RECEIVED_ACTION is withheld and provider queries are filtered.

Google Play lists an exception 'SMS-based money management — apps that track and manage budget' covering READ_SMS, RECEIVE_SMS, RECEIVE_MMS and RECEIVE_WAP_PUSH, but it needs an approved Permissions Declaration and Play frames exceptions as temporary and only where no alternative exists (seen via Play Help search excerpts; the page itself was blocked). The main value of READ_SMS over NLS is onboarding backfill, so it is 'next', not MVP.

Sideloading as a way around Play is shrinking. Android 13+ restricted settings block NLS and Accessibility grants for sideloaded APKs. Developer verification is enforced for participating stores in Brazil, Indonesia, Singapore and Thailand from 2026-09-30 and goes global in 2027 (the advanced flow has a 24-hour wait). Android 16 Advanced Protection Mode blocks sideloading.

Android PRE-SPEND should rely on user-initiated surfaces. MVP: share target (ACTION_SEND), text-selection 'Ask BRAKE' (ACTION_PROCESS_TEXT), widgets (RemoteViews have no EditText) and paste-on-tap (background clipboard reads are impossible since Android 10; Android 12+ shows a toast). Next: a Quick Settings tile with the Android 13 requestAddTileService prompt.

App-open detection via UsageStatsManager needs the PACKAGE_USAGE_STATS app-op. It returns null while the device is locked, events are 'only kept … a few days', and there is no public push callback, so it means polling; the new queryAppUsageDuration requires internal|role QUERY_APP_USAGE. Classify it as research. AccessibilityService and SYSTEM_ALERT_WINDOW overlays should be avoided: untrusted touches are blocked since Android 12, setHideOverlayWindows exists, Android 15 narrowed the FGS exemption, and policy and ethics argue against them.

One-tap labelling on Android supports 3 action buttons (Notification.MAX_ACTION_BUTTONS = 3) plus app-supplied RemoteInput.setChoices() chips, which AOSP SystemUI renders as smart replies with precedence over assistant suggestions, plus free-text direct reply. The registry surface should be maxQuickActions = 3, supportsTextInput = true; OEM rendering of chips is unverified.

BRAKE can register a upi:// intent filter, appear in the chooser and forward a freshly built intent to the user's UPI app (Android 16 intent-redirection hardening rules out re-launching the received intent). This puts BRAKE inside a regulated payment flow, changes the caller the PSP app sees, and risks default-handler 'hijack', so it is research/avoid for MVP.

AppFunctions (Android 16+, an MCP-like tool API called by agents holding EXECUTE_APP_FUNCTIONS) is the forward path for 'Hey Gemini, should I buy this?'. Gemini integration was in private preview with trusted testers as of May 2026; App Actions remains documented but is the legacy path.

Since 2026-08-31 Play has required new apps and updates to target API 36. The SMS/Call Log policy revision announced 2026-07-15 takes effect 2027-01-27, and the change visible in the search excerpts only removes phone-call verification as a READ_CALL_LOG use.

key_findings: iOS has no NotificationListenerService, SMS-inbox or accessibility-service equivalent; a Notification Service Extension only modifies BRAKE's own remote pushes. iPhone users therefore get passive real-time spend sensing only from the Shortcuts Wallet Transaction trigger, FinanceKit (stream 02), server-relayed aggregator data, or user-initiated capture.

The Shortcuts Wallet 'Transaction' trigger (iOS 17+) is the only near-real-time IN-SPEND/POST-SPEND iOS signal that needs no entitlement. It passes card/pass, merchant and amount into a BRAKE App Intent that can run in the background (iOS 26 supportedModes, about 30 s budget) and can be set to Run Immediately. It covers Apple Pay taps only, the user must build the automation by hand, and it does not work for Apple Watch taps (forum, Mar 2026).

Apple Developer Forums show the Wallet trigger is unreliable. It times out while waiting for issuer data (FB14035016/FB16379100, unresolved as of Feb 2026, worse for some Mastercard issuers), fires on declined transactions, and occasionally delivers an empty merchant or a 0.0 amount to custom App Intents. BRAKE must ingest it as status=pending with medium confidence, treat 0/blank as missing, and track automation health with a heartbeat.

Screen Time shields (FamilyControls individual auth + ManagedSettings + a ShieldConfiguration extension with title/subtitle/two buttons/secondaryButtonSubmenuItems) are BRAKE's strongest PRE-SPEND friction lever. From iOS 26.5, ShieldActionResponse.openParentalControlsApp lets a shield hand off to BRAKE's own app, which Apple called unsupported until then; private-API workarounds were rejected in May 2026.

DPLA section 3.3.3(P) limits Family Controls data to providing usage controls, bans sharing it with third parties, and bans transmitting it off the device. Guideline 4.10 bans monetizing Screen Time APIs. BRAKE needs a sealed device_local_only module for shield and DeviceActivity events that sync and analytics cannot read.

The Family Controls distribution entitlement had a 2026 review backlog (waits of 9 days to over a month, Mar-May 2026). DTS said in April 2026 that approval is now team-scoped. BRAKE should apply in week 1 and use the Shortcuts 'App opened' automation (the one sec pattern) as a no-entitlement fallback; that fallback is fragile (iOS 26.6 'When App Is Closed' regression, FB24505842).

One-tap labeling is feasible. The HIG allows up to four action buttons in the expanded notification, UNNotificationCategory docs say banners show only the first two, UNTextInputNotificationAction gives free text, and a Notification Content Extension (iOS 12+) can render interactive chips. Design: top-2 predicted labels first, a third choice, and an 'Other…' text-input action.

The SMS Message Filter extension cannot legitimately feed BRAKE. It only sees SMS/MMS from unknown senders, cannot write to containers shared with the app, has no direct network access (only a system POST of sender+text to the developer server), and Guideline 2.5.12 bans using that data for other purposes. Indian bank-SMS signals on iPhone must come from Account Aggregator or email instead.

EU-only iOS capabilities are not appropriate for BRAKE. approvedWithDataAccess/FamilyActivityData (iOS 26.4+, EU device and EU account) is limited to one app per device and displaces Apple's Screen Time. TelephonyMessagingKit (iOS 26) requires being the default SMS app. NFC HCE CardSession is EEA-only and for payment apps. They belong in the capability registry, not the roadmap.

User-initiated iOS capture is global, cheap, low-risk and should be the MVP backbone for 'User C'. It comprises App Intents/App Shortcuts (Siri, Spotlight, Action button, iOS 18 Controls), a Share extension for product URLs and screenshots, UIPasteControl (prompt-free paste), DataScannerViewController (A12+, TextContentType.currency, barcodes/QR) and a Safari Web Extension with per-site Ask/Allow/Deny permission for web checkout. No finance or shopping App Intents schema domain exists for Apple Intelligence.

On-device processing is now practical but device-gated. Foundation Models (iOS 26+, Apple Intelligence devices; Apple's Feb 2026 note cites a 4,096-token context; iOS 27 adds image prompts with Vision OCRTool/BarcodeReaderTool) and Vision RecognizeDocumentsRequest (iOS 26, receipts with tables/lists) allow local parsing. The capability registry must model device class (A12+, Apple Intelligence-eligible), not just OS and country.

Live Activities (max 8 h active + 4 h on the Lock Screen, 4 KB payload, no network or location, HIG says avoid sensitive info) and widgets (no text input, buttons inactive while locked) can serve shopping-session and glanceable budget surfaces. Lock Screen visibility and Guideline 4.5.4 (no sensitive info in pushes) mean numbers should be hidden by default, and server data should arrive as E2E-encrypted pushes decrypted in an NSE.

remaining_concerns: The biggest architecture risk is now policy eligibility, not engineering. The current DPLA 3.3.3(P) primary-purpose clause may make Family Controls (shields, DeviceActivity) unavailable to a spending-decision app. BRAKE should hold an App Review consultation before investing in the sealed Screen Time module, and the doc's PRE-SPEND strategy should not depend on shields.

key_findings: A user-initiated 'Scan with BRAKE' QR flow is the best MVP payment-rail signal. It is the only rail-level signal that reliably precedes authorisation on both Android and iOS. One EMVCo MPM TLV parser (tags 00-63; CRC-16/CCITT-FALSE, poly 0x1021, init 0xFFFF) plus a GUID-keyed profile registry decodes Bharat QR, Pix, SGQR/PayNow, PromptPay, DuitNow, QRIS, VietQR and KHQR. A second parser handles upi://pay URIs.

Static QRs (EMV tag 01=11, or UPI without am) give payee identity but no amount. Dynamic QRs (01=12, or UPI am+tr) give the amount and a merchant reference. A dynamic Pix code may hold the charge behind tag 26.25 (a location URL), and BRAKE should not fetch it by default for privacy reasons. For static codes BRAKE must ask for a user-declared amount.

Intercepting upi:// intents on Android is technically possible: any app can declare the scheme and Android shows a disambiguation dialog. To do it, BRAKE must forward the URI byte-for-byte (signed intents use mode 02/05 with sign as the final SHA-256-with-RSA tag and orgid) and relay txnId/responseCode/ApprovalRefNo/Status/txnRef back to the merchant app. No NPCI rule covering non-PSP intermediaries was found, so this is 'research', not MVP.

iOS gives BRAKE no interception position. Apple documents that if multiple apps register the same URL scheme 'the app the system targets is undefined', and canOpenURL hand-off probing is capped at 50 LSApplicationQueriesSchemes entries (25 for apps linked on iOS 27+). The iOS QR flow must hand off through a curated, remotely updated list of app-specific schemes.

UPI is no longer just a bank debit. Funding can come from UPI Lite (Rs 1,000 per transaction, Rs 5,000 balance), a RuPay credit card, a pre-sanctioned credit line (purpose-bound since OC-171A), a Reserve Pay block (all funding sources since OC-228), or a UPI Circle delegate (Rs 5,000 per transaction, Rs 15,000 per month, extended to IoT/software delegates by OC-201B). Observations must carry payment_rail, funding_instrument and initiator as separate fields to avoid double counting and transfer mislabelling.

P2P vs P2M can be inferred from the payload: mc (MCC 7407 marks P2PM small merchants, with limits of Rs 10k per transaction, 25k per day and 1L per month), sign+orgid (verified merchant), tr/dynamic amount, and EMV tag 52. P2P collect requests have been discontinued since 1 Oct 2025 (OC-220), so any incoming collect request is merchant-initiated.

UPI AutoPay pre-debit notifications (24 h before execution, with MCC exemptions such as FASTag/NCMC) are a genuine PRE-SPEND subscription signal. OC-223 lets users view and port mandates across UPI apps, but no third-party API exists, so capture depends on the SMS and notification adapters.

UPI app share is concentrated but shifting. In May 2026 PhonePe had about 46-49%, Google Pay about 33-38% and Paytm about 6-8%; PhonePe plus Google Pay fell to 79%, their first sub-80% reading. The NPCI 30% per-TPAP volume-cap deadline is 31 Dec 2026. Notification parsers for 4-5 apps plus bank SMS cover about 90% of UPI volume on Android, but must be data-driven and remotely updatable.

Reconciliation should bridge pre-spend and post-spend observations on hashed payee identifier (VPA, proxy or Pix key) plus exact amount plus time proximity. Rail references are strong where the consumer can see them: UPI 12-digit RRN, M-Pesa receipt code, Pix endToEndId in Open Finance. Merchant references (UPI tr, EMV 62.05, Pix txid) rarely appear in consumer alerts.

Web checkout APIs deliberately hide payment details from third parties. SPC is Chrome 95+ only and Payment Request in Firefox is still pref-gated. A browser extension can see only DOM and URL context (cart total, Place-order click, confirmation pages, redirects). That makes browser-checkout-dom the web counterpart to the QR scan ('next'), while wrapping PaymentRequest is 'research' and SPC is 'avoid'.

Swish, Bizum, BLIK, iDEAL/Wero, Vipps MobilePay, SEPA Instant, FedNow/RTP, Pix NFC and PayPay expose no consumer-side payload or API to a third-party app. In BRAKE they should be rail labels in the capability registry, observed only through notifications, SMS, email and open-banking feeds, not dedicated adapters.

NPCI rules changed materially throughout FY2025-26: P2P collect ban, beneficiary-name display from the Validate Address API, API usage limits, AutoPay portability, on-device biometrics replacing the PIN, Reserve Pay, IoT delegation and the UPI HELP AI pilot. The capability registry needs an owner and a refresh pipeline, for example the twice-daily NPCI circular RSS feeds on GitHub.

key_findings: Every Gmail read scope is restricted, including gmail.metadata. gmail.metadata also cannot use the q search parameter or format=full/raw (verified in the Gmail discovery doc, revision 20260727). On Gmail, a metadata-only connection therefore buys no compliance relief and forces BRAKE to enumerate more of the mailbox. The narrowest practical server path is gmail.readonly with a strict q filter (sender list plus category:purchases/category:reservations).

Server-side Gmail access requires restricted-scope verification (brand, scope justification, demo video, app-type review) plus a CASA assessment renewed at least every 12 months. Reported 2026 lab prices are about $540-$1,800/yr at Tier 2 and $4.5k-$8k at Tier 3. Unverified apps have a 100-user lifetime cap, and Testing-mode refresh tokens expire after 7 days. BRAKE should start verification during the MVP phase but not depend on it for the MVP.

Google Limited Use applies to raw, aggregated and derived data. It forbids ads, data brokers and use 'to determine credit-worthiness or for lending purposes', bars humans from reading data without per-item affirmative agreement, and prohibits training models beyond the user's personalized model. These rules should become company-wide commitments for all email data: they rule out Gmail-fed lending products and constrain how templates and labels are built.

Gmail app-type eligibility is a real approval risk. The permitted monitoring category reads 'reporting or monitoring services for the benefit of users that improve the email experience (such as ... travel itineraries or ... package delivery statuses)', so BRAKE must frame its Gmail feature as receipt, subscription and bill tracking and seek a pre-read from Google.

Microsoft Graph Mail.ReadBasic (excludes body, previewBody, attachments and extended properties) and Mail.Read can be granted by personal Microsoft accounts without admin consent. Message change notifications average under 1 minute (3 minutes max), subscriptions last up to 10,080 minutes, and delta query is per-folder with only a receivedDateTime filter. This makes Outlook a lower-burden second provider with a genuinely narrower metadata tier.

A user-configured forwarding inbox (a per-user BRAKE address fed by the user's own sender filter) needs no OAuth scope, verification or CASA. It enforces narrowness the user can see and keeps the original DKIM signature on auto-forward, so it is the MVP path. Microsoft 365 work tenants block automatic external forwarding by default for most orgs since 2021, and Outlook.com IMAP basic auth and app passwords have been off since 16 Sep 2024.

Email is mostly POST-SPEND (minutes), but it carries regulated PRE-SPEND signals. RBI's 2026 e-mandate framework (RBI/DPSS/2026-27/396) requires a pre-transaction notification at least 24 hours before each recurring debit, stating merchant, amount, date/time and mandate reference. Trial-ending, renewal, price-change, bill-due and reservation emails are also pre-spend. The only IN-SPEND email signal (payment OTP emails) should be avoided by default.

For Indian iOS users, bank alert emails may be the best near-real-time sensor. HDFC reportedly emails every UPI transaction, including the 12-digit UPI reference (RRN), even below its SMS thresholds (since 25 Jun 2024). But RBI mandates only SMS alerts (email is optional), ICICI and SBI are reportedly unsuitable, bank sender domains moved to *.bank.in in 2025 (match DKIM d=, not From), and RBL sent false 'credited' e-alerts in 2026.

Email should enrich bank-sourced TransactionCandidates rather than create spend on its own. Amazon charges per shipment and Subscribe & Save charges land 14-19 days after the order email. Tips, wallets, gift cards, FX and partial refunds break amount equality. Fusion should use strong keys first (UPI RRN, then order ID, then Message-ID), use merchant-specific time windows, and allow N:M order-to-charge mapping.

Extraction should be layered and fact-only: schema.org JSON-LD/microdata (Order, Invoice, ParcelDelivery, Reservation; 2026 prevalence unmeasured), then DKIM-gated per-sender templates, then schema-constrained on-device LLMs (Android ML Kit GenAI Prompt API with structured output, still beta4 as of Sep 2026). Persist extracted facts and a message reference, never bodies, and defend against prompt injection and phishing by gating trust on DKIM.

Trust history is the existential risk. Unroll.me's parent Slice sold e-receipt-derived data (NYT 2017); the FTC's 2019 order required deletion and user notice with no fine, and Unroll.me is reported as NielsenIQ-owned and still supplying aggregated reports in 2025. BRAKE needs structural commitments: no sale of any email-derived data or aggregates, on-device extraction by default, no retained bodies, and per-source disconnect-and-delete.

Gmail's July 2025 'Manage subscriptions' view and the List-Unsubscribe header concern newsletter subscriptions, not paid ones. BRAKE must detect paid subscriptions from receipts, renewal notices and e-mandate notices combined with transaction recurrence, and must never treat marketing senders as subscriptions.

Apple's Foundation Models can silently route to Private Cloud Compute or server models. BRAKE's provenance claim ('never left your device') needs an explicit technical guard and a test.

key_findings: Treat the alert text as the asset and capture paths as separate capabilities: one on-device 'sms' parsing adapter (signed, OTA-updatable template packs keyed by sender entity, heuristic fallback, optional on-device LLM with a deterministic validator) should accept text from the Android SMS permission, the Android notification listener (SMS, RCS and WhatsApp as rendered), and iOS paste/Shortcuts.

On Android, READ_SMS/RECEIVE_SMS are 'dangerous' plus 'hardRestricted' (the installer must allow-list them; AOSP manifest), and Google Play limits them to default handlers or approved exception cases (developer.android.com, updated 2026-02-26). So the Android MVP should run on NotificationListenerService, with the SMS permission as an opt-in upgrade (exact sender header plus history backfill) once Play approves BRAKE's declaration. Approval for budgeting apps is plausible but unverified.

Android is walling off OTPs. Android 15 redacts OTP-bearing notifications for untrusted listeners (the exemption permission RECEIVE_SENSITIVE_NOTIFICATIONS is signature|role). Android 17 (API 37, docs updated 2026-10-01) withholds OTP SMS for 3 hours: SMS_RECEIVED_ACTION is withheld and provider queries are filtered. BRAKE must drop OTPs in native capture code before any persistence or logging and must not build in-spend features on 'OTP for Rs X at MERCHANT' messages.

Indian bank alerts arrive from DLT headers like JD-KOTAKD-S (live example, May 2026). Parsers treat the -S suffix as service/transaction alerts and -T/-P/-G as OTP/promotional/government, which gives BRAKE a strong sender allow-list key and an OTP pre-filter. The underlying TRAI regulation text is unverified because the regulator's site was unreachable.

Indian banks have started moving alerts to RCS: Kotak's UPI 'Sent' alerts moved from SMS to RCS by 2026-05-29, and SBI Card and PNB also send RCS alerts. Android has no public RCS API. The notification listener sees these alerts with only a display-name sender. An undocumented route (Google Messages rows in content://mms with tr_id 'proto:<base64>' containing '<brand>_<id>_agent@rbm.goog') works but is fragile.

SMS alerts carry strong fusion and reconciliation keys: the 12-digit UPI RRN, the NEFT/RTGS UTR, the 10-character M-Pesa code, the bKash TrxID and the mandate UMRN/UMN. The same RRN on a debit alert and a credit alert across two of the user's own accounts deterministically identifies an own-account transfer. A running-balance chain detects both missed and forged alerts.

SMS has genuine PRE-SPEND value in India: mandate/UPI AutoPay pre-debit notices ('will be debited ... towards NETFLIX', UMRN), card-due alerts and merchant payment requests. Open-source parsers discard them as non-transactions. BRAKE should emit them as subscription_event/mandate context observations to power renewal interventions.

The fusion layer's same-connection veto would wrongly block merging one event seen by several publishers (Messages app, bank app, UPI app) through a single notification-listener grant. SourceRef needs a channelKey, with the veto keyed on (connectionId, channelKey); intra-channel duplicates (broadcast plus provider rescan) are handled by body hash.

Real fixtures expose normalization pitfalls that template packs must handle: lakh grouping (INR 13,30,614.75), malformed separators (PKR 55.000.00), date order that varies by template (06/07/26 dd/mm/yy vs 3/18/26 m/d/yy), amount/balance confusion, 3- vs 4-digit masked tails, credit-card 'debited' meaning a card spend, inline fees (M-Pesa, bKash), and Mathematical Sans-Serif Unicode in RCS. Use NFKC; never strip non-ASCII, which deletes the rupee sign and Indic text.

Prevalence is uneven. India is near-universal (RBI-mandated, unverified). SMS is the mobile-money system of record in Kenya, Tanzania, Mozambique and Bangladesh (formats verified). Nigeria has common bank SMS (formats verified; fees unverified). The US, UK and EU are push-dominant with opt-in SMS (e.g. Chase short code 24273). No evidence of SMS-led alerting turned up for Indonesia or Brazil, so the registry should mark them unknown/limited.

WhatsApp offers no third-party consumer read API: Meta's published v23.0 spec is business-side only (MARKETING/UTILITY/AUTHENTICATION templates; order_details with payment_type upi; order_status). Passive capture is possible only through the Android notification listener with per-sender opt-in. A BRAKE WhatsApp number that users forward receipts to is a cross-platform research option.

iOS cannot read SMS, RCS or WhatsApp. Message Filter extensions see only unknown senders' SMS/MMS, have no direct network access and cannot write to shared containers, so using them for ingestion would misuse the API. Serve iOS users in SMS markets with UIPasteControl paste (no prompt, iOS 16+), Shortcuts message automations into an App Intent (trigger behaviour unverified), on-device Foundation Models parsing (iOS 26+), and AA/email for the ledger.

key_findings: The only surface that works for every user, including those with no connected accounts, is an amount-first 'Should I buy this?' check reachable in about two taps from system surfaces: iOS widgets, Controls and the Action button; Android widgets, Quick Settings tile and app shortcuts; the share sheet. Each check creates a purchase_intent observation that fusion later resolves to purchased or abandoned, which is BRAKE's core way of measuring whether it helps.

On iPhone, Screen Time shields are now the best automatic pre-spend trigger. iOS 26.4 added up to 3 secondary-button submenu items (secondaryButtonSubmenuItems) and iOS 26.5 added ShieldActionResponse.openParentalControlsApp, which ends the notification-tap workaround. App selection is private (FamilyActivityPicker tokens) and shield extensions are sandboxed with no network access.

Shipping shields requires Apple's 'Family Controls (Distribution)' entitlement for each bundle id and each Screen Time extension, and 2026 forum reports show unpredictable approval times, so the request should be filed on day 1. App Review Guideline 4.10 (as of 2026-06-08) forbids monetizing Screen Time APIs, which limits paywalling the shield feature.

Android has no third-party equivalent of shields. Background activity launches have been restricted since Android 10, so a policy-safe design is opt-in UsageStatsManager ACTIVITY_RESUMED detection plus a notification nudge. Accessibility-service or overlay interception would work technically but should be avoided on privacy and Play-policy grounds.

In India, an in-app UPI QR scanner is the strongest in-store in-spend surface: it parses pa, pn, mc, am and tr, shows budget context, then hands the original upi:// URI to the user's own UPI app. It yields a checkout observation keyed by payee VPA and merchant reference that later fuses with the SMS or notification RRN. QR scanning has little value in the USA.

Share and paste payloads usually carry only a URL and title, so price must come from product-page metadata resolved on-device: schema.org JSON-LD Offer.price + priceCurrency (ISO 4217, '.' decimal) first, then Meta product:price tags (not part of core Open Graph), then DOM heuristics. On iOS, a share extension with NSExtensionJavaScriptPreprocessingFile reads the live Safari DOM, including cart totals, without a browser extension.

Browser extensions give the best in-flow timing for web shopping but reach few BRAKE users: desktop, Safari on iOS/macOS and Firefox only, with no Chrome-on-Android extensions (unverified), and Indian commerce is app-first. The recommended design is activeTab-first with per-site optional host permissions.

BRAKE must reject affiliate and coupon monetization entirely. After the Honey scandal, Chrome enforced stricter affiliate rules from 2025-06-10 (disclosure, user action, tangible benefit). Firefox policy section 7.3 bans affiliate-tag injection and has required data_collection_permissions declarations for new extensions since 2025-11-03. Chrome's Limited Use policy forbids using browsing data for credit-worthiness or lending.

On-device extraction for price tags, receipts and screenshots is now practical. Android: ML Kit Text Recognition v2 (Latin, Devanagari, Chinese, Japanese, Korean), plus the code scanner and document scanner, which need no camera permission. iOS: DataScannerViewController .currency (iOS 17), Vision RecognizeDocumentsRequest (iOS 26), and Foundation Models image attachments with OCRTool/BarcodeReaderTool (iOS 27). On-device LLMs only reach some devices, so deterministic parsers should come first.

Automatic screenshot detection should not be built. The iOS userDidTakeScreenshotNotification and Android 14 ScreenCaptureCallback fire only while BRAKE's own UI is visible and provide no image. User-initiated screenshot sharing is the right design and yields strong keys such as the UPI UTR and order ids.

Voice: Siri via App Intents / App Shortcuts with value prompts is production-ready. On Android, App Actions' status under Gemini is unclear and AppFunctions (Android 16+) Gemini integration was a private preview as of May 2026, so Android voice should be deferred.

Pre-spend amounts are list prices (US sales tax, shipping, coupons, Indian MRP vs selling price, ranges, multi-item carts). Fusion's ±15% / 24 h intent rule should instead key on merchant domain and time, treat amount as soft evidence, and use horizons per entry path (QR about 15 min, checkout 1–2 h, quick check 72 h, share 7 d, wishlist 30 d).

key_findings: Strong friction (pauses of seconds, 24 h holds) should come only from rules the user wrote. Model-initiated interventions should be capped at a non-blocking one-sentence nudge (L2). The best direct evidence (Gruning et al. 2023 PNAS, one sec) is for brief, self-chosen, skippable friction: about 36% of opening attempts abandoned and about 57% fewer attempts over 6 weeks. These figures are as recalled and were not re-verified this session.

Scolding is self-defeating. Controlling language triggers reactance, shame drives withdrawal, and the ostrich effect means users stop looking at bad financial news. Post-spend copy should compare with the user's own baseline, state one fact plus an optional action, close with explicit freedom ('Your call'), and say nothing when there is no new insight.

Proposed attention budget: at most 1 model-initiated push per day and 3 per week; at most 2-3 label questions per week after onboarding (never more than 1 per day); at most 1 regret prompt per week; at most 4 non-user-requested prompts per week in total; 1 weekly digest; quiet hours 22:00-08:00. Unanswered items are never re-sent. The platforms already penalize noise: Android 13+ notifications are off by default, Android 15 cools down repeated notifications for up to 2 minutes, and the Apple HIG warns that repeats lead users to turn off all of an app's notifications (all verified 2026-10-04).

Label questions should be chosen by expected value of information (EVOI) under a weekly budget with an adaptive shadow price. Each question asks one attribute and offers the top-2 predicted answers plus 'Other'. When transfer probability is at least 0.2, 'Not spending (transfer)' must be one of the options. Each answer should generalize via a one-time 'Always treat <merchant> as X?' offer. Android allows at most 3 notification action buttons; iOS shows at most 2 actions when space is limited (up to 10 when expanded); both support text input (verified).

Regret prompts must be partly random (about 50% uniform, stratified by amount) with the propensity logged, and estimated with inverse-propensity weighting. A sampler that only asks about suspected-regret purchases produces biased 'you usually regret X' claims. SatisfactionAssertion should gain propensity, delayHours, selectionReason, askContext and promptVariant fields.

Regret-prompt delay should depend on purchase type, not be a fixed 24-72 h. Consumables and experiences: 18-36 h (before rosy-view drift). Physical goods: about 3 days after delivery and before the return window closes, so a remedy exists. Large planned purchases: 14-30 days, rarely. Subscriptions: a 'keep?' check 3 days before renewal instead. No study establishes an optimal delay, so BRAKE should randomize delay buckets in an opt-in research mode.

Personalization must be able to reduce friction as well as add it. Hyperopia research shows long-run regrets of under-spending, especially on experiences, and tightwads already feel too much pain of paying. A spending-style prior and 'worth it' affirmations guard against harming frugal users.

Never show regret totals, streaks, scores or 'money wasted'. Personal quantification can reduce enjoyment (Etkin 2016). Guardrails: pause prompts after 3 ignored, stop for the week after 3 'wish I hadn't', and always offer one-tap 'Don't ask about these'.

Communicate uncertainty with fixed confidence bands: at least 0.95 a plain statement, 0.80-0.95 'Looks like...', 0.50-0.80 a question in the title, below 0.50 silent. Predictions about the user should use natural frequencies from their own answers ('4 of your last 6'), surfaced only when n is at least 5. Vague verbal hedges are interpreted inconsistently and lower trust more than numeric ranges.

Late-night, mood and social-media triggers have mostly lab or correlational evidence. Ego depletion failed a multisite preregistered replication (d about 0.04). Local hour should be a per-user model feature, not a universal rule, and is valid only with real-time timestamps. Passive emotion inference and cross-app usage timelines should be avoided.

BRAKE's own UX falls under dark-pattern rules: India's CCPA 2023 guidelines (13 patterns, including confirm shaming and nagging), EU DSA Art. 25, EU AI Act Art. 5 (since 2 Feb 2025) and Apple 3.1.2(a). Paywall, cancellation, source-disconnect and deletion flows must be frictionless. Apple guideline 4.5.4 discourages sensitive personal information in push notifications, so BRAKE should generate them locally with lock-screen-safe public versions.

Evaluate with micro-randomized trials from launch: randomize no intervention vs the chosen level at each decision point and log propensities. Primary outcomes: the inverse-propensity-weighted share of discretionary spending later rated 'worth it', goal progress, the CFPB Financial Well-Being Scale and an autonomy item. Guardrails: channel mutes, 'stop asking' taps and habituation. Plan for effect decay, and never optimize for engagement.

key_findings: No ecosystem guarantees an ID join from a pending record to its posted record. Plaid sets pending_transaction_id only 'if Plaid matches', and authorization holds can vanish. UK Open Banking v4.0.1 has no link field. Australia's CDR v1.36.0 says there is 'no provision … to correlate a pending transaction with an associated posted transaction'. Brazil's transactionId may change until TRANSACAO_EFETIVADA. India's AA deposit schema carries posted transactions only. BRAKE must therefore implement pending-to-posted as a fuzzy supersede match with retraction semantics, not as a key lookup.

Strong reconciliation keys are rail-specific and often left blank: UPI RRN (12 characters), Pix EndToEndId (32 characters with an embedded UTC minute), UK TransactionReference (may hold the FPID), SEPA endToEndId/mandateId/creditorId, Plaid transaction_id and AA txnId. FinecoBank documents endToEndId and entryReference as 'currently not used', so key availability must be registered per institution, not per country.

Balance-after-transaction is a near-decisive and under-used matching key. It is required in AA deposit records (currentBalance), present in UK OB (Balance) and Plaid (running_balance, posted only), and common in Indian alerts (unverified). The core Observation model should gain a balanceAfter field and a balance-continuity check to find missing or duplicate events.

Fusion should use Fellegi–Sunter weights with three properties: term-frequency-adjusted amount weights, because round amounts are weak evidence; complete-linkage assignment with no connected-components clustering; and a one-event-per-source constraint. Missing fields are neutral, and auto-merges between ledger records from different connections need posterior ≥0.95 or a strong reference or balance key.

Own-account transfers should be matched as exact equal-and-opposite pairs between owned instruments, assigned one-to-one with exact matches ranked first. Sure auto-matches within ±4 days, uses a 30-day manual window, and allows a ±10% FX band only when both accounts are linked. Single-leg cases fall back to Plaid PFC TRANSFER_* / counterparty type payment_app, ISO 20022 purpose codes (CCRD, GP2P, MP2P, MP2B, SALA, CASH), Brazil partiePersonType plus counterparty CPF equality, and self-name matches. Anything still uncertain stays an 'unclassified outflow' outside discretionary pace.

Credit-card bill payments are never spending. If the card is not connected, show the payment as 'unitemized card spending' outside discretionary pace. India-specific traps: UPI payments drawn on credit cards (the UPI data model has payer account type CREDIT) and EMI conversions (unverified pattern).

UPI's P2P vs P2M decision (payee persona PERSON/ENTITY, payee MCC) exists only inside issuer/PSP systems. BRAKE can rely on QR/intent `mc` when it scanned or launched the payment, on VPA and narration heuristics, and on one question per new material counterparty. Small merchants paid on personal VPAs are the main failure case.

Recurring detection should be BRAKE's own on-device engine. Shape: group by merchant/counterparty key plus currency (not by card); cluster amounts within 7.5% of the running mean (the value used by both Actual Budget and Sure); allow ±2 days on a circular day-of-month calendar, or k·P gap tolerance; and use statuses EARLY → MATURE (≥3 occurrences, ≥2 for annual) → TOMBSTONED, mirroring Plaid. Plaid streams are per account, have no quarterly enum, and can no longer be modified by users (is_user_modified 'always false'), so they serve only as hints.

Subscription intelligence in the MVP should be limited to recurring detection plus passive subscription labels and 'upcoming known bills', which are needed for correct spending interpretation. Renewal nudges, trial-conversion, price-increase, duplicate and dormant detection are 'next'. They need email or mandate signals; app-store aggregator descriptors hide the underlying service (unverified); and BRAKE has no usage data for 'dormant'. India e-mandate pre-debit notices are the exception worth shipping early.

Plaid specifics as of spec 2020-09-14_1.762.0: PFC v2 is mandatory for Transactions/Enrich enabled on or after 2025-12-03; merchant_category_code is in beta and running_balance is new; PFC has no refund or wallet-load category; Recurring is an add-on that recommends ≥180 days of history; Enrich takes 100 transactions per request with US/CA location; Plaid checks institutions 1–4 times per day.

Enrichment vendors are B2B and North-America-centric: Plaid Enrich (US/CA), Spade (an issuer authorization-path product with a transferType internal/external flag), and Ntropy (person/organization counterparty, intermediaries, recurring vs subscription). Use an on-device descriptor normalizer that keeps intermediaries first. Splitwise's self-serve API 'may not be used in connection with any fee-based service', so shared-expense import needs a commercial licence.

key_findings: Extracting on the device and discarding the raw message is BRAKE's strongest legal de-risker. Apple defines 'collect' as transmitting data off the device beyond real-time servicing [V]. It also defuses interception theories (UK IPA, California CIPA), which turn on content reaching a person other than the recipient [U], and it reduces CCPA 'sensitive personal information' exposure, since that category includes the contents of email and text messages [U]. Make on-device extraction the default for SMS, notifications and email.

India: an unregulated BRAKE cannot be an Account Aggregator FIU. Clause 3(xii) of the AA Master Direction requires an entity 'registered with and regulated by a financial sector regulator' [S]. The Indian MVP should therefore use the Android notification listener plus SMS bank alerts; Google Play lists an 'SMS-based money management' exception for READ_SMS and RECEIVE_SMS [S]. AA access should come later through a regulated partner FIU.

India DPDP timeline: the Rules were notified on 14 Nov 2025. Consent Manager registration starts about Nov 2026 and the substantive obligations start about 13 May 2027 [S]. BRAKE must be 18+ only, because s.9 bans behavioural monitoring of under-18s [U]. Until DPDP commencement, the SPDI Rules 2011 treat financial information as sensitive personal data [U].

US: the CFPB Section 1033 rule is enjoined and its first 1 Apr 2026 compliance date never took effect. The reconsideration NPRM went to OIRA on 6 Aug 2026 [S]. US bank data therefore depends on aggregator contracts and possible bank fees, not on a legal right. BRAKE should still adopt the 2024 rule's third-party duties as its baseline: authorisation of at most 12 months, no ads, no cross-selling, no sale, easy revocation [U]. It should also assume the GLBA Safeguards Rule applies, including 30-day FTC notice for incidents affecting 500+ consumers [U].

Spending data reveals special-category and health data. CJEU case law treats indirectly revealing data as GDPR Art. 9 data (C-184/20, C-252/21, C-21/23 on pharmacy orders) [U]. Washington's MHMDA covers health inferences derived from non-health data, requires separate consent and allows private suits [U]. A 'Medical' label therefore needs explicit or separate consent, must stay on the device, must be excluded from cross-user learning, and must be redacted on the lock screen.

Gmail is the most regulated source. gmail.readonly and even gmail.metadata are Restricted scopes, and metadata cannot run q queries [S]. Server-side use needs an annual third-party security assessment [V]. Limited Use applies to raw, aggregated, anonymised and derived data, and forbids ads, sale, credit-worthiness use and human reading without consent [V]. The Workspace policy forbids training non-personalised AI/ML models [S]. A user-configured forwarding address, which makes BRAKE the intended recipient, is a lighter-weight email route.

EU/UK: reading other apps' notifications on the device likely needs ePrivacy Art. 5(3) or PECR consent, per source [U]. A DPIA is effectively mandatory, because BRAKE meets at least five WP248 criteria [U]. AIS data must flow through a licensed AISP or agent model, and PSD2 Art. 67 limits use to the AIS the user requested [U]. AI Act Art. 5 has banned manipulative techniques and the exploitation of economic vulnerability since 2 Feb 2025 [U], so interventions must be user-configured, overridable and non-deceptive.

Platforms are tightening. Android 15 redacts OTP-bearing notifications to untrusted listeners [V]. Android 17 withholds WebOTP SMS from non-recipient apps for 3 hours [V]. Apple 5.1.2(i) requires explicit permission before personal data is shared with third-party AI [V], and 5.1.1(ix) requires finance apps to be submitted by a legal entity [V]. FinanceKit is a managed entitlement that Apple reviews [V]. The Chrome Web Store tightened Limited Use from 1 Aug 2026 [S].

PCI DSS stays out of scope only if BRAKE never ingests, stores or transmits a full PAN or CVV and keeps last-4 at most [U]. Receipt OCR, screenshots and manual entry therefore need Luhn-based PAN detection and redaction before persistence, logging or any network call.

Model processing must be tiered: deterministic parsers first, then on-device models (Apple Foundation Models; Gemini Nano via AICore, which 'doesn't store any record of the input data or the resulting outputs' [V]), then an opt-in cloud LLM. The cloud tier needs zero-retention and no-training contracts, pre-redaction, schema-constrained output and prompt-injection defences. Gmail-derived data must never feed non-personalised or cross-user models.

Architecture: each adapter must ship a reviewed PolicyProfile covering ingest filter, processing locus, raw and fact retention class, legal basis per jurisdiction, platform gates, cross-user-learning and cloud-LLM eligibility, and counterparty hashing. Policy tags propagate to TransactionCandidates using the most restrictive member. The capability registry must hold legal facts with as_of dates and evidence levels. The doc lists 40 concrete privacy requirements (PR-01 to PR-40), a retention schedule (R0-R9) and a consent-receipt schema modelled on the AA ConsentDetail.

key_findings: Indian trackers built on sensed spending data have repeatedly become credit businesses. Walnut, the archetypal SMS-reading tracker, was acquired by digital lender Capital Float on 2018-08-14 and became axio (BNPL, personal loans, FDs). Fi raised $168M, failed to grow lending, and in March 2026 began winding down banking on its platform for more than 3.5M users. BRAKE must choose a non-credit model up front and enforce 'sensed data never feeds credit, affiliate or ad decisions' in the architecture.

Dependence on one permission, vendor or partner is the most common way these products die: Google Play's January 2019 SMS/Call Log policy (default handler or approved declaration, otherwise removal), Mint folding into Credit Karma (shut down by 2024-03-23), GoCardless Bank Account Data closing to new accounts from July 2025, and Fi losing its bank partner in 2026. Adapters, the capability registry and per-institution multi-provider routing are survival requirements.

Aggregator-fed PFMs (Mint, Copilot, Monarch, YNAB, Emma) are retrospective ledgers. SimpleFIN refreshes about once per 24h with at most 90 days of history, and FinanceKit background delivery is at best hourly (iOS 26+). In the US, UK and EU, BRAKE's pre-spend and in-spend value must come from non-bank mechanisms: app shielding, browser checkout detection, share-sheet and manual checks.

The strongest behavior-change evidence comes from attention-friction apps (one sec, Opal, ScreenZen), which put a short, skippable pause at app launch. iOS supports this through FamilyControls individual authorization (iOS 16+, distribution entitlement required), ManagedSettings shields and DeviceActivity. The shield handler gets only opaque tokens, never app names. No friction app uses financial context; that gap is BRAKE's core differentiator.

Apple FinanceKit is the only on-device, aggregator-free financial source on iOS. It requires the Finance category and US/UK distribution. It covers Apple Card, Apple Cash and Savings in the US (iOS 17.4+) and 13 UK banks via Wallet (iOS 18.4+), and exposes merchantName, merchantCategoryCode (ISO 18245) and status (authorized, booked, pending, rejected, memo). BRAKE should apply for the managed entitlement during MVP.

Android allows at most three notification action buttons (plus RemoteInput), which fits BRAKE's one-tap labeling as 'top-2 predictions + Other'. Prior art shows two extremes, Copilot's short review queue and YNAB's approve-every-transaction (both unverified); BRAKE should ask only when uncertain, with a daily prompt cap and a batch-review fallback.

Android 15 redacts OTP-bearing notifications for untrusted NotificationListenerService apps; Android 16 adds no further listener changes. The notification listener remains the best Play-safe successor to Walnut-style SMS capture, but the adapter must degrade gracefully as redaction expands.

Bank gambling blocks with a cooling-off period before removal show that users accept self-imposed commitment devices with delayed reversal (details unverified), but only issuers can apply them and they are MCC-coarse. BRAKE should offer 'assisted controls' (explain, deep-link, remember) in MVP and only later pursue issuer partnerships.

The trust incidents (Unroll.me/Slice, Yodlee, Honey, Avast/Jumpshot, Cleo FTC; all unverified in this session) share one pattern: data collected for the user was reused for parties who profit from more spending. Apple guideline 5.1.2(i)-(iii) already forbids repurposing and covert profiling. BRAKE should publish a machine-readable data-flow manifest per adapter that drives its 'How did BRAKE know this?' UI.

Receipt and rewards apps (Fetch, Ibotta) and email parsers (Slice) show that line items are the richest semantic layer and that users share receipts for an immediate payoff, but they are funded by brands that want more purchases. BRAKE should adopt their sensing (on-device receipt OCR, allow-listed email parsing) and reject their monetization.

Open-source local-first PFMs confirm demand for privacy-first finance and match BRAKE's adapter model. Actual Budget (MIT, about 29.3k stars) has pluggable bank sync via Akahu, Enable Banking, GoCardless, Pluggy AI and SimpleFIN. Maybe Finance was archived 2025-07-27, which shows how fragile pure-PFM economics are.

No mainstream PFM verified in this session runs systematic post-purchase satisfaction or regret prompts. A sparse regret-feedback loop feeding a personal friction ladder (nothing, context line, skippable pause, reflective question, user-committed delay) is BRAKE's clearest unoccupied position.

key_findings: MCC (ISO 18245) is the most widely available structured merchant-category signal, but it is a merchant-level prior assigned by the acquirer, not a purchase-level truth. It appears in Plaid (a beta field, mostly on card transactions), Apple FinanceKit, UK Open Banking v4.0.1 MerchantDetails, Berlin Group card accounts, Australia CDR v1.36.0, Open Finance Brasil credit cards, India AA credit-card data, EMV merchant QR (tag 52) and UPI QR (mc). It is absent from India AA deposit transactions, which carry only mode CASH/ATM/CARD/UPI/FT/OTHERS plus a free-text narration.

In India the MCC can be known before the user pays: a BRAKE UPI or EMV QR scan reads the merchant's name, MCC and (for EMV) city before payment. In card markets the MCC only arrives after the spend. This makes QR scanning BRAKE's best pre-spend merchant-context source in QR-first markets.

MCC formats differ across sources and must be normalized on ingest to a zero-padded 4-character string, with null for placeholders. FinanceKit uses an Int16 and Brazil payeeMCC an integer, so leading zeros are lost (0742 becomes 742). UK Open Banking allows 3-4 characters, Ntropy returns a list of integer MCCs per entity, Pix QR commonly carries 0000, and the AA credit-card sample instance has mcc="".

Merchant identity should be resolved on-device against open brand data keyed by Wikidata IDs. Sources: the OSM name-suggestion-index (BSD-3, with country scoping and match names; for example Starbucks is Q37158 and DMart is Q5203271) and Overture Places (about 81.6M places in the September 2026 release under CDLA-Permissive-2.0, Apache-2.0 or CC0, with no ODbL share-alike). Vendor IDs such as Plaid merchant_entity_id become aliases, and descriptors are not sent off-device by default.

Intermediaries are the main normalization trap. Plaid's own example 'DD DOORDASH BURGERKIN' resolves to DoorDash (type marketplace) plus Burger King (type merchant). Plaid counterparty types include payment_terminal and payment_app, and Ntropy models intermediaries separately. BRAKE's MerchantObservation should gain an intermediary field from day one.

Most context BRAKE needs can be derived from data the user already consented to share. Store location comes from Plaid location, EMV QR city and postal code, or the Berlin Group card-acceptor address. Online vs in-store comes from Plaid payment_channel, UK Open Banking AuthorisationType, or whether a QR is static or dynamic. Travel comes from foreign currency, airline or hotel MCCs, and Android's time-zone-change broadcast. Payday comes from recurring income deposits. Upcoming bills come from recurring outflows, the AA credit-card dueDate and minDueAmount, and Australia CDR BPAY billerCode and DIRECT_DEBIT entries.

Background location and geofencing fail the proposed Context Justification Test, so they should be avoided for MVP. They require ACCESS_BACKGROUND_LOCATION (granted only through a settings page on Android 11+). Android allows 100 geofences per app with latency usually under 2 minutes and up to 6; iOS allows 20 monitored conditions. Being near a shop says little about intent to buy, and the data reveals sensitive places. For user-initiated moments, prefer Android 17's session-scoped location button or iOS reduced-accuracy location.

Avoid reading the user's calendar, but adopt write-only calendar access for renewal and bill reminders. Options: iOS 17 write-only access, or EventKitUI with no permission; Android ACTION_INSERT with no permission; the Google calendar.app.created scope, which only covers a calendar the app creates.

Time-of-day features need minute-precision timestamps, which many feeds lack. Plaid warns authorized_datetime may contain default 00:00:00 values, and the AA credit-card txnDate is date-only. Every observation therefore needs time_precision and time_basis fields, and late-night features must abstain when precision is too coarse.

Sensitive merchant categories need a hard deny-list: political (8651), religious (8661), medical (8011, 8062, 8099), pharmacy (5912), dating/escort (7273) and betting (7995). These classes must never appear in server telemetry, nudge copy, default regret prompts or off-device training.

Taxonomies changed recently, so lookup packs must be versioned. Plaid customers who enabled Transactions or Enrich on or after 2025-12-03 receive only PFC v2. Overture removed its categories field in September 2026 in favour of taxonomy (about 2,300 categories) and basic_category (about 280 labels). Google Places terms (last modified 2026-06-10) forbid using Places content with a non-Google map and cap latitude/longitude caching at 30 days, so Google Places is a poor default enrichment path.

Proposed governance: a registry-enforced Context Justification Test with eight checks (decision link, derive before collecting, measured lift with a confidence interval, user expectation, least precision, sensitive-inference screen, independent consent and reversibility, no third-party leakage). Each signal gets a machine-readable justification card and is switched off automatically when its lift evidence goes stale.
open_questions: How often do Indian FIPs populate the AA credit-card mcc attribute (schema-required, but the sample is empty), and how often do major UK banks populate Open Banking MerchantDetails? This needs sandbox or production sampling.
What is the current NPCI UPI QR/intent parameter set and the P2P vs merchant convention (mc value for P2P, verified-merchant indicators)? The primary spec was unreachable this session.
Is Pix tag-52 MCC 0000 mandated by the BCB manual or merely common practice?
How good is Plaid Enrich on non-US descriptors (Indian SMS text, AA narration), and under what terms, compared with BRAKE's on-device resolver on a labelled sample?
Which Plaid PFC v2 detailed categories replace v1 income labels such as INCOME_WAGES, for payday detection?

Does the user's own late-night regret rate measurably improve intervention helpfulness over amount, velocity and category alone? Run the Context Justification Test lift test before shipping hour-based friction.
Would an opt-in, user-named, on-device, expiring 'trouble spots' geofence mode pass the user-expectation check, and with what false-positive rate?
What Overture tile size and update cadence keep on-device POI packs small (target 20 MB or less per metro) while covering local merchants?
What open, maintainable source per country exists for intermediary descriptor patterns (payment gateways, delivery platforms, app-store billing, wallets)?
What are the real-world latency and reliability of FinanceKit BackgroundDeliveryExtension, and how much does merchantName differ from originalTransactionDescription?
What is the current (2026) text and status of the CFPB Section 1033 secondary-use limits, and how do they apply to derived features computed on-device?
What are India's DPDP Rules phase-in dates, and how do their purpose and consent-manager provisions interact with AA purpose code 102 for derived context features?
Can a consumer app without issuer status get access to Visa or Mastercard merchant lookup APIs, and do their terms allow showing results to consumers?
unverifiable: CFPB Section 1033 status in 2026: consumerfinance.gov, federalregister.gov and ecfr.gov were blocked. The only indirect evidence is Plaid OpenAPI 1.762.0, which says 1033-related expiration is 'not currently' enforced.

NPCI UPI Linking Specification parameters (pa, pn, mc, tr, ...): the primary PDF (npci.org.in) and the labnol.org copy were blocked, so only a secondary AI-generated GitHub transcription of v1.6 (2017) was read. Newer NPCI QR tables are not public.
P2P UPI QRs carry mc=0000 or omit it.
Pix BR Code MCC 0000 is a BCB mandate rather than an implementation convention: bcb.gov.br was blocked.
Whether ISO 18245:2003 has been superseded by a newer edition: iso.org was blocked.
MCC 5552 (EV charging) and MCC 5723 (firearms, ISO 2022 approval, paused rollout): neither is in the cited table, and iso.org was blocked.
Whether FinanceKit requires an organization (not individual) developer account.
Google Play background-location declaration and location-button policy details and enforcement dates: support.google.com was blocked.
CJEU C-184/20 (2022) and C-21/23 (2024) holdings on indirectly revealed special-category data: curia was blocked.
RBI e-mandate pre-debit notification of at least 24 hours: rbi.org.in was blocked.
India DPDP Rules phase-in dates and consent-manager interaction with AA purpose codes: meity and dpdpa sites were blocked.
Gelman et al. (Science 2014), Olafsson & Pagel (RFS 2018) and Nissenbaum (2004): background knowledge only.
Plaid PFC v2 income labels (e.g. INCOME_SALARY): plaid.com/documents/pfc-taxonomy-all.csv was blocked; only third-party code transcriptions were seen.
Visa and Mastercard merchant lookup API fields, access and terms: developer portals were blocked.
Ntropy coverage, pricing and data residency: docs.ntropy.com was blocked.
Plaid product pricing, and Recurring Transactions country availability.
How often Indian FIPs actually populate the AA credit-card mcc and deposit transactionTimestamp time-of-day, and how often UK banks populate MerchantDetails.
Semantics of UK OB AuthorisationType ConsumerDevice and None: the OB code-set repo was not accessible.
Overture download file format (GeoParquet) is not stated on the guide page.
remaining_concerns: Web search was exhausted and many primary regulator and standards domains were blocked. Regulatory status (CFPB 1033, DPDP Rules, RBI e-mandate, CJEU case law) is therefore still unverified and needs a session with access to consumerfinance.gov, federalregister.gov, rbi.org.in, meity.gov.in and curia.

UPI facts rest on a secondary, AI-generated transcription of a 2017 spec (v1.6). NPCI's current QR and intent rules, including signed QR, verified-merchant indicators and mc population rates, need primary confirmation. India is BRAKE's lead market, so this is a material gap.

The sensitive-MCC deny-list is a design judgment, not a legal standard. Have privacy counsel review it against GDPR Art. 9, DPDP and US state health-data laws such as Washington's My Health My Data Act. Sensitive store types from NSI/Overture also need a deny-list, not just MCCs.

Apple 5.1.2(i) now names 'third-party AI'. Any LLM-based merchant or descriptor enrichment, including first-party server models from a third-party provider, may need explicit consent. This affects the opt-in server-enrichment step of the resolver.
The CJT thresholds (90% derivability lift, 70% expectation, 95% CI) are the author's proposals, not evidence-based standards; treat them as starting points.
FinanceKit eligibility details (organization vs individual account, background delivery latency) and the Android 17 location-button Play policy enforcement dates are unverified.

Population rates for the 'available' schema fields (AA credit-card mcc, UK OB MerchantDetails, Berlin Group card-account endpoints, CDR merchantCategoryCode) are unknown. The capability registry should mark these as schema-available but empirically unverified until sandbox or production sampling is done.
Overture's own guide gives inconsistent counts (about 2,300 vs '2.1k' taxonomy; about 280 vs 'about 300' basic categories). Pin to the schema, not the prose.

The working tree contains uncommitted changes to other files (other docs and packages) that this fact-check did not make. Only docs/research/13-merchant-and-contextual-signals.md was edited here. A single read-only git status was run to confirm that, despite the instruction not to run git.

plaid-transactions.name: Plaid Transactions (/transactions/sync + webhooks)
plaid-transactions.rationale: The only turnkey ledger source for the US and Canada. It has the cleanest pending-to-posted lifecycle (pending_transaction_id), a merchant entity graph and confidence-scored categories. It is post-spend confirmation and context, not in-spend sensing.
plaid-transactions.typical_latency: Pending: hours after authorization (typical, unverified). Posted: typically 1-3 business days (unverified). Plaid 'typically checks… between one and four times per day, depending on the institution'. /transactions/refresh (a paid add-on) forces an on-demand check (<10 s typical, sometimes 30 s+). SYNC_UPDATES_AVAILABLE signals new data. As of 2026-10-04.
plaid-transactions.access_requirements: Plaid contract and production approval. Transactions is billed per Item; Balance is pay-per-call. /transactions/refresh and Recurring Transactions are add-ons that need a product access request, and refresh has a separate per-request fee (list prices unverified). A backend must hold access tokens and receive webhooks.
plaid-transactions.policy_constraints: Data Transparency Messaging consent scopes. consent_expiration_time and the 7-day PENDING_EXPIRATION webhook apply in EU/UK; the 7-day PENDING_DISCONNECT applies in US/CA. Users manage connections in Plaid Portal. The 1033 reauthorization field is 'not currently used' (Sept 2026 spec), so Plaid is not applying 1033-style 12-month expiry. The 1033 rule itself was enjoined in Oct 2025 and is under reconsideration (secondary).

plaid-transactions.name: Plaid Transactions (/transactions/sync)
plaid-transactions.rationale: Primary US ledger. BRAKE must treat `removed` as retraction and supersede pending records with posted ones. The spec populates `pending_transaction_id` only 'where applicable', and the 'if Plaid matches' docs wording is unverified. Ingest PFC v2 and counterparty types as type hints. `running_balance` is in the spec but flagged x-hidden-from-docs, so it cannot be relied on as a balance-after key.
plaid-transactions.access_requirements: Plaid contract. days_requested defaults to 90 (max 730; min 30 in Production) and cannot be changed after Transactions is added to an Item. /transactions/refresh is a separately priced add-on.
dedup_keys: persistent_account_id (TAN institutions only: Chase, PNC, US Bank)
plaid-transactions.policy_constraints: Server-side aggregator access token. Countries listed are the Plaid stream's scope (coverage not verified in this stream).
plaid-transactions.typical_latency: Hours: Plaid checks institutions 1–4 times per day depending on institution (spec 1.762.0, as of 2026-10-04); pending→posted 1–5 business days per Plaid docs (unverified).

plaid-transactions.name: US aggregator transaction APIs (Plaid and similar)
plaid-transactions.rationale: Ledger-grade US data, but access depends on aggregator contracts while the CFPB 1033 rule is enjoined and being rewritten (secondary). GLBA Safeguards likely applies (unverified). It becomes mvp only if the US is the launch market and a GLBA-grade security program exists.
plaid-transactions.access_requirements: Aggregator contract and production review; GLBA Safeguards / Privacy Rule program (unverified); 1033 rule enjoined with NPRM at OIRA since 2026-08-06 (secondary).
plaid-transactions.policy_constraints: Call /item/remove on disconnect; users can revoke at my.plaid.com; some OAuth institutions may still show a removed Item as active (verified, Plaid OpenAPI). 1033 baseline: at most 12-month authorisation, no targeted ads, cross-selling or sale (unverified).

plaid-transactions.name: US aggregator-fed PFMs (Mint, Copilot, Monarch, YNAB, Rocket Money, Simplifi, Cleo, Origin) via Plaid/MX/Finicity
plaid-transactions.rationale: Rich context, but post-spend only (hours to about a day), costly, and connections break. Mint's ad and referral model ended in shutdown by 2024-03-23 (search summaries only). As of 2026-10-04, Plaid's API spec says 1033-related expiration is not enforced, so US access rests on aggregator contracts, not a statutory right. US MVP can rely on FinanceKit, email, manual entry and friction. When built, route per institution across multiple aggregators (the Monarch lesson, unverified).
plaid-transactions.policy_constraints: CFPB 1033 not enforced as of 2026-10 (Plaid spec); legal status of the rule unverified

plaid-transactions.name: Plaid Transactions merchant enrichment fields
plaid-transactions.rationale: Provides merchant_name, a stable brand-level merchant_entity_id, and counterparties[] with type (merchant, financial_institution, marketplace, payment_terminal, payment_app, income_source) and confidence_level. Also provides personal_finance_category v1/v2 with confidence, a beta merchant_category_code (mostly card transactions), payment_channel (online, in store, other) and location (physical stores only, mostly large chains). authorized_datetime is returned only for select institutions and may hold default 00:00:00 values. These fields come at no extra integration cost wherever the Plaid adapter ships. The CountryCode enum is US, CA, GB, NO and 16 EU states; per-country field coverage is unverified.
plaid-transactions.access_requirements: Plaid production access; Transactions product (pricing unverified)
plaid-transactions.policy_constraints: Data is under Plaid Link consent. Fetching logos from plaid-merchant-logos.plaid.com leaks merchant and IP. Clients that enabled Transactions/Enrich on or after 2025-12-03 get PFC v2 only.

plaid-recurring-transactions.name: Plaid Recurring Transactions (/transactions/recurring/get)
plaid-recurring-transactions.rationale: Provides predicted_next_date, frequency and stream status (MATURE, EARLY_DETECTION, TOMBSTONED) for upcoming renewals and bills. It is an add-on that needs an access request, and users cannot correct streams through the API. BRAKE should run its own recurrence detector and use Plaid's streams as one input.
plaid-recurring-transactions.typical_latency: Daily-ish, following Transactions updates; RECURRING_TRANSACTIONS_UPDATE webhook.
plaid-recurring-transactions.access_requirements: Add-on to Transactions (product access request). At least 180 days of history recommended. Availability outside US/CA unverified.

plaid-recurring-transactions.name: Plaid Recurring Transactions (/transactions/recurring/get)
plaid-recurring-transactions.rationale: A useful prior for US users (MATURE/EARLY_DETECTION/TOMBSTONED, predicted_next_date). It cannot be the engine: streams are per account, the frequency enum has no quarterly value, users can no longer modify streams, and BRAKE must behave the same across AA, SMS and manual data.
plaid-recurring-transactions.access_requirements: Paid add-on to Transactions requested through the product access process; ≥180 days of history recommended.

plaid-recurring-transactions.name: Plaid /transactions/recurring/get streams
plaid-recurring-transactions.rationale: Returns inflow and outflow streams with frequency, predicted_next_date and status. MATURE needs at least 3 transactions on a regular cadence, or 2 for annual; the other statuses are EARLY_DETECTION, TOMBSTONED and UNKNOWN. is_user_modified is deprecated and always false because user edits were discontinued. BRAKE needs its own detector for every country anyway, so Plaid streams serve as a second opinion. Country availability of the add-on is unverified.
plaid-recurring-transactions.access_requirements: 'Offered as an add-on to Transactions' via a product access request (pricing and country availability unverified). Request at least 180 days of history.

plaid-balance.name: Plaid Balance (/accounts/balance/get, cached /accounts/get)
plaid-balance.rationale: Affordability context for pre-spend checks. The cached balance is free and updates about daily. The real-time call is billed per request and takes under 10 s typically (sometimes 30 s or more), so use it only on explicit user action.
plaid-balance.typical_latency: Cached: about daily. Real-time: under 10-30 s per call.

plaid-enrich.name: Plaid Enrich (/transactions/enrich for non-Plaid transactions)
plaid-enrich.rationale: Could normalize merchants and categories for SMS, notification or AA transactions, but it sends transaction text to a third party, which works against local-first, and its non-US coverage is unverified. Benchmark it against on-device normalization first.

plaid-enrich.name: Plaid Enrich (/transactions/enrich)
plaid-enrich.rationale: Enriches non-Plaid descriptors. US users with Plaid already get the same enrichment, and the location schema is US/CA, so it adds little. It also sends data off-device.
plaid-enrich.access_requirements: Plaid contract. Max 100 transactions per request.
data_fields: input: id, description, amount, direction INFLOW/OUTFLOW, iso_currency_code, mcc, date_posted, location(country US|CA)
output: counterparties, entity_id, merchant_name, website, logo_url, phone_number, payment_channel, personal_finance_category
plaid-enrich.policy_constraints: Third-party processing of transaction descriptors; requires explicit consent and a DPA.

plaid-enrich.name: Plaid Enrich for non-Plaid transactions
plaid-enrich.rationale: Enriches descriptors from SMS, email or non-Plaid banks, up to 100 per request, with optional mcc and location inputs. The input schema is oriented to US and Canada. It sends data that was not obtained through Plaid to a third party, which breaks local-first processing, so evaluate it against the on-device resolver first.
data_fields: input: id, description, amount, direction, iso_currency_code, location, mcc, date_posted
output: counterparties, entity_id, merchant_name, payment_channel, personal_finance_category, location, logo_url, website, phone_number
