plaid-enrich.policy_constraints: Needs separate consent; do not send client_user_id

india-account-aggregator.name: India Account Aggregator (Sahamati/ReBIT AA network)
india-account-aggregator.rationale: The highest-quality posted ledger in India, with a strong consent model and FIP-to-FIU encryption. It is gated by the regulated-FIU requirement, posted-only data, the 45-fetches/month ceiling and a 31-day Data Life under purpose 102. Credit-card data (MCC, dues) is not a first-class FI type in AA API v1.1.2 or in the fair-use rules, so do not count on it. In India, near-real-time awareness should come from notifications/SMS, with AA adding correction, balances and investment/transfer disambiguation.
india-account-aggregator.typical_latency: On-demand fetch, bounded by consent Frequency (default purpose-102 rule: <= 1/day or <= 45 per calendar month). Posted transactions only. As of 2026-10-04.
india-account-aggregator.access_requirements: BRAKE must be, or partner with, an FIU, defined in the RBI NBFC-AA Master Direction as 'an entity registered with and regulated by any financial sector regulator' (verified via a mirror of the MD text updated 22 Feb 2024). Integration goes through an AA or TSP (e.g. Finvu, Setu). Sahamati fair-use templates must be followed and the exact purpose text displayed.
india-account-aggregator.policy_constraints: Consent is created only in the AA's app. Default purpose-102 rule: PERIODIC, consent <= 1 year, FI data range <= 13 months, Data Life 31 days. CT019 (7 days) is an FIU-specific exception. Violations return HTTP 412. DPDP Rules 2025 were notified 13 Nov 2025, with most obligations from 13 May 2027.
data_fields: credit card (if obtainable): mcc, maskedCardNumber, dueDate, totalDueAmount, minDueAmount

india-account-aggregator.name: India Account Aggregator (deposit and credit-card FI data)
india-account-aggregator.rationale: India's confirming ledger. The Sahamati-hosted deposit XSD has posted-only transactions with a required balance-after (currentBalance, 'Available balance'), which suits reconciliation with real-time alerts. ReBIT Deposit FI schema v2.0.0 replaced v1.x in July 2025 and changed mandatory flags, so the field list must be re-verified against v2.0.0. The credit-card FI type carries MCC and statement/due data for card-bill matching.
india-account-aggregator.access_requirements: Via a licensed NBFC-AA (as FIU or through a TSP); consent artefact with purpose, fetch frequency and data life; FIU parser must support Deposit FI schema v2.0.0 (v1.x decommissioned by FIUs before 2025-07-27 per Sahamati FAQ).
data_fields: currentBalance (Available balance; v2 mandatory status unverified)
creditcard: txnId, txnType, txnDate (date only), amount, valueDate, narration, statementDate, mcc, maskedCardNumber, currentDue, totalDueAmount, minDueAmount, dueDate
dedup_keys: UPI RRN parsed from narration (unverified format)
india-account-aggregator.policy_constraints: Consent-bound purpose and data life. Narration formats are bank-specific. txnId stability across fetches is unverified. Field set is per schema version (v2.0.0 live since mid-2025).
india-account-aggregator.typical_latency: Per consent fetch; not real-time (exact lag unverified).

india-account-aggregator.name: India RBI Account Aggregator (FIP -> AA -> FIU)
india-account-aggregator.rationale: Only entities 'registered with and regulated by any financial sector regulator' can be FIUs. This is in the 2016 Master Direction para 3(1)(xii), kept in the RBI (NBFC - Account Aggregator) Directions, 2025 (secondary). Unregulated BRAKE cannot consume AA data directly. Research the regulatory path, then go 'next' via a regulated partner FIU. The consent artefact (DataLife, Purpose, Frequency, FIDataRange) is the model for BRAKE's consent receipts.
india-account-aggregator.access_requirements: Regulated FIU status, or a partnership with a regulated FIU as its technology service provider. Sahamati Fair Use templates enforced by AAs as 'primary enforcers' (verified).
india-account-aggregator.policy_constraints: Store no longer than consent DataLife; use only for consent Purpose (verified spec v1.1.2). DPDP on top, including the Rule 8(3) one-year minimum log retention from 13 May 2027 (secondary). RBI localisation may flow down via partners (unverified).
india-account-aggregator.typical_latency: hours to a day (periodic fetch within Fair Use)

india-account-aggregator.name: India Account Aggregator consented bank data (Fold, CRED, Jupiter, Fi prior art)
india-account-aggregator.rationale: Authoritative posted ledger with explicit, revocable consent, and the reconciliation backbone for notification-sensed candidates. The ReBIT deposit schema field names are verified, and mode (CASH/ATM/CARD/UPI/FT/OTHERS) gives a rail hint. FIU or partner access requirements, a multi-step consent journey and fetch-on-demand latency make it a poor first-run experience. Indian prior art used AA mostly as a lending or investing funnel (unverified).

india-account-aggregator.name: India Account Aggregator FI data (merchant/context view)
india-account-aggregator.rationale: Deposit rows have no MCC or merchant field: only mode, narration and transactionTimestamp. transactionTimestamp is xs:dateTime, so the UTC offset is optional, and whether FIPs send a real time of day is unverified. Credit-card rows carry a required mcc attribute (the sample is empty and actual population is unverified), and txnDate is date-only. The card Summary has dueDate, totalDueAmount and minDueAmount for upcoming bills. Consent purpose code 102 ('Customer spending patterns, budget or other reportings') fits BRAKE.
india-account-aggregator.access_requirements: RBI-regulated FIU onboarding with an AA
india-account-aggregator.policy_constraints: Purpose-coded consent artefact (101-105), dataLife, periodic fetch at most 1 per hour (Setu doc citing the AA spec)

india-aa-providers-and-tsps.name: India AA providers and TSPs (Setu, Finvu, OneMoney, Anumati)
india-aa-providers-and-tsps.rationale: The integration plumbing for AA consent and FI fetch. All are bound by the same fair-use rules. Choose by FIP coverage and fetch success rates once a regulated FIU partner is in place. Finvu is confirmed as an AA in Sahamati's repo; the other roles are unverified.

uk-open-banking-ais.name: UK Open Banking AIS (OBIE Read/Write v4.0.1)
uk-open-banking-ais.rationale: Rich standardized data: MerchantDetails, CardInstrument, ISO purpose codes, booking/pending/future status, and standing orders, direct debits and scheduled payments for pre-spend obligations. Poll-only, because the event-notification spec defines only resource-update events. Access via an aggregator's AISP licence or agency.
uk-open-banking-ais.typical_latency: Poll-based. Under UK-RTS Art. 36(5), <= 4 per 24 h without the user present and unlimited while the user is active (secondary; the FCA Handbook was unreachable). Same-day for Faster Payments.
uk-open-banking-ais.access_requirements: Registered AISP under PSRs 2017, or agent/client of an authorised AISP (TrueLayer, Plaid UK, Tink, Yapily, etc.). The perimeter question needs counsel.
uk-open-banking-ais.policy_constraints: FCA PS21/19 replaced bank-side 90-day SCA with AISP 90-day consent reconfirmation. 2026 secondary sources still describe it as current, and the in-force date is unverified. Consumer Duty.

uk-open-banking-ais.name: UK Open Banking Account and Transaction API v4.0.1
uk-open-banking-ais.rationale: Rich but optional reconciliation fields: TransactionReference (may be the FPID), Balance (typed ITAV/ITBD), CreditorAccount (own-account detection), CurrencyExchange, ISO CategoryPurposeCode (GP2P/MP2P/MP2B/SALA/SWEP/TOPG; CCRD is ambiguous), and MerchantDetails.MCC. TransactionId is unique and immutable when present but optional. There is no pending→booked link, and bank adoption of v4 fields is unverified.
uk-open-banking-ais.access_requirements: FCA-authorised AISP or agent; periodic consent reconfirmation rules (details unverified this session).

uk-open-banking-ais.name: UK Open Banking account information (FCA)
uk-open-banking-ais.rationale: Mature bank API coverage. Requires FCA AISP registration or agent status (unverified). The consent model is explicit and bounded: Permissions, ExpirationDateTime and transaction date range (verified, OBIE spec), a good template for BRAKE consent receipts. Unlike the EU, there is no periodic bank-side SCA, but the AISP must have the user reconfirm every 90 days.
uk-open-banking-ais.access_requirements: FCA-registered AISP or agent of one (unverified). Consumer Duty if FCA-regulated (unverified). SCA-RTS Art. 10A removes periodic bank-side SCA; Art. 36(6) requires the AISP to have the user reconfirm consent every 90 days or stop background access (secondary).
uk-open-banking-ais.policy_constraints: UK GDPR as amended by the Data (Use and Access) Act 2025, with Arts 22A-22D in force since 5 Feb 2026 (secondary). Consent ExpirationDateTime is open-ended if unset (verified).

uk-open-banking-ais.name: UK Open Banking Account and Transaction API v4.0.1 merchant fields
uk-open-banking-ais.rationale: MerchantDetails provides MerchantName and a 3-4 character MerchantCategoryCode. CardInstrument provides CardSchemeName and AuthorisationType (ConsumerDevice, Contactless, None or PIN), which indicates whether the card was present. Fields are conditional, so population varies by bank.
uk-open-banking-ais.access_requirements: FCA-authorised AISP or agent of one

uk-open-banking-vrp.name: UK Variable Recurring Payments (sweeping / commercial VRP)
uk-open-banking-vrp.rationale: A write capability, not a signal. It could power an opt-in 'sweep what you did not spend to savings' intervention. Requires PISP permissions or a partner. Plaid exposes supports_commercial_payment_consents per institution. UKPI launched its commercial VRP scheme on 2 June 2026 (secondary); bank coverage and permitted use cases are unverified.

eu-psd2-ais.name: EU PSD2 AIS (Berlin Group NextGenPSD2, STET, national standards)
eu-psd2-ais.rationale: Broad bank coverage, but banks implement subsets of the standard. Background access defaults to 4 per 24 h, while user-initiated access is uncapped. The bank requires SCA again every 180 days for AISP access. Use an aggregator, not direct bank integrations. As of May 2026, PSD3/PSR were at the early-second-reading stage and not applicable; FiDA status is unknown.
eu-psd2-ais.typical_latency: Poll-based. Without the user present: <= 4 per 24 h unless a higher frequency is agreed bilaterally with the user's consent. Unlimited while the user is actively requesting (RTS Art. 36(5)).
eu-psd2-ais.access_requirements: AISP registration with a home NCA plus passporting, or agent/licence-as-a-service via Tink, Salt Edge, TrueLayer or Plaid (specifics unverified).
eu-psd2-ais.policy_constraints: RTS 2018/389 Art. 36(5) access-frequency rule; Arts. 10/10a (as amended by Delegated Reg. 2022/2360, consolidated 2023-07-25) 180-day SCA renewal; GDPR.

eu-psd2-ais.name: EU PSD2 account information services (open banking)
eu-psd2-ais.rationale: AIS is a regulated payment service. The route is a licensed AISP partner (agent or licence-as-a-service); own AISP registration is later. The EBA's 2025 white-labelling report means licence-as-a-service arrangements may be re-characterised in 2026. PSD2 Art. 67 limits use to the AIS the user explicitly requested and bars requesting sensitive payment data (unverified).
eu-psd2-ais.access_requirements: AISP registration (PSD2 Art. 33) and PII insurance, or an agent or licensed-partner model (unverified). Bank-side SCA at most every 180 days under Delegated Regulation (EU) 2022/2360, in force since 25 Jul 2023 (secondary); some aggregators still enforce 90 days.
eu-psd2-ais.policy_constraints: GDPR plus PSD2 explicit consent. Silent-party data only for the service (EDPB 06/2020, unverified). PSD3/PSR: provisional agreement 27 Nov 2025, formal adoption pending as of 2026-10-04 (secondary); permission dashboards (unverified).

brazil-open-finance.name: Open Finance Brasil (customer data APIs)
brazil-open-finance.rationale: Mandatory counterparty CPF/CNPJ (since 02/05/2023, IN BCB 371) gives the strongest transfer-vs-spending signal of any regime, and LANCAMENTO_FUTURO gives future obligations up to 12 months ahead. Brazil is not an initial market, and access requires a BCB-authorised receiver or partner (unverified).
brazil-open-finance.typical_latency: Poll; /transactions-current covers 7 days back plus 12 months forward; Pix near-real-time (unverified).
brazil-open-finance.access_requirements: BCB-authorised receiving institution, or partner platform (unverified).
brazil-open-finance.policy_constraints: Consents may be indefinite (expirationDateTime omitted) or time-limited and extendable via /extends; unauthorised consents are REJECTED after 60 minutes. LGPD.

brazil-open-finance.name: Open Finance Brasil accounts transactions + Pix EndToEndId
brazil-open-finance.rationale: Not a launch market. Counterparty person type (PESSOA_NATURAL/JURIDICA) and counterparty CPF/CNPJ give deterministic P2P/P2M and own-account detection, and the same pattern should shape BRAKE's counterparty model. transactionId immutability is D0 for PIX/TED/TEF and D+1 for DOC/BOLETO and others. The Pix EndToEndId time is only a ±12 h bound.
dedup_keys: transactionId (once TRANSACAO_EFETIVADA; D0 or D+1 by type)
brazil-open-finance.policy_constraints: Counterparty tax IDs are third-party personal data; hash them on ingestion.

australia-cdr.name: Australia Consumer Data Right (banking, NBL/BNPL)
australia-cdr.rationale: Mature standards (v1.36.0, 2025-12-04, still the latest on master as of 2026-10-04) with merchantName, MCC and BPAY fields, but no pending-to-posted correlation guarantee (retained in the current v1.36.0 OpenAPI). Access requires ADR status or a CDR representative arrangement. Not an initial market.
australia-cdr.access_requirements: ACCC accreditation as an ADR, or CDR representative of a principal ADR (e.g. Basiq) (unverified).
australia-cdr.policy_constraints: Consent duration capped at one year (sharing_duration). Deletion/de-identification duties (unverified).

us-fdx-bank-apis.name: US bank FDX APIs / Section 1033 developer interfaces
us-fdx-bank-apis.rationale: Banks expose FDX APIs to aggregators, not to individual apps (unverified). The 2024 §1033 rule is enjoined (E.D. Ky., 29 Oct 2025; secondary) and under reconsideration. A reconsideration rule went to OIRA on 2026-08-04 (secondary). Banks have begun charging aggregators for access (JPMorgan, 2025; secondary). Consume through Plaid or MX rather than integrating directly.
us-fdx-bank-apis.policy_constraints: CFPB 1033 rule enjoined and under reconsideration as of 2026-10-04 (CFPB site lists an ANPR, verified via mirror; injunction and OIRA submission are secondary). GLBA / FTC Safeguards Rule.

canada-consumer-driven-banking.name: Canada consumer-driven banking framework
canada-consumer-driven-banking.rationale: A first Act passed in 2024 (C-69). A more comprehensive Consumer-Driven Banking Act (Bill C-15) received Royal Assent on 26 Mar 2026, with draft regulations pre-published in the Canada Gazette I on 27 Jun 2026. The Bank of Canada oversees it, and Phase 1 is read-only. It was not live as of mid/late 2026 (all secondary). Serve Canada through Plaid until accreditation opens.
canada-consumer-driven-banking.policy_constraints: Reported screen-scraping prohibition once the regime applies (secondary).

singapore-sgfindex.name: Singapore Financial Data Exchange (SGFinDex)
singapore-sgfindex.rationale: Singpass-consented sharing only among participating financial institutions and government agencies, viewed in their apps; not open to third-party fintechs (unverified). Singapore users need device, email and manual sources.

saudi-open-banking.name: Saudi Arabia SAMA Open Banking Framework (AIS)
saudi-open-banking.rationale: AIS framework (2022) and sandbox exist (unverified). Licensing path for a foreign consumer app and aggregator coverage are unclear.

uae-open-finance.name: UAE CBUAE Open Finance (Al Tareq / Nebras)
uae-open-finance.rationale: Open Finance Regulation and central infrastructure rolling out from 2025 (unverified). Licensing requirements for consumer apps are to be determined.

japan-bank-api-episp.name: Japan bank APIs for registered electronic payment intermediaries
japan-bank-api-episp.rationale: Under the 2017 Banking Act amendment, apps need FSA registration and contracts with each bank for read APIs (unverified). Likely served through a partner (Money Forward or Moneytree-style platforms).

mexico-open-finance.name: Mexico open finance (Ley Fintech Art. 76)
mexico-open-finance.rationale: Secondary rules for transactional data were never issued (unverified). Aggregators rely on credential-based access, which BRAKE should avoid.

truelayer-data-api.name: TrueLayer Data API
truelayer-data-api.rationale: UK-first AIS/PIS aggregator with a separate pending-transactions endpoint, standing orders, direct debits and an agent model (field names unverified this session). Shortlisted with Plaid UK for the UK launch.

tink-data.name: Tink (Visa) account data and enrichment
tink-data.rationale: Broad EU PSD2 coverage, categorisation/enrichment and licence-as-a-service (unverified). EU option alongside Plaid.

salt-edge-account-information.name: Salt Edge Account Information
salt-edge-account-information.rationale: Wide but uneven multi-country coverage (some connectors credential-based) and a partner programme for unlicensed clients (unverified). Useful for long-tail markets later.

gocardless-bank-account-data.name: GoCardless Bank Account Data (ex-Nordigen)
gocardless-bank-account-data.rationale: Official client libraries are 'no longer actively updated or maintained' (last Python release 1.4.2, 2025-04-07). GoCardless reportedly stopped accepting new Bank Account Data accounts in July 2025 (secondary: Actual Budget docs). It is unavailable to a new build such as BRAKE.

mx-platform.name: MX Platform API
mx-platform.rationale: US redundancy option to Plaid. Spec shows transaction status (POSTED/PENDING), is_subscription, is_recurring, merchant_guid, MCC, transacted_at vs posted_at, and repeating_transactions with predicted_occurs_on.

mastercard-open-banking-finicity.name: Mastercard Open Banking (Finicity / Aiia)
mastercard-open-banking-finicity.rationale: Strong in lending/verification use cases (unverified). An alternative aggregator if Plaid pricing or coverage fails.

yodlee.name: Envestnet Yodlee
yodlee.rationale: Long-tail global coverage on an older stack. Envestnet announced the sale of Yodlee to STG in June 2025 (secondary; closing unverified), which adds ownership-transition risk. It reportedly has an Indian AA-licensed affiliate (unverified). Fallback option only.

akoya-data-access-network.name: Akoya Data Access Network
akoya-data-access-network.rationale: Bank-owned, FDX-based, API-only network (unverified). Its reach comes through aggregators, so a direct integration adds little for BRAKE.

belvo.name: Belvo
belvo.rationale: LatAm aggregator; Open Finance Brasil receiver; credential-based connectors elsewhere (unverified). Relevant only when BRAKE enters LatAm.

basiq.name: Basiq
basiq.rationale: Australian ADR offering a CDR representative model, so BRAKE could avoid its own accreditation (unverified). Relevant when BRAKE enters Australia.

enable-banking.name: Enable Banking (EU/UK AIS aggregator)
enable-banking.rationale: Missing from the doc's aggregator landscape. GoCardless Bank Account Data closed to new signups in July 2025, and Enable Banking is one of the remaining EU-wide AIS options that 2026 integrator notes cite for low-volume use: a Finnish-FSA-registered AISP with about 2,700 banks in 30 European countries, whose per-bank maximum consent validity is commonly 180 days. All of this is secondary and unverified; vendor docs were not reachable. Benchmark it alongside Tink, TrueLayer and Plaid for the EU tail.

apple-financekit.name: Apple FinanceKit (full-authorization queries + background delivery)
apple-financekit.rationale: Only sanctioned iOS on-device feed of card and bank transactions (US: Apple Card, Apple Cash, Savings; UK: Wallet connected open-banking accounts). Rich fields (status, transactionType, MCC, FX) and processed locally, but entitlement-gated, US/UK only, and background delivery at most hourly, so it serves post-spend only (pre-spend only weakly via due dates and balances).
apple-financekit.access_requirements: Managed entitlement com.apple.developer.financekit requested by the Account Holder of an organization Apple Developer account and granted per bundle ID; app listed in the Finance category and distributed on the US/UK iPhone App Store; must provide financial management tools; NSFinancialDataUsageDescription; user authorization per account with an earliest-date choice.
apple-financekit.policy_constraints: Excludes Apple Card Family participants and children using Apple Cash Family; App Review 5.1.1(ix) requires submission by a legal entity for financial services; the user can revoke access in Settings.
dedup_keys: FinanceKit Transaction.id (device-scoped, stable across status changes)
apple-financekit.typical_latency: Foreground: as Wallet updates; background: within ~1 hour (.hourly), or daily/weekly

apple-financekit.name: FinanceKit (Wallet accounts, balances, transactions; cross-reference to stream 02)
apple-financekit.rationale: On-device Wallet financial data with status and MCC; the iOS 26 background delivery extension enables timely updates. Coverage is narrow in the US: only Apple Card, Apple Cash and Savings (iOS 17.4+), so it confirms Wallet taps only for those cards. In the UK (iOS 18.4+) it uses open banking to reach major banks (Barclays, HSBC, Lloyds, Monzo, Nationwide, NatWest, Santander, etc.), which makes it a broader on-device feed there.
apple-financekit.access_requirements: Managed FinanceKit entitlement (Apple reviews against criteria); organization-level developer account; Account Holder request; NSFinancialDataUsageDescription; app listed in the Finance category and distributed on the US or UK App Store for iPhone, providing financial management tools (e.g., budgeting).
apple-financekit.policy_constraints: Wallet orders: documented API is save-only (no third-party read). TransactionPicker allows user-selected sharing. Issuers offering financial products must not block sharing with FinanceKit.
apple-financekit.typical_latency: background delivery (iOS 26) or on app open

apple-financekit.name: Apple FinanceKit transactions
apple-financekit.rationale: On-device and clean for reconciliation. It has a status enum (authorized/pending/booked/rejected/memo), a type enum (transfer, billPayment, refund…), MCC, and foreignCurrencyAmount as an exact FX bridge. From iOS 26.0, a BackgroundDeliveryExtension delivers finance-store changes (latency unverified). Whether `id` (documented only as 'A unique internal ID') is stable across status changes is unverified. Account/country coverage belongs to the FinanceKit stream.
apple-financekit.access_requirements: Managed entitlement, organization developer account (Account Holder), NSFinancialDataUsageDescription; iOS 17.4+ (background delivery iOS 26.0+).

apple-financekit.name: Apple FinanceKit (Wallet financial data on the device)
apple-financekit.rationale: Reading on the device behind user authorisation (requestAuthorization()) aligns with local-first storage, and data not sent off the device is not 'collected' per Apple (verified). Gated by a managed entitlement that Apple reviews case by case (verified). The docs do not state country availability; the US-only entry is (unverified).
apple-financekit.access_requirements: FinanceKit managed entitlement: meet Apple's criteria, organisation-level developer account, request made by the Account Holder, usage-description string; Apple reviews each application (verified).
apple-financekit.policy_constraints: Apple 5.1.1/5.1.2 data use limits; no repurposing without consent (verified).

apple-financekit.name: Apple FinanceKit on-device Wallet financial data
apple-financekit.rationale: The only aggregator-free, on-device financial source on iOS. Covers Apple Card, Apple Cash and Savings (US, iOS 17.4+) and 13 UK banks via Wallet (iOS 18.4+); still US/UK only as of 2026-10-04. Supports incremental history tokens, and background delivery to an extension on iOS 26+ (hourly/daily/weekly as minimum intervals). Gated by a managed entitlement and Finance-category eligibility. Guideline 3.2.1(viii) (money-management apps submitted by the financial institution) is an extra review risk. Apply during MVP and ship as soon as granted.
apple-financekit.typical_latency: on-device; background delivery no more often than hourly, and only when data changes (iOS 26+)
apple-financekit.access_requirements: Managed entitlement request by the organization's Account Holder; NSFinancialDataUsageDescription; Finance category; US/UK App Store distribution
apple-financekit.policy_constraints: App Review 5.1.1(ix) legal-entity requirement; 3.2.1(viii) money-management apps 'should be submitted by the financial institution' (interpretation for PFMs unverified); 5.1.2 data-use limits

apple-financekit.name: Apple FinanceKit (Wallet transactions)
apple-financekit.rationale: On-device Transaction data with merchantName, merchantCategoryCode (an Int16 raw value, so leading zeros are lost), foreignCurrencyAmount and originalTransactionDescription. US: iOS 17.4+, with Apple Card (excluding Apple Card Family participants), Apple Cash (excluding children in Apple Cash Family) and Savings. UK: iOS 18.4+, using open banking with institutions 'including' 13 named banks, which is not a closed list.
apple-financekit.access_requirements: FinanceKit managed entitlement, requested by the Account Holder and granted per bundle ID (whether an organization account is required is unverified). The app must be in the Finance category, distributed on the US or UK App Store, and provide financial management tools. NSFinancialDataUsageDescription is required.
apple-financekit.policy_constraints: Apple review criteria; US/UK App Store only

apple-financekit-transaction-picker.name: Apple FinanceKitUI TransactionPicker
apple-financekit-transaction-picker.rationale: The user picks specific Wallet transactions to share, with ephemeral access ('the picker will not remember or store any of the transactions shared') and fewer requirements than full access. Narrowest consent; a good fallback if the full entitlement is denied.
apple-financekit-transaction-picker.access_requirements: iOS 18.0+; whether the full managed entitlement is required is unverified ('fewer requirements' per Apple).
data_fields: FinanceKit Transaction fields for the selected transactions only

apple-wallet-orders.name: Apple Wallet Orders / automatic order tracking
apple-wallet-orders.rationale: Merchants (and, since iOS 26, Apple Intelligence parsing Mail) create orders with orderNumber, lineItems and fulfillments. Third-party apps can only add or update orders (saveOrder(signedArchive:), iOS 17+) and cannot read them. Apple names no countries for Mail-based tracking (it follows Apple Intelligence availability; country list unverified), and the reported iOS 27 AU/CA expansion is unverified. Item context must come from the email stream.
apple-wallet-orders.access_requirements: None to write own orders; there is no read access.

ios-shortcuts-wallet-transaction-automat.name: iOS Shortcuts personal automation on Wallet card tap
ios-shortcuts-wallet-transaction-automat.rationale: Reported to fire when the user taps a chosen Wallet card and to pass merchant, amount and card name to a shortcut that can call a BRAKE App Intent. It could be the only seconds-latency iOS signal for Apple Pay taps on any card. Fields and behaviour were unverified in this session (support.apple.com blocked); this mechanism is shared with the iOS device-signals stream.
ios-shortcuts-wallet-transaction-automat.access_requirements: User-configured automation; App Intent exposed by BRAKE.

google-wallet.name: Google Wallet / Google Pay transaction data
google-wallet.rationale: Google Wallet APIs are for issuing passes and the Google Pay API is for merchants. No third-party read API for users' payment history was found (unverified; developers.google.com blocked, no primary citation available). Post-tap Wallet notifications should be handled as a template inside android-notification-listener.
google-wallet.access_requirements: No read API (unverified); NotificationListenerService via the Android-notifications stream.
data_fields: notification merchant and amount (via notification listener; format unverified)

fidel-select-transactions.name: Fidel API Select Transactions (card-linked)
fidel-select-transactions.rationale: Real-time network-grade auth, clearing and refund events, but only for purchases at program locations. Each location requires 'the Brand (with approved consent)', so a protective watch-list would need the watched merchant to agree, which is unlikely. Locations take 1-2 weeks to sync and the economics are offer-oriented. JP is beta. Docs current to 2026-09-21.
fidel-select-transactions.access_requirements: Commercial Fidel contract; program with brands that have approved consent and onboarded locations (Location Sync 1-2 weeks); card linking via SDK with termsOfUse opt-in; Visa, Mastercard, Amex.
fidel-select-transactions.policy_constraints: Merchant-subset coverage; brand consent required per location; offer-driven model conflicts with BRAKE's mission.
fidel-select-transactions.typical_latency: Auth: real-time (seconds; no SLA seen); clearing: 48-72 h

card-network-card-linked-offers.name: Visa / Mastercard / Amex card-linked offer and issuer-control programmes
card-network-card-linked-offers.rationale: Offer programmes report only qualifying merchant transactions. Real-time consumer controls and alerts (e.g. Visa Transaction Controls) are issuer-integrated and not open to non-issuer apps (unverified; network developer portals blocked).
card-network-card-linked-offers.access_requirements: Network partner agreements; issuer participation for controls.

cardlytics.name: Cardlytics bank-channel offers
cardlytics.rationale: Advertising platform embedded in partner banks' channels; no consumer-consented data feed to third-party apps, and its purpose (driving merchant spend) conflicts with BRAKE's (details unverified; site blocked).
cardlytics.access_requirements: Not available to consumer apps as a data source (unverified).

visa-intelligent-commerce.name: Visa Intelligent Commerce / Trusted Agent Protocol (agentic commerce)
visa-intelligent-commerce.rationale: AI agents buying with tokenized credentials create a new purchase-instruction step where BRAKE could act as a consumer spending policy. It also introduces PAR as a cross-token card identifier. Emerging; consumer-app eligibility unverified.
visa-intelligent-commerce.access_requirements: Visa Developer Center credentials; partner eligibility unverified.

brake-issued-card.name: BRAKE-issued card with real-time authorization decisioning (umbrella)
brake-issued-card.rationale: The only mechanism with true in-spend control (approve or decline within the processor window: 2 s for Adyen, 1-7 s configurable for Marqeta JIT, unverified for Stripe and Lithic) plus instant authoritative post-spend events. Lithic adds an out-of-band cardholder challenge. It covers only spend on the BRAKE card and needs a sponsor bank or EMI programme, KYC, Reg E or e-money compliance and network rules. Best as a later opt-in commitment card with user-authored rules, essential-MCC safe-lists and fail-open fallback (confirm each processor's timeout default).
brake-issued-card.access_requirements: Issuer processor (Adyen/Stripe/Lithic/Marqeta) plus BIN sponsor bank or EMI; KYC/AML; Apple/Google Pay provisioning agreements (unverified specifics). Country availability per processor unverified.
brake-issued-card.policy_constraints: Regulated programme-manager role; declines at point of sale carry harm risk; must fail open.
brake-issued-card.typical_latency: <1 s (decision deadline 2-7 s depending on processor)

brake-issued-card.name: BRAKE-issued debit/prepaid/virtual card with real-time authorization webhooks
brake-issued-card.rationale: Pre-approval visibility (e.g. Stripe Issuing issuing_authorization.request with amount, merchant_data.category_code, network_data.transaction_id, card spending_controls) but needs a sponsor bank or licence (RBI PPI/co-brand in India, unverified), compliance, and users switching instruments; conflicts with the 'not the rail' principle for MVP.
brake-issued-card.access_requirements: BaaS issuer-processor + sponsor bank / licence; KYC/AML

adyen-issuing-relayed-authorisation.name: Adyen Issuing relayed authorisation + transaction webhooks
adyen-issuing-relayed-authorisation.rationale: Documented 2-second response window with configurable fallback logic: the right pattern for a fail-open decision hook. balancePlatform.transaction.created provides pending and booked events.
adyen-issuing-relayed-authorisation.access_requirements: Adyen Issuing / Balance Platform account and programme approval (country availability unverified).

stripe-issuing-realtime-auth.name: Stripe Issuing real-time authorizations (issuing_authorization.request)
stripe-issuing-realtime-auth.rationale: Rich authorization object (merchant_data with category_code, authorization_method, wallet, pending_request with network_risk_score), approved by responding to the webhook directly. Exact response window and consumer-programme eligibility unverified (docs blocked).
stripe-issuing-realtime-auth.access_requirements: Stripe Issuing approval; consumer programmes need sponsor-bank approval (unverified).

lithic-auth-stream-access.name: Lithic Auth Stream Access (ASA) + Authorization Challenges
lithic-auth-stream-access.rationale: HMAC-signed synchronous authorization decisioning with a fully documented request schema. Response result APPROVED approves and any other value declines. CHALLENGE (cardholder-initiated only) plus the card_authorization.challenge webhook gives an out-of-band 'confirm with the cardholder' path, a potential gentler in-spend friction than a hard decline. The response deadline and timeout default are unverified; a CUSTOMER_ASA_TIMEOUT detailed result exists, so treat it as possibly fail-closed until confirmed.
lithic-auth-stream-access.access_requirements: Lithic programme and sponsor bank (US; other countries unverified).
lithic-auth-stream-access.policy_constraints: Regulated card programme; timeout behaviour must be confirmed to be fail-open before use.
lithic-auth-stream-access.typical_latency: <1 s (deadline unverified); challenge path asynchronous (lifetime unverified)

marqeta-gateway-jit.name: Marqeta Gateway JIT Funding
marqeta-gateway-jit.rationale: The programme funds or declines each authorization in real time. The gateway funding-source timeout_millis is configurable from 1000 to 7000 ms. Commando Mode (COMMANDO_AUTO on timeout or error, or COMMANDO_MANUAL) 'makes a decision in your place based on defined business rules', so those rules must be set to approve for fail-open. MANAGED_JIT marks Commando-funded transactions, and unsent webhooks are replayed later. Country availability is unverified.
marqeta-gateway-jit.access_requirements: Marqeta programme plus sponsor bank (country list unverified).
marqeta-gateway-jit.policy_constraints: Regulated programme-manager role; Commando Mode business rules must be configured to fail open.

investec-card-code.name: Investec Programmable Banking Card Code (beforeTransaction/afterTransaction/afterDecline)
investec-card-code.rationale: User-deployed JavaScript runs at authorization on the user's own bank card: beforeTransaction returns true or false. This gives in-spend decisioning without BRAKE being an issuer. The template warns of a 'limited execution time' (no number given), and outbound calls are unverified. It is a reference design for the DecisionHook interface, with small, premium reach.
investec-card-code.access_requirements: Investec private-banking client; OAuth2 with 'cards' scope; programmable feature toggled per card (toggle-programmable-feature).
data_fields: simulation inputs: centsAmount, currencyCode, merchantCode, merchantName, merchantCity, countryCode
investec-card-code.typical_latency: <1 s (execution limit exists but is unspecified)

investec-programmable-banking.name: Investec Programmable Banking account information API
investec-programmable-banking.rationale: OAuth API with accounts, balance, transactions and pending-transactions endpoints for SA private-banking clients. Niche; pair with Card Code.

monzo-developer-api.name: Monzo Developer API + transaction.created webhook
monzo-developer-api.rationale: Excellent seconds-latency webhooks with merchant enrichment and decline reasons, but Monzo states the API 'is not suitable for building public applications' (own account or small allow-list only). Use it for internal dogfooding and fusion ground truth; reach Monzo users via UK open banking or FinanceKit UK.
monzo-developer-api.access_requirements: OAuth with in-app SCA approval; one active token per user; refresh tokens only for confidential clients; full history only within 5 minutes of auth, then 90 days.

starling-developer-api.name: Starling Bank Public API (personal tokens/webhooks)
starling-developer-api.rationale: Public API and Payment Services API exist (official samples); the SDK is archived and unsupported. Personal-token, webhook and third-party production terms are unverified (portal blocked); assume personal-use-only.

up-bank-api.name: Up Bank API (Australia) + webhooks
up-bank-api.rationale: Beta API, Personal Access Tokens only. Webhooks TRANSACTION_CREATED/SETTLED/DELETED, signed with X-Up-Authenticity-Signature, give a seconds-latency HELD-to-SETTLED lifecycle. Webhooks carry only an id and link, so the relay must fetch details with the token. On rare occasions SETTLED is replaced by DELETED + CREATED (new id), so DELETED is only a provisional cancellation. Third-party PAT use is a ToS and security question; the sanctioned route is CDR.
up-bank-api.access_requirements: Personal Access Token from api.up.com.au; no OAuth for third parties.
up-bank-api.policy_constraints: Personal use; PAT sharing with third parties unverified.
dedup_keys: Up transaction id (usually stable; replaced in rare DELETED+CREATED case)

revolut-open-banking-api.name: Revolut Open Banking API (AIS)
revolut-open-banking-api.rationale: The only third-party route to Revolut retail data, via a regulated TPP or licensed aggregator. Provides Pending/Booked status, MerchantName, ProprietaryBankTransactionCode and CardInstrument. It provides NO MCC: OBMerchantDetails1 has only MerchantName. Full history only within 5 minutes of consent, then 90 days. After that, unattended reads are capped at 4 per account per 24 h, so background freshness is about 6 h; on-demand reads are allowed while the user is present. There is no retail personal API.
revolut-open-banking-api.access_requirements: Regulated PSD2 TPP (AISP) or licensed aggregator.
revolut-open-banking-api.policy_constraints: No more than 4 unattended transaction reads per account per 24 h after the first 5 minutes; 90-day history after 5 minutes.
revolut-open-banking-api.typical_latency: Unattended: up to 4 polls per 24 h (about 6 h); user present: on demand

wise-personal-api.name: Wise personal API tokens + webhooks
wise-personal-api.rationale: Personal tokens and webhooks exist, but event names, scopes and PSD2 restrictions for UK/EEA personal tokens could not be verified (docs blocked). Assume personal-use-only.

brazil-open-finance-credit-cards.name: Open Finance Brasil credit-card accounts API (incl. Nubank)
brazil-open-finance-credit-cards.rationale: A regulated route to Nubank and other issuers' card data, with payeeMCC, bills, limits, 12-month history, a 7-day transactions-current window and instalment fields (chargeIdentificator = instalment number, required for A_PRAZO; chargeNumber = instalment count). transactionType values: PAGAMENTO, TARIFA, OPERACOES_CREDITO_CONTRATADAS_CARTAO, ESTORNO, CASHBACK, OUTROS. v2.3.1 is the latest stable version; 2.4.0-beta.2 exists. Adopt the instalment and bill model in the schema now.
brazil-open-finance-credit-cards.access_requirements: Authorised Open Finance Brasil participant or licensed aggregator; ecosystem consent API.

paypal-transaction-search.name: PayPal Transaction Search API
paypal-transaction-search.rationale: Merchant-reporting API: third parties must be in the PayPal partner network; up to 3 h latency; 31-day query windows. Not a consumer-consented personal history feed. Resolve PayPal merchants via receipt emails joined to card or bank debits.
paypal-transaction-search.access_requirements: Account owner credentials or PayPal partner network.

us-p2p-wallet-history.name: Venmo / Cash App transaction history
us-p2p-wallet-history.rationale: No public consumer-data APIs found (unverified). Sense these via app notifications, emails and the funding debit, with a strong transfer/shared-expense prior. Future §1033 coverage of digital wallets belongs to the Plaid/1033 stream.

india-wallet-history.name: Paytm / PhonePe / Amazon Pay wallet history
india-wallet-history.rationale: No consumer-consented third-party history APIs found (unverified). Most spend is UPI, so use bank AA data, SMS and notifications keyed on UPI RRN. PPI wallet-funded spend is the remaining gap.

sea-wallet-history.name: GCash / GrabPay wallet history
sea-wallet-history.rationale: Only merchant-acceptance developer products found (unverified); track Philippine open-finance developments. Sense via notifications, SMS and email receipts meanwhile.

mpesa-statements.name: M-Pesa confirmation SMS and statements
mpesa-statements.rationale: Daraja APIs serve organisations with shortcodes, not consumers (unverified, portal blocked). Each transaction produces a confirmation SMS with a unique transaction code (real time, excellent dedup key), and PDF statements support batch backfill via user upload with local parsing.
mpesa-statements.access_requirements: Android SMS access where policy permits (SMS stream) or user-uploaded statement.

storekit-app-store-server-api.name: StoreKit / App Store Server API purchase receipts
storekit-app-store-server-api.rationale: First-party only: Transaction is a purchase 'in your app'; the Server API returns data for 'your app' customers; showManageSubscriptions shows only 'your app' subscriptions. It cannot detect the user's other subscriptions.
storekit-app-store-server-api.access_requirements: Only for BRAKE's own in-app purchases.

google-play-billing.name: Google Play Billing purchase data
google-play-billing.rationale: First-party only: sells digital goods 'in your Android app', and queryPurchasesAsync covers your app's purchases. Billing Library 8+ is required for new apps and updates from 2026-08-31, with extensions available until 2026-11-01. Relevant only to BRAKE's own monetization.
google-play-billing.access_requirements: Only for BRAKE's own in-app purchases.

app-store-receipt-emails.name: App Store / Google Play receipt emails + card descriptors for subscription detection
app-store-receipt-emails.rationale: The practical route to cross-app subscription intelligence: receipt emails name the app, price and renewal date (enabling pre-spend renewal nudges), and bank or card descriptors (e.g. APPLE.COM/BILL, unverified) confirm the charge. Sender and template details unverified; belongs with the email stream.
app-store-receipt-emails.access_requirements: Email connector with narrow sender filters; bank or card feed for descriptor confirmation.

bnpl-provider-history.name: BNPL provider history (Klarna, Afterpay/Clearpay, Affirm and similar)
bnpl-provider-history.rationale: Missed by the doc. BNPL splits one purchase into several card or bank debits, the same instalment-group problem as Brazilian parcelado, and upcoming instalments are strong PRE-SPEND obligations. No consumer-consented third-party data API was verified (unverified; not researched in this session). Sense via order and schedule emails, app notifications and the matching card or bank debits, modelled with purchase_group/instalment_of.
bnpl-provider-history.access_requirements: None verified; email and notification streams plus bank or card feeds.
data_fields: instalment schedule and due dates (email, unverified)

mastercard-agent-pay.name: Mastercard Agent Pay (agentic commerce)
mastercard-agent-pay.rationale: Missed counterpart to Visa Intelligent Commerce. To stay network-agnostic, BRAKE's agent-spending-policy idea should be designed against both networks' agentic-token frameworks. Existence, scope and consumer-app eligibility are unverified in this session (developer.mastercard.com blocked).

android-notification-listener.name: Android NotificationListenerService
android-notification-listener.rationale: Highest coverage-to-cost Android sensor. It works across banks, UPI apps, wallets and countries, and also catches SMS/RCS bank alerts through the messaging app's notification without SMS permission. OTP content is redacted on Android 15+, OEM kills and the lack of history reduce reliability, and the all-or-nothing OS grant requires allow-list-first native filtering and on-device parsing.
android-notification-listener.typical_latency: Callback fires as soon as the notification is posted; seconds to minutes after payment depending on the issuer (unverified measurements)
android-notification-listener.access_requirements: User grants Notification access (Settings.ACTION_NOTIFICATION_LISTENER_SETTINGS / ACTION_NOTIFICATION_LISTENER_DETAIL_SETTINGS on API 30+). The service is declared with BIND_NOTIFICATION_LISTENER_SERVICE. Not available on low-RAM devices running Android 10 or lower. Android 13+ restricted settings apply to sideloaded APKs. No NLS-specific Play declaration found (unverified for 2026).
android-notification-listener.policy_constraints: Play User Data prominent-disclosure and consent rules, Data safety form, and spyware/stalkerware rules apply (details unverified). Android 15+ untrusted listeners receive redacted OTP-bearing notifications. A companion-device association or RECEIVE_SENSITIVE_NOTIFICATIONS is not obtainable or appropriate for BRAKE.
dedup_keys: SMS sender header + message timestamp (via messaging app)

android-notification-listener.name: Android NotificationListenerService on messaging apps (SMS/RCS via Messages, WhatsApp)
android-notification-listener.rationale: Expected to capture SMS and RCS alerts as the Messages app renders them, plus bank/UPI app pushes and WhatsApp, without the restricted SMS permission. That would make it the best single Android sensor for India. No cited implementation reads bank SMS/RCS from messaging-app notifications, though: PennyWise's listener allow-list has only bank/fintech apps. MVP status is therefore conditional on a device prototype (full text vs truncation, RBM sender labels, grouping, OTP redaction). Weaknesses: no history, display-name senders, and dependence on notifications being enabled. Needs package and sender allow-lists.
android-notification-listener.access_requirements: User grant in Special app access > Notification access; service protected by BIND_NOTIFICATION_LISTENER_SERVICE (signature).
android-notification-listener.policy_constraints: OTP-bearing notifications redacted for untrusted listeners (Android 15+); unavailable on low-RAM devices on Android 10 and below; ignored in work profiles; Play personal/sensitive data disclosure (unverified).

android-notification-listener.name: Bank/wallet app notifications (reconciliation keys)
android-notification-listener.rationale: The real-time founding observation, later confirmed by the ledger. Carries RRN, last4 and balance-after (formats unverified per bank), which enable near-deterministic joins with AA records. Policy assessment belongs to its own stream.

android-notification-listener.name: Android NotificationListenerService (bank/UPI/wallet app notifications)
android-notification-listener.rationale: Best-coverage, lowest-latency source that needs no regulated status, and the flagship source for India. It is legally defensible only with a user-chosen package allowlist, in-memory discard of everything else, extraction on the device, facts-only persistence and per-source consent (ePrivacy Art. 5(3) in the EU). The listener cannot bind on low-RAM devices running Android 10 or earlier, which matters for Android Go phones in India. Play Protect blocks sideloaded APKs that request it in India, so the source is effectively Play-distribution-only.
android-notification-listener.access_requirements: User enables Notification access in system Settings. Play prominent disclosure and affirmative consent (unverified). Data safety declaration. EU ePrivacy consent (unverified). In India, Play Protect enhanced fraud protection blocks internet-sideloaded apps requesting listener access (secondary). Sideloaded builds may also hit restricted settings (unverified).
android-notification-listener.policy_constraints: Android 15+ redacts OTP-bearing notifications for untrusted listeners (verified). Not available on low-RAM devices running Android Q and below; ignored in work profiles (verified). Sees all notifications including chats, health and 2FA, so allowlist filtering is mandatory. Never upload notification text by default.

android-notification-listener.name: Android NotificationListenerService on bank, UPI-app and SMS-app notifications
android-notification-listener.rationale: Lowest-friction near-real-time post-spend sensor on Android; no SMS permission needed; the natural successor to Walnut-style capture. Android 15 redacts content of OTP-bearing notifications for untrusted listeners (companion-device associations exempt). As of the 2026-10-01 docs, neither Android 16 nor Android 17 adds listener changes; Android 17 tightened SMS OTP access instead. Filter by an on-device package/sender allow-list and drop everything else.
android-notification-listener.access_requirements: User enables notification access in system settings
android-notification-listener.policy_constraints: Android 15 OTP redaction for untrusted listeners; no further listener changes in Android 16/17 docs (as of 2026-10-01)

android-sms-read.name: Android SMS inbox and SMS_RECEIVED broadcast (READ_SMS / RECEIVE_SMS)
android-sms-read.rationale: Bank SMS alerts are dense in India, and READ_SMS uniquely allows historical backfill at onboarding and capture of e-mandate pre-debit notices (PRE-SPEND for recurring payments). It is gated by a discretionary Play exception ('SMS-based money management'; Play excerpt, unverified) that requires a Permissions Declaration. OTP SMS are delayed 3 h for non-exempt apps (standard OTP SMS once targeting API 37). RCS alerts are likely not in the SMS provider (unverified). Pursue after NLS and do not make it MVP-critical.
android-sms-read.typical_latency: Seconds after SMS delivery (broadcast); backfill instant at onboarding
android-sms-read.access_requirements: READ_SMS and RECEIVE_SMS are hard-restricted permissions that the installer on record must allow-list. On Play this needs an approved Permissions Declaration under the 'SMS-based money management' exception (READ_SMS, RECEIVE_SMS, RECEIVE_MMS, RECEIVE_WAP_PUSH; Play excerpt, unverified), or the default SMS handler role (which must be requested before the permissions and requires the ability to send texts).
android-sms-read.policy_constraints: Play SMS/Call Log policy treats exceptions as temporary and allows them only where no alternative exists (Play excerpt). A revision announced 2026-07-15 takes effect 2027-01-27 (unverified; secondary corroboration only). OTP SMS are withheld 3 h from non-exempt apps: Retriever-hash format before Android 17, WebOTP for all apps on Android 17, and standard OTP SMS for apps targeting API 37.
dedup_keys: exact body match with the NLS sighting of the same SMS

android-sms-read.name: Android SMS permission capture (READ_SMS/RECEIVE_SMS: SMS_RECEIVED broadcast + provider backfill)
android-sms-read.rationale: Gives the exact originating address (the strongest sender verification), months of history for an instant baseline, and capture that does not depend on notification settings. It is also the only route any cited implementation uses for RCS (through the MMS provider). The permissions are hardRestricted and Play-gated. Play's policy lists 'SMS-based money management' as a permitted use (secondary), but approval is case by case, and the permission exposes the whole inbox. File the declaration early. Consider a RECEIVE_SMS-only variant (no backfill) to narrow the exposure.
dedup_keys: hash(normalized sender entity | normalized body) for broadcast vs provider duplicates
android-sms-read.typical_latency: real-time on arrival; history backfill on grant
android-sms-read.access_requirements: RECEIVE_SMS (+ READ_SMS for backfill) runtime grant; installer allow-listing of hard-restricted permissions; Google Play Permissions Declaration under the 'SMS-based money management' use case (secondary), demo video, prominent disclosure and runtime prompt.
android-sms-read.policy_constraints: Google Play SMS/Call Log policy; Android 17 withholds WebOTP (all apps) and standard OTP SMS (target API 37+) for 3 h; only the default SMS app can write to the provider.

android-sms-retriever.name: SMS Retriever / SMS User Consent APIs
android-sms-retriever.rationale: Designed only for phone-number verification and OTP autofill of messages addressed to the app itself (app hash or per-message consent). It cannot observe third-party bank alerts.
android-sms-retriever.typical_latency: Immediate for the targeted message (Retriever listens up to 5 minutes for one matching SMS)
android-sms-retriever.access_requirements: Google Play services (play-services-auth-api-phone); no SMS permission
android-sms-retriever.policy_constraints: Android 17 steers OTP-reading apps to these APIs; they do not apply to transaction alerts.
data_fields: single SMS body addressed to the app

android-sideload-distribution.name: Sideloaded / alternative-store distribution
android-sideload-distribution.rationale:
Getting around Play policy by sideloading runs into several obstacles:
- Android 13+ restricted settings block NLS and Accessibility grants for sideloaded apps.
- Developer verification covers installs from participating stores in BR/ID/SG/TH from 2026-09-30. Direct sideloads are not affected until the 2027 global rollout.
- Android 16 Advanced Protection Mode blocks unknown-source installs for users who opt in.
- Play Protect scanning applies.
It also mimics banking-malware distribution and damages trust.
android-sideload-distribution.access_requirements: Verified developer identity for installs from participating stores (Google Play, Galaxy Store, Xiaomi GetApps, OPPO App Market, vivo V-Appstore, HONOR App Market, Transsion Palm Store) in BR/ID/SG/TH from 2026-09-30, and for all apps on certified devices globally from 2027. Users must enable 'Allow restricted settings' for NLS and Accessibility. From 2027, unverified-developer installs need the advanced flow: developer mode, anti-coaching check, restart and re-auth, then a one-day wait. ADB is exempt. Limited-distribution accounts allow up to 20 devices.
android-sideload-distribution.policy_constraints: Android developer verification, restricted settings, Advanced Protection Mode (opt-in), and Play Protect enhanced fraud protection (scope unverified).

android-usage-stats.name: UsageStatsManager app-open / foreground events
android-usage-stats.rationale: Gives app_context such as 'shopping app opened at 23:40' or 'payment app foregrounded', which can feed regret learning and opt-in goal reminders. Limits: polling only, data unavailable while locked, events kept only a few days, no ability to shield apps on Android, and a high privacy cost. Not MVP.
android-usage-stats.typical_latency: Bound by polling interval (seconds with a foreground service; at least 15 min with WorkManager)
android-usage-stats.access_requirements: PACKAGE_USAGE_STATS app-op granted by the user via Settings.ACTION_USAGE_ACCESS_SETTINGS. Package-label lookup needs <queries> or QUERY_ALL_PACKAGES (Play declaration). queryAppUsageDuration requires QUERY_APP_USAGE (internal|role) and is unavailable to BRAKE.
android-usage-stats.policy_constraints: Data safety disclosure (unverified detail). Continuous polling needs a justified foreground-service type such as specialUse with Play review.
dedup_keys: none financial; temporal proximity to payment observations

android-usage-stats.name: Android UsageStatsManager shopping-app launch detection + notification nudge
android-usage-stats.rationale: PACKAGE_USAGE_STATS is granted in Settings. BRAKE polls queryEvents for ACTIVITY_RESUMED (API 29+) on user-chosen packages. It cannot show interstitials (BAL restricted since Android 10), so it posts a notification. Near-real-time detection needs a continuously running foreground service: WorkManager's minimum interval is 15 min, and no FGS type fits app monitoring, so it must be specialUse, reviewed in the Play Console. Fallback if Play refuses: read usage only when BRAKE opens and show retrospective context.
android-usage-stats.typical_latency: seconds with a specialUse foreground service; >=15 min without one (WorkManager)
android-usage-stats.access_requirements: User grants Usage access in Settings (Settings.ACTION_USAGE_ACCESS_SETTINGS); FOREGROUND_SERVICE_SPECIAL_USE + PROPERTY_SPECIAL_USE_FGS_SUBTYPE; POST_NOTIFICATIONS
android-usage-stats.policy_constraints: Avoid QUERY_ALL_PACKAGES (Play policy). FGS types must be declared in the Play Console (Policy > App content) for apps targeting Android 14+, and the specialUse justification is reviewed. Any separate Play declaration for usage access is unverified.

android-accessibility-service.name: AccessibilityService (screen content / window events)
android-accessibility-service.rationale: Technically the strongest IN-SPEND sensor: it can read checkout and UPI screens. Using it for a non-accessibility purpose conflicts with Play's Accessibility API policy and with the brief's ban on invasive surveillance. It hits restricted settings for sideloads and looks like banking malware.
android-accessibility-service.access_requirements: BIND_ACCESSIBILITY_SERVICE service with user enablement. Non-accessibility tools need prominent disclosure and a Play declaration (unverified 2026 text). isAccessibilityTool (API 31) is only for tools that serve users with disabilities.
android-accessibility-service.policy_constraints: Play Accessibility API policy, Android 13+ restricted settings, and possible Android 16 Advanced Protection mitigations (unverified).

android-accessibility-service.name: Android AccessibilityService-based shopping/checkout interception
android-accessibility-service.rationale: Technically strongest Android in-flow signal (reads any app's screen) but maximally invasive and policy-risky; non-accessibility tools trigger a system privacy notification; contradicts BRAKE privacy principle.

android-accessibility-service.name: Android AccessibilityService screen reading
android-accessibility-service.rationale: Play restricts the Accessibility API to genuine accessibility tools (unverified). It reads everything on screen, including banking screens and passwords, and has a stalkerware-like abuse profile.

android-overlay-window.name: SYSTEM_ALERT_WINDOW overlays
android-overlay-window.rationale:
Only an intervention surface, and a fragile one:
- Android 12 blocks untrusted touches.
- Payment apps can hide overlays with setHideOverlayWindows.
- Android 15 narrowed the overlay FGS exemption, and Android 17 hardens background activity launch further.
It also reads as a dark pattern. Use a user-started Live Update timer instead.
android-overlay-window.access_requirements: SYSTEM_ALERT_WINDOW granted via Settings.ACTION_MANAGE_OVERLAY_PERMISSION ('Very few apps should use this permission').
android-overlay-window.policy_constraints: Android 12 untrusted-touch blocking; Android 15 requires a visible overlay for background FGS start; Android 17 BAL hardening.

android-share-intent.name: Android share target (ACTION_SEND / SEND_MULTIPLE, Direct Share)
android-share-intent.rationale: User-initiated, permission-free capture of a product being considered (URL, title, price, screenshot) and of receipts after purchase. Works in every country.
android-share-intent.access_requirements: Activity intent filter for android.intent.action.SEND with text/plain and image/* MIME types; no permission

android-process-text.name: Text-selection action (ACTION_PROCESS_TEXT)
android-process-text.rationale: Adds 'Ask BRAKE' to the text-selection toolbar of any app at near-zero cost. Explicit, minimal data.
android-process-text.access_requirements: Activity filtering android.intent.action.PROCESS_TEXT (text/plain); API 23+; no permission

android-clipboard.name: Clipboard (explicit paste only)
android-clipboard.rationale: Offer 'Paste copied link' when the user is already in BRAKE. getPrimaryClipDescription shows no toast; the content is read only on tap. Background reading is impossible since Android 10 and Android 12+ shows an access toast.
android-clipboard.access_requirements: BRAKE must be the focused app (or the IME). No permission.
android-clipboard.policy_constraints: Android 10 focus restriction; Android 12 'APP pasted from your clipboard' toast; Android 13 EXTRA_IS_SENSITIVE on source clips.

android-app-widget.name: Home-screen App Widget
android-app-widget.rationale: Low-cost entry point ('Ask before I buy') and glance or label surface (pace, last transaction). RemoteViews have no EditText, so price entry opens an activity.
android-app-widget.typical_latency: Immediate on tap; content updates batched by the system
android-app-widget.policy_constraints: None specific; Android 17 widget memory limit for apps targeting it

android-quick-settings-tile.name: Quick Settings tile (TileService)
android-quick-settings-tile.rationale: One-swipe 'Should I buy this?' or 'Start a pause' entry point. Android 13+ requestAddTileService lowers the setup friction.
android-quick-settings-tile.access_requirements: TileService with BIND_QUICK_SETTINGS_TILE; StatusBarManager.requestAddTileService on Android 13+
android-quick-settings-tile.policy_constraints: System may stop showing the add prompt after repeated denials

android-notification-actions.name: Notification action buttons + RemoteInput (one-tap labelling)
android-notification-actions.rationale: BRAKE's main Android labelling input. It offers 3 action buttons (MAX_ACTION_BUTTONS = 3; docs: 'up to three action buttons'), plus app-supplied RemoteInput choice chips (AOSP SystemUI; precedence over NAS suggestions for apps targeting P+) and free-text direct reply (Android 7.0+). Each tap is a UserAssertion. Notifications are bridged to Wear OS by default; whether actions and choices work on the watch is unverified.
android-notification-actions.policy_constraints: Android 12 notification-trampoline restriction for apps targeting 31+ (label via a BroadcastReceiver with no UI; open UI via an activity PendingIntent). Chip rendering on OEM skins unverified.

rcs-business-messaging.name: RCS business messages (bank/merchant alerts over RCS)
rcs-business-messaging.rationale: There is no public API for third-party apps to read RCS. The only path is NLS on the messaging app's notification. RCS alerts are likely invisible to READ_SMS (unverified), which makes NLS the more future-proof route.

rcs-business-messaging.name: RCS Business Messaging (RBM) bank and merchant messages
rcs-business-messaging.rationale: Indian bank alerts are appearing over RCS. SBI Card and PNB RCS parsers exist, and a PennyWise PR merged 2026-05-29 says Kotak migrated alerts to RCS, though that rests on a single report and the scope is unverified. Saudi STC Bank RCS alerts are also parsed. There is no public read API. The planned capture is the notification listener (unproven for RCS content; prototype first). The only shipped route in the cited sources is the undocumented READ_SMS + content://mms route. The RBM agent id would be a strong sender identity, but notifications expose only a display name. Styled Unicode requires NFKC.
data_fields: RBM agent id (only via undocumented MMS route)
dedup_keys: UPI RRN and other alert keys
body hash vs any SMS fallback copy
rcs-business-messaging.access_requirements: Notification listener (supported API; RCS content unverified); no Android RCS content API.
rcs-business-messaging.policy_constraints: RBM agent verification and carrier launch rules unverified; RBM delivery to iOS unverified.

android-live-updates.name: Live Updates (promoted ongoing notifications) for a user-started cooling-off timer
android-live-updates.rationale: Possible compliant intervention surface for a user-initiated 'wait 10 minutes' countdown. Usage criteria require activities that are ongoing, user-initiated and time-sensitive. Ads/promotions, chat messages, alerts, upcoming calendar events and quick access to app features are listed as inappropriate, so a budget meter or post-spend alert does not qualify. OEMs can add criteria.
android-live-updates.access_requirements: Android 16+; POST_PROMOTED_NOTIFICATIONS (added API 36.1, normal|appops) in addition to POST_NOTIFICATIONS; setRequestPromotedOngoing / EXTRA_REQUEST_PROMOTED_ONGOING; ongoing (FLAG_ONGOING_EVENT); content title; no custom content view; not a group summary; not colorized; channel not IMPORTANCE_MIN; Standard, BigText, Call, Progress or Metric style
android-live-updates.policy_constraints: Live Update usage criteria; OEM criteria

android-appfunctions.name: AppFunctions / App Actions (Gemini and assistant integration)
android-appfunctions.rationale: AppFunctions (Android 16+) lets allowlisted agents and assistants call app tools such as checkPurchase or logPurchase. Gemini integration was in private preview with trusted testers as of May 2026 (page updated 2026-09-22), and the API is experimental. App Actions/BIIs are still documented as a current feature with no deprecation notice (2026-07-16). Whether Gemini fulfils BIIs is unverified.
android-appfunctions.access_requirements: Android 16+; AppFunctions Jetpack library; callers need EXECUTE_APP_FUNCTIONS (protection level normal) and pass runtime allowlist checks; Gemini integration is in private preview (Early Access Program)
android-appfunctions.policy_constraints: Experimental API subject to change; minimise data returned to agents

upi-intent-url.name: upi:// intent handling (BRAKE as chooser target that forwards to the user's UPI app)
upi-intent-url.rationale: Technically feasible: declare an intent filter for scheme upi, appear in the chooser, read payee, amount and tr before payment, then hand off to the user's UPI app with startActivityForResult, preferably via a freshly built explicit intent containing only validated parameters. It interposes BRAKE in a regulated payment flow, changes the caller the PSP sees, only works for implicit intents, and risks default-handler hijack. Needs NPCI/legal review; prefer BRAKE's own QR scanner and post-spend NLS.
upi-intent-url.access_requirements: Intent filter <data android:scheme="upi"/>; <queries> for scheme upi to list UPI apps (Android 11+); callers that use startActivityForResult are automatically visible; no permission
upi-intent-url.policy_constraints: Android 16 intent-redirection hardening (all apps on Android 16) targets launching untrusted sub-level intents taken from extras. Its effect on forwarding the received top-level upi:// intent is not documented (unverified), so build a fresh intent as good practice. NPCI/PSP rules for intermediating apps are unknown. Parameters follow the NPCI UPI Linking Specification (not re-verified; npci.org.in blocked).
data_fields: result extras (txnId, responseCode, Status, txnRef; unverified)

upi-intent-url.name: UPI deep-link/intent URL handler (Android upi:// intent filter with forward/relay)
upi-intent-url.rationale: A true in-spend moment before PIN entry. But it puts BRAKE inside a regulated payment flow and requires byte-exact forwarding and result relay. User defaults and explicit-package SDKs bypass it, and there is no iOS equivalent. NPCI OC-73 (2019) says UPI apps should answer merchant intents only when the user is registered with a UPI PIN in that app, to avoid chooser clutter and timeouts. A non-UPI app in the chooser goes against that intent, even though the rule binds members, not BRAKE. OC-76A/76C disallow P2P intents and intents to offline non-verified merchants, so BRAKE would see only verified/online P2M intents.
data_fields: result: txnId, responseCode, ApprovalRefNo, Status, txnRef
upi-intent-url.access_requirements: Manifest intent filter (scheme upi). Explicit opt-in. Likely needs comfort from NPCI or a partner PSP.
upi-intent-url.policy_constraints: Android disambiguation dialog/defaults; Android 11 package visibility; NPCI OC-73 (only registered UPI apps should respond to intents); OC-76A/76C (no P2P or offline non-verified intents); possible Play deceptive-behaviour review (unverified). Must never modify the payload or block payment.

upi-intent-url.name: UPI intent URLs (upi://pay) received before payment
upi-intent-url.rationale: Valuable pre-spend signal, but whether a non-PSP app may register for and forward upi:// intents to a PSP app without NPCI/TPAP standing is unverified. BRAKE must never initiate or alter payment instructions.
upi-intent-url.policy_constraints: Payee VPA and name of P2P payees are third-party personal data; hash them for storage.

upi-intent-url.name: BRAKE QR front-door handing off via upi://pay intent
upi-intent-url.rationale: Prior-art PFMs became full UPI TPAPs (CRED, Jupiter, Fi; unverified) to own the payment moment, which is heavyweight. A scan-then-hand-off pattern gives BRAKE pre/in-spend timing with user-chosen routing, but PSP-app handling of third-party intents needs verification.

android-digital-wellbeing.name: Digital Wellbeing / screen-time controls
android-digital-wellbeing.rationale: No third-party API for Digital Wellbeing timers or focus mode, and no equivalent of iOS FamilyControls/ManagedSettings shielding. Only UsageStatsManager and Settings.ACTION_APP_USAGE_SETTINGS exist. queryAppUsageDuration is internal|role.

android-private-space.name: Android 15+ private space (platform constraint)
android-private-space.rationale: Not a source but a degradation factor. Private-space apps are stopped while the space is locked and post no notifications. Main-profile listeners appear to receive their notifications while it is unlocked (inferred from AOSP, unverified on device). Apps cannot tell whether they run in private space.
android-private-space.access_requirements: n/a (ACCESS_HIDDEN_PROFILES is for default launchers only)

wear-os-surfaces.name: Wear OS (bridged notifications, Tiles/complications)
wear-os-surfaces.rationale: Phone notifications, including BRAKE's labelling notifications, are bridged to paired watches by default (verified 2026-10-04). Whether action buttons and RemoteInput choices are usable on the watch is not stated on the bridging page (unverified). A dedicated watch app (Tile showing discretionary budget left) adds a glanceable surface but no new financial signal.
wear-os-surfaces.access_requirements: None for bridging (can be controlled with setBridgeTag/BridgingManager); a Wear OS app for Tiles/complications

android-default-sms-role.name: Default SMS handler role (ROLE_SMS)
android-default-sms-role.rationale: Would give full SMS access and exempt BRAKE from the Android 17 OTP delay, but BRAKE would have to become the user's complete SMS client (able to send messages), which is out of scope and hurts trust.
android-default-sms-role.access_requirements: User selects BRAKE as default SMS app; must ask for the role before requesting SMS permissions
android-default-sms-role.policy_constraints: Play default-handler requirements (core functionality, privacy policy)

android-companion-device-association.name: CompanionDeviceManager association (trusted-listener status)
android-companion-device-association.rationale: A CDM association makes an NLS 'trusted', which exempts it from OTP redaction and from the SMS OTP delay. It is intended for genuine companion devices, so using it to get around redaction would be policy abuse.
android-companion-device-association.policy_constraints: Misuse would violate platform intent and likely Play policy

android-autofill-service.name: AutofillService (AssistStructure of other apps' checkout screens)
android-autofill-service.rationale: Missed by the original stream. An autofill service receives the view hierarchy of the focused app via onFillRequest(), which on checkout screens could expose amounts and card fields. However, the developer guide states 'Autofill services must not use information for purposes other than providing suggestions'. Users normally run their password manager as the single autofill service (unverified), and using it as a sensor is the screen-surveillance pattern the brief rules out.
android-autofill-service.access_requirements: Service with BIND_AUTOFILL_SERVICE; user selects it in system settings (Settings.ACTION_REQUEST_SET_AUTOFILL_SERVICE)
android-autofill-service.policy_constraints: Developer guide forbids non-suggestion use; Play user-data and deceptive-behaviour policies (unverified detail)
data_fields: AssistStructure view nodes (not to be used)

android-autofill-service.name: Android AutofillService as a checkout-field detector
android-autofill-service.rationale: A user-enabled AutofillService (API 26+) receives a ViewStructure of all views on screen when the user focuses an editable field in any app, including autofill hints such as card fields and web domains. A compatibility mode for browsers falls back to accessibility APIs. That gives a precise in-spend trigger, but it would displace the user's password manager (single provider; unverified on 2026 builds), sees the whole screen, and repurposes a filling API for monitoring (Play policy risk; unverified).
android-autofill-service.access_requirements: BIND_AUTOFILL_SERVICE; user selects BRAKE as the autofill service in Settings (Settings.ACTION_REQUEST_SET_AUTOFILL_SERVICE)
android-autofill-service.policy_constraints: Google Play policy on autofill/accessibility misuse (2026 text unverified); contradicts BRAKE's minimum-collection principle

android-screenshot-detection.name: Screenshot detection API (Android 14+)
android-screenshot-detection.rationale: Missed by the original stream; relevant to the brief's 'screenshot detection initiated by user'. Activity.registerScreenCaptureCallback() fires only when the user screenshots while the app's own activity is visible, and the callback does not provide the image. BRAKE cannot detect screenshots taken in shopping or payment apps; use the share target for user-shared screenshots instead.

ios-shortcuts-wallet-transaction-trigger.name: Shortcuts personal automation - Wallet 'Transaction' trigger feeding a BRAKE App Intent
ios-shortcuts-wallet-transaction-trigger.rationale: The only zero-entitlement near-real-time spend signal on iPhone; enables immediate post-tap insight and labeling. Offered as an opt-in beta because it needs manual setup, covers Apple Pay taps only, and has documented timeout, empty-field and declined-fire failure modes (forums, Oct 2024 to Feb 2026). Apple Watch payment coverage is unverified.
ios-shortcuts-wallet-transaction-trigger.access_requirements: No entitlement. The user creates the automation by hand in Shortcuts (choose cards, add BRAKE action, enable Run Immediately). Requires Apple Pay and a real device (not testable in Simulator). The BRAKE intent uses supportedModes = .background (iOS 26) with a ~30 s budget.
data_fields: amount (type unverified; Double in forum example)
dedup_keys: match to FinanceKit Transaction.id/accountID/transactionAmount/merchantName/transactionDate (US: Apple Card/Apple Cash only; UK: FinanceKit-connected bank cards)
ios-shortcuts-wallet-transaction-trigger.policy_constraints: The user-built automation is the consent; BRAKE cannot create or detect automations. Never treat as confirmed (it fires on declines).
ios-shortcuts-wallet-transaction-trigger.typical_latency: seconds after tap; times out if issuer data reaches Wallet late (reports of 3+ hours)

ios-shortcuts-wallet-transaction-trigger.name: iOS Shortcuts Wallet 'Transaction' personal automation (Apple Pay tap → App Intent)
ios-shortcuts-wallet-transaction-trigger.rationale: Missed by this stream; owned by the iOS stream (doc 04). Reportedly (iOS 17+) runs a user-built automation 'When I tap' a Wallet card, passing card, merchant and amount to an App Intent. That would give Apple Pay in-store taps an immediate signal in any country, without FinanceKit or an aggregator. Unverified this session (support.apple.com blocked; doc 04 relied on search snippets). Coverage for online/in-app Apple Pay and the availability of a transaction ID are unknown.
ios-shortcuts-wallet-transaction-trigger.access_requirements: User creates the personal automation in Shortcuts; BRAKE exposes an App Intent

ios-shortcuts-app-open-trigger.name: Shortcuts personal automation - 'App is Opened/Closed' trigger for launch friction
ios-shortcuts-app-open-trigger.rationale: No-entitlement launch friction for shopping apps (the one sec pattern). Given the DPLA 3.3.3(P) primary-purpose clause, Family Controls may never be granted to a spending app, so this may be BRAKE's long-term iOS launch-friction path, not just a stopgap. It is fragile and setup-heavy: the iOS 26.6 regression (FB24505842, Aug 2026) fires 'When App Is Closed' when Control Center or Notification Center opens.
ios-shortcuts-app-open-trigger.access_requirements: No entitlement; the user creates one automation per app; the BRAKE intent must support a foreground mode (e.g., .foreground(.immediate)).
ios-shortcuts-app-open-trigger.policy_constraints: Implement a pass-through window to avoid loops; avoid scolding copy.

ios-screen-time-shields.name: Screen Time API shields: FamilyControls + ManagedSettings + ShieldConfiguration/ShieldAction extensions
ios-screen-time-shields.rationale: Technically the strongest, most privacy-preserving pre-spend friction on any platform. Users pick apps/sites/categories via opaque tokens; shield text is customizable (budget context from App Group); a 3-item submenu arrives in iOS 26.4; openParentalControlsApp hand-off to BRAKE arrives in iOS 26.5. However, the DPLA (Aug 18, 2026) requires an app using Family Controls to have a PRIMARY PURPOSE of family controls or individual device/focus management, and BRAKE's primary purpose is spending decisions. Eligibility must be confirmed with App Review (30-min consultation) before treating this as MVP. There is also a 2026 entitlement backlog and forum-reported reliability bugs.
ios-screen-time-shields.access_requirements: com.apple.developer.family-controls distribution entitlement requested by the Account Holder (team-scoped per DTS Apr 2026; docs still mention per-extension requests); iOS 16+ individual authorization with Face ID/Touch ID; secondaryButtonSubmenuItems needs iOS 26.4+; openParentalControlsApp needs iOS 26.5+.
data_fields: shield extension sees display names, bundle IDs, domains (sandboxed, no network)
