ios-screen-time-shields.policy_constraints: DPLA 3.3.3(P) (Aug 2026): primary-purpose requirement (family controls, or individual focus/productivity/personal device usage management); data only for family controls or individual device management; no sharing beyond the individual and their device; no advertising or data brokers (no explicit off-device clause; keep device-local as the conservative reading). Guideline 4.10: Screen Time APIs not monetizable. Guideline 2.5.1: intended purpose; private APIs (LSApplicationWorkspace) rejected May 2026.

ios-deviceactivity-monitor.name: Screen Time API DeviceActivity monitor (schedules and usage thresholds)
ios-deviceactivity-monitor.rationale: Enables context-aware friction (e.g., long late-night shopping-app sessions). It is purpose-limited and gated on the same Family Controls eligibility as shields. Forum reports describe extension wake failures and a possible iOS 26.2 threshold regression (FB21267341).
ios-deviceactivity-monitor.access_requirements: Same Family Controls entitlement and DPLA primary-purpose eligibility; extension point com.apple.deviceactivity.monitor-extension (ITMS-90349 otherwise).
ios-deviceactivity-monitor.policy_constraints: DPLA 3.3.3(P) (Aug 2026): use only for individual device management; no sharing beyond the individual and their device; keep device-local.
ios-deviceactivity-monitor.typical_latency: minutes (threshold granularity); callbacks only while device in use

ios-deviceactivity-report.name: Screen Time API DeviceActivityReport extension (display-only usage reports)
ios-deviceactivity-report.rationale: Can only render usage inside BRAKE UI; sandbox prevents network and moving data out of the extension, so it cannot feed fusion.
data_fields: rendered app/category/web-domain activity (not readable by app logic)

ios-familyactivitydata-eu.name: EU-only non-tokenized app/website usage (approvedWithDataAccess, FamilyActivityData)
ios-familyactivitydata-eu.rationale: Gives real bundle IDs/domains/usage but only on EU devices with EU accounts, only one app per device, and reportedly displaces Apple's own Screen Time; disproportionate for a spending coach when tokens suffice.
ios-familyactivitydata-eu.access_requirements: com.apple.developer.family-controls.app-and-website-usage entitlement, iOS/iPadOS 26.4+, EU location + EU Apple Account.
ios-familyactivitydata-eu.policy_constraints: Exclusive per device; DPLA 3.3.3(P) still applies.

ios-app-intents-siri-spotlight.name: App Intents / App Shortcuts via Siri, Spotlight, Shortcuts, interactive snippets
ios-app-intents-siri-spotlight.rationale: Cheap, global, user-initiated 'Should I buy this?' and manual logging entry points; automatically surfaced in Siri/Spotlight/Shortcuts; no finance schema domain exists so BRAKE must rely on its own App Shortcut phrases.
dedup_keys: user-entered; link to later candidate by amount+merchant+time
ios-app-intents-siri-spotlight.policy_constraints: Apple may extract anonymized App Shortcuts phrases; avoid indexing sensitive amounts in Spotlight.

ios-controls-action-button.name: WidgetKit Controls in Control Center, Lock Screen and Action button
ios-controls-action-button.rationale: Thin wrapper over BRAKE intents making 'Ask BRAKE' or 'Shopping mode' one press; can start a Live Activity from background via LiveActivityIntent.
ios-controls-action-button.access_requirements: iOS 18+; Action button only on newer iPhones (model list unverified).

ios-interactive-widgets.name: Interactive Home/Lock Screen widgets (Button/Toggle with App Intents)
ios-interactive-widgets.rationale: Glanceable budget context and quick-amount checks; no text input and inactive on locked devices; visible surfaces require non-numeric defaults.
ios-interactive-widgets.policy_constraints: Guideline 2.5.16 widgets must relate to app content.

ios-live-activities.name: Live Activities and Dynamic Island (shopping session / cooling-off timer)
ios-live-activities.rationale: Behaviourally promising in-spend companion but constrained (8 h + 4 h, 4 KB, no network/location, push budgets) and Lock Screen visibility conflicts with financial privacy.
ios-live-activities.access_requirements: NSSupportsLiveActivities; foreground start or LiveActivityIntent; push-to-start on iOS 17.2+ (inferred).
ios-live-activities.policy_constraints: HIG: no ads, avoid sensitive info; Guideline 4.5.3 no spam via Live Activities.
ios-live-activities.typical_latency: push/app update; up to 8 h active

ios-share-extension.name: Share extension (share product URL / text / screenshot to BRAKE)
ios-share-extension.rationale: Canonical 'share product to BRAKE' pre-spend path; works from any app using the share sheet; strictly user-initiated.
dedup_keys: canonicalized product URL / merchant domain + product id
ios-share-extension.policy_constraints: Strip tracking params; Guideline 4.4 no ads/IAP in extensions.

safari-web-extension-ios.name: Safari Web Extension on iOS (product and checkout page context)
safari-web-extension-ios.rationale: True in-spend web checkout signal (cart total, items, order id) with per-site consent, but Safari-only reach and per-merchant DOM maintenance.
safari-web-extension-ios.access_requirements: iOS 15+; user enables extension and grants per-site Ask/Allow/Deny; prefer activeTab/narrow host_permissions.
safari-web-extension-ios.policy_constraints: Guideline 4.4.2; never ship page contents off-device by default.

ios-notification-actions.name: Actionable notifications for one-tap labeling and regret check-ins
ios-notification-actions.rationale: Implements the brief's one-tap labeling: up to 4 buttons expanded, first 2 in banners, text-input action for Other; actions launch app in background.
ios-notification-actions.access_requirements: Notification permission; passive/active interruption levels (no time-sensitive for labeling).
ios-notification-actions.policy_constraints: Guideline 4.5.4: no sensitive info in pushes; prefer local notifications or E2EE.

ios-notification-content-extension.name: Notification Content Extension (interactive custom notification UI)
ios-notification-content-extension.rationale: Allows richer label grids/satisfaction scales in expanded notifications (interactive since iOS 12) beyond the 4-button limit.
ios-notification-content-extension.access_requirements: UNNotificationExtensionUserInteractionEnabled; payload/App Group data only; no network/long tasks.

ios-notification-service-extension.name: Notification Service Extension for BRAKE's own (E2EE) pushes, optionally with notification filtering
ios-notification-service-extension.rationale: Infrastructure to relay server-side aggregator observations as end-to-end-encrypted pushes that are decrypted and fused on the device. With the managed usernotifications.filtering entitlement the NSE can silence pushes that carry no meaningful insight, which fits the brief's 'say nothing'. It cannot read other apps' notifications.
ios-notification-service-extension.access_requirements: Remote notifications with an alert and mutable-content: 1; limited execution time. Optional managed entitlement com.apple.developer.usernotifications.filtering (iOS 13.3+, apply to Apple; approval criteria unverified).
dedup_keys: upstream source ids carried in payload (e.g., aggregator transaction_id)
ios-notification-service-extension.policy_constraints: Guideline 4.5.4 (no sensitive personal info in pushes); transmit-minimum principle.

ios-message-filter-extension.name: SMS/MMS Message Filter extension (ILMessageFilterExtension, IdentityLookup)
ios-message-filter-extension.rationale: Sees only unknown-sender SMS/MMS, cannot write to shared containers or access the network directly; the only egress is a system POST of sender+text to the developer server, and Guideline 2.5.12 forbids using filter data for other purposes. Not a legitimate transaction feed.
ios-message-filter-extension.access_requirements: User enables BRAKE as the (single) SMS filter in Settings; Associated Domains for network deferral.
ios-message-filter-extension.policy_constraints: Guideline 2.5.12 purpose limitation; 2.5.1 intended purpose; violates BRAKE local-first principle.

ios-message-filter-extension.name: iOS IdentityLookup Message Filter extension
ios-message-filter-extension.rationale: Sees only SMS/MMS from unknown senders, cannot access the network directly and cannot write to shared containers. Using server deferral to collect bank SMS would repurpose a spam-filter API and risk App Review violations (5.1.1/5.1.2). At most, a later option to tidy the user's Messages folders, with no data to BRAKE.

ios-message-filter-extension.name: iOS ILMessageFilterExtension (SMS filtering)
ios-message-filter-extension.rationale: Apple's purpose for this API is identifying and filtering unwanted SMS. Repurposing it to harvest transaction data conflicts with App Review 5.1.2(ii) purpose limitation (verified) and likely with the extension's sandboxing (unverified).
ios-message-filter-extension.access_requirements: Message Filter app extension; server deferral needs Associated Domains with the messagefilter service.
ios-message-filter-extension.policy_constraints: Filtering-only purpose; it only sees unknown senders (unverified).

ios-telephonymessagingkit-eu.name: TelephonyMessagingKit (EU default carrier messaging app)
ios-telephonymessagingkit-eu.rationale: Usable only if BRAKE becomes the user's default SMS/MMS/RCS app in the EU, which means shipping a full messaging client.
ios-telephonymessagingkit-eu.access_requirements: com.apple.developer.carrier-messaging-app entitlement; iOS 26+; iPhone only; EU account and device located in the EU; the user selects the app as the default carrier messaging app.
data_fields: SMS/MMS/RCS messages and history in the default app
ios-telephonymessagingkit-eu.policy_constraints: DPLA 3.3.7(H) (Aug 2026): must offer user-initiated sending and viewing of received messages; store and transmit messages securely (encrypted in transit and at rest if synced); no unsolicited messages, phishing or spam.

ios-clipboard-paste.name: Clipboard via UIPasteControl and pattern/value detection
ios-clipboard-paste.rationale: Prompt-free, user-tapped paste of product links and prices in the manual check flow. detectPatterns can check for URLs without notifying the user.
ios-clipboard-paste.access_requirements: iOS 16+ for UIPasteControl; iOS 14+ for DetectionPattern; iOS 15+ for DetectedValues.
data_fields: DetectedValues (moneyAmounts, links, shipmentTrackingNumbers; notification behaviour unverified)

ios-visionkit-data-scanner.name: VisionKit DataScannerViewController (price tags, barcodes, QR)
ios-visionkit-data-scanner.rationale: Live currency-typed text and barcode/QR capture for in-store price checks and payment-QR capture (QR parsing is owned by the QR/UPI stream).
ios-visionkit-data-scanner.access_requirements: iOS 16+, A12 Bionic or later, camera permission (NSCameraUsageDescription).
ios-visionkit-data-scanner.policy_constraints: Guideline 5.1.2(vi) bans marketing/ad use of data from depth/facial-mapping tools incl. Camera/Photo APIs; applying it to OCR is conservative. Product lookups leak purchase interest; prefer local lookup.

ios-vision-document-ocr.name: Vision RecognizeDocumentsRequest / text recognition for receipts
ios-vision-document-ocr.rationale: On-device receipt structure (tables/lists/barcodes, iOS 26) yields item-level semantics without email access; basic OCR available on older iOS.
ios-vision-document-ocr.access_requirements: iOS 26+ for RecognizeDocumentsRequest; camera/photos access via picker.
ios-vision-document-ocr.policy_constraints: Process locally; retain extracted facts not images.

ios-visual-intelligence.name: Visual Intelligence integration via IntentValueQuery (camera/screenshot search)
ios-visual-intelligence.rationale: Novel user-initiated screenshot/camera entry point (labels + pixelBuffer) but search-oriented, one-query limit, Apple Intelligence device gating; share extension covers most value.

ios-visual-intelligence.name: iOS visual intelligence app integration
ios-visual-intelligence.rationale: IntentValueQuery receives SemanticContentDescriptor (generic en_US labels + pixelBuffer) from camera or screenshot to return app content; designed for content search, labels too generic to price; review fit unclear.

ios-foundation-models.name: Foundation Models framework (on-device LLM) as local processing capability
ios-foundation-models.rationale: Enables on-device merchant normalization, categorization and text/OCR extraction with @Generable structs, avoiding third-party AI disclosure; gated by Apple Intelligence device/region and model-version drift.
ios-foundation-models.access_requirements: iOS 26+, Apple Intelligence-enabled device and region; model availability checks.
data_fields: n/a (processing): structured outputs mirroring TransactionCandidate fields
ios-foundation-models.policy_constraints: Guideline 5.1.2(i) applies if falling back to server/third-party LLMs.

ios-background-tasks.name: iOS background execution limits (BGTaskScheduler, background push, intent runtime)
ios-background-tasks.rationale: Design constraint: ~30 s windows, throttled silent pushes, no persistent services; adapters must be short event handlers writing to an App Group store.

ios-nfc-hce-eea.name: Core NFC host card emulation (CardSession), EEA only
ios-nfc-hce-eea.rationale: EEA-only HCE behind managed entitlements for in-store payments, car keys, closed-loop transit, corporate badges, hotel keys, loyalty and event tickets. A possible future partner route, not a BRAKE sensor.
ios-nfc-hce-eea.access_requirements: com.apple.developer.nfc.hce (+ iso7816.select-identifier-prefixes; optional default-contactless-app) via Apple's application process; iOS 17.4+; EEA.
data_fields: APDUs for the app's own credential

ios-location-monitoring.name: Core Location region monitoring for store/mall arrival context
ios-location-monitoring.rationale: Potential pre-spend context but invasive; only as user-defined places processed on-device; details not re-verified this session.
ios-location-monitoring.access_requirements: Location permission (Always for background events; unverified details).
ios-location-monitoring.policy_constraints: Brief: avoid invasive surveillance; Guideline 5.1.1(iv) alternatives if declined.

qr-scan.name: BRAKE in-app QR scanner (UPI URI + EMVCo MPM + share/gallery image)
qr-scan.rationale: The only rail-level signal that reliably precedes authorisation on both OSs. The user starts it and parsing happens on device. One parser plus a GUID profile registry covers most QR-payment markets; it must scan MAI 26-51 and templates 80-99 (Pix Automatico uses tag 80). In India the scan is a pre-spend observation, but a seamless hand-off is not guaranteed: forwarding the URI as an intent is disallowed for P2P and offline non-verified merchants (NPCI OC-76A/76C), and paying from a shared image (QR share & Pay) is capped at Rs 2,000 for those payees. The default UX is therefore 'check with BRAKE, then scan in your UPI app'. Completion stays unknown until a post-spend signal matches.
qr-scan.access_requirements: None for parsing. Camera permission. BRAKE must never generate or modify payment payloads.
qr-scan.policy_constraints: Android: ACTION_VIEW with the original URI only for verified/online merchants (intent modes 04/05 disallowed for P2P and offline non-verified merchants, OC-76A/76C); otherwise send the user to rescan in their UPI app. QR share & Pay <= Rs 2,000 for P2P and non-verified offline P2M, and not allowed for UPI Global P2M. iOS: open() of an app-specific scheme is unconstrained; only canOpenURL detection needs LSApplicationQueriesSchemes (max 50; 25 for apps linked on iOS 27+). Signed payloads must not be modified.

upi-qr.name: UPI QR (upi://pay URI; static, dynamic, signed)
upi-qr.rationale: Dominant retail payment trigger in India. Dynamic QRs carry the amount and tr. Signed QRs (UPI 2.0, launched 16 Aug 2018: 'Signed Intent & QR'; mode 02 with sign + orgid) mark verified merchants. Readable only when scanned with BRAKE. Hand-off back to the PSP is constrained by NPCI initiation-mode rules (OC-76A/76C).
upi-qr.access_requirements: None to read. Banks were required to enable dynamic QR generate/read by 20 Dec 2016 (NPCI Circular 11).
upi-qr.policy_constraints: Do not alter signed payloads. Never auto-open the url param. Re-launching a scanned QR as an intent (mode 04/05) is disallowed for P2P payees and offline non-verified merchants (OC-76A/76C). QR share & Pay is capped at Rs 2,000 for P2P and non-verified offline P2M.

bharat-qr.name: Bharat QR (EMV MPM with card and UPI templates)
bharat-qr.rationale: Interoperable card+UPI QR: tags 02 Visa, 04 Mastercard, 06 RuPay, 08 IFSC/account, 26 UPI VPA, 27 tr/url, 28 Aadhaar. Parsed by the generic EMV parser.

emvco-mpm-qr.name: EMVCo Merchant-Presented Mode QR (generic TLV parser)
emvco-mpm-qr.rationale: A single well-specified format underlies most national QR schemes. A CRC catches corruption (but not sticker swaps). Unknown GUIDs degrade gracefully to name/city/country.

upi-counterparty-classification.name: UPI / EMV QR P2P vs P2M vs P2PM inference from payload and alerts
upi-counterparty-classification.rationale: Feeds transfer-vs-spend directly. UPI signals: mc (MCC 7407 = P2PM per Circular 70/OC-181), sign/orgid (verified merchant), tr and dynamic amount. P2P collect has been banned since 1 Oct 2025 (OC-220, 29 Jul 2025) and P2P intents are disallowed (OC-76A/76C), so collect and intent payments are P2M by construction. OC-101A (P2P/P2PM only) means the app shows the banking name, which may differ from the QR pn. EMV profiles: QR Ph com.p2pqrpay (tag 27) vs ph.ppmi.p2m (tag 28) [secondary]; VietQR QRPUSH vs QRIBFTTA/QRIBFTTC.

pix-br-code.name: Pix BR Code (QR and copia e cola)
pix-br-code.rationale: EMV profile with GUI br.gov.bcb.pix (26.01 key, 26.02 info, 26.25 location URL) and txid in 62.05 ('***' static). Cheap to add on top of the EMV parser. The dynamic amount may sit behind a location URL that should not be fetched by default.

pix-automatico.name: Pix Automatico (recurring Pix authorisations)
pix-automatico.rationale: The BCB Pix API (Automatico tags since 2.7.0-RC1; current 2.10.0) defines Rec/SolicRec/CobR/LocRec and rec.dadosQR (pixCopiaECola <=512 chars, jornada). BCB examples carry the recurrence in a BR Code tag 80 template (00=br.gov.bcb.pix, 25=.../qr/v2/rec/<id>), so BRAKE can detect a subscription sign-up offline. The amount and periodicity (SEMANAL/MENSAL/TRIMESTRAL/SEMESTRAL/ANUAL) sit behind the /rec/ location and are not in the payload. Journeys: JORNADA_1 (external notification, no QR), _2 (recurrence QR), _3 (composite QR + immediate charge), _4 (composite QR with due-date/static contract). Field-test against real QRs before promoting.

pix-nfc.name: Pix por aproximacao (NFC Pix)
pix-nfc.rationale: No payload is visible to third-party apps, so only post-spend bank notifications or Open Finance data apply. Launch details unverified.

sgqr-paynow.name: SGQR / PayNow QR
sgqr-paynow.rationale: EMV profile: tag 26 GUID SG.PAYNOW; 01 proxy type (0 mobile/2 UEN), 02 proxy value, 03 editable. SGQR spec v1.7. Profile row plus tests.

promptpay-qr.name: PromptPay / Thai QR
promptpay-qr.rationale: Tag 29 GUID A000000677010111 with mobile (01), tax/national ID (02) or e-wallet (03). Currency 764. A P2P proxy is often a national ID, so hash it.

duitnow-qr.name: DuitNow QR
duitnow-qr.rationale: Tag 26 GUID A0000006150001 (PayNet), 01 acquirer ID, 02 merchant account. Currency 458.

qris.name: QRIS (Indonesia)
qris.rationale: MAI 26-45 per PJSP plus tag 51 national merchant ID (NMID) and MPAN. Merchant criteria UMI/UKE/UME/UBE/URE give a size prior. Static-to-dynamic conversion is common.

qr-ph.name: QR Ph (Philippines)
qr-ph.rationale: EMVCo-based national QR. Secondary (reverse-engineered test vectors): P2P in MAI tag 27 with GUID com.p2pqrpay, P2M in tag 28 with GUID ph.ppmi.p2m, sub-tag 01 = acquirer BIC; currency 608. A provisional profile row is cheap, but confirm against BSP/PPMI specs before relying on it.

vietqr.name: VietQR (NAPAS)
vietqr.rationale: Tag 38 GUID A000000727: 01 beneficiary (00 BIN, 01 account/card), 02 service code QRIBFTTA (to account) / QRIBFTTC (to card) / QRPUSH (merchant payment) / QRCASH (ATM cash), 62.08 purpose. Currency 704. NAPAS spec v1.5.2. QRPUSH is a direct P2M signal, and QRCASH is a cash withdrawal, not spending.

khqr.name: KHQR (Bakong, Cambodia)
khqr.rationale: Tags 29/30 with a name@bank Bakong ID; tag 99 timestamp/expiry (required for dynamic). KHR 116 or USD 840. The MD5 of the QR string is the Bakong transaction-lookup key (merchant side).

upi-autopay-mandate.name: UPI AutoPay mandates and pre-debit notifications
upi-autopay-mandate.rationale: The 24 h pre-debit notification gives advance warning of subscription debits. Exempt: FASTag MCC 4784 and NCMC MCC 7412 auto-replenishment (OC-207). AFA threshold is Rs 15k, raised to Rs 1L for mutual funds, insurance premiums and credit-card bills (OC-151A quoting RBI, 12 Dec 2023). OC-215A: at most 1 attempt plus 3 retries per mandate, executed in non-peak hours (peak 10:00-13:00, 17:00-21:30). OC-223 (7 Oct 2025): users view and port mandates across UPI apps, user-driven only. UPI HELP (OC-227) adds a first-party unified mandate view. No third-party API, so capture relies on SMS/notification adapters (Android) or share/paste (iOS).

upi-autopay-mandate.name: UPI AutoPay / e-mandate messages (mandate creation, pre-debit notice, execution)
upi-autopay-mandate.rationale: The most precise recurring signal in India. A vendor (Google Cloud Issuer Switch) model of UPI mandates has a UMN, EXACT/MAX amount rule and recurrence patterns. It was read from a third-party mirror because the canonical googleapis path was removed; NPCI's spec and RBI pre-debit rules are unverified this session. BRAKE sees mandates only through user-facing messages.

upi-lite.name: UPI Lite on-device balance (funding-instrument label)
upi-lite.rationale: Rs 1,000 per transaction / Rs 5,000 total (OC-169A, after RBI 4 Dec 2024), with auto top-up (OC-205). A Lite load is an own transfer, not spending. By design, banks send a consolidated periodic debit SMS rather than one per payment (OC-138), so bank-SMS-only users under-count small spends. PSP-app notifications or history are the per-payment source. Tap & Pay amounts up to Rs 500 go through Lite if enabled (OC-186).

rupay-credit-on-upi.name: RuPay credit card on UPI (funding-instrument label)
rupay-credit-on-upi.rationale: One purchase yields a UPI alert, a card statement line and later a card-bill payment (a transfer). The limit is the lowest of the credit limit, the issuer's UPI risk limit and the customer limit. Needed for double-count avoidance.

upi-credit-line.name: Pre-sanctioned credit line on UPI (funding-instrument label)
upi-credit-line.rationale: Merchant payments funded by bank credit lines (OC-171), purpose-bound since OC-171A. Repayments are loan payments, not spending. Mostly a schema concern.

upi-reserve-pay.name: UPI Reserve Pay / Single-Block-Multiple-Debits
upi-reserve-pay.rationale: A block is a commitment, not spending; each debit is the spend. Introduced by OC-200 (31 Jul 2024). OC-228 (8 Oct 2025) extends it to all UPI-permitted funding sources (SA, CA, OD, RuPay credit card, credit lines). Caps: block <= Rs 10,000, <= 90 days, one active block per mobile number per merchant, initially only online verified low-ticket, high-frequency merchants. Label blocks so they are not counted as spend.

upi-circle.name: UPI Circle delegated payments (incl. IoT/software/AI-profile delegates)
upi-circle.rationale: Full delegation: Rs 5k per transaction / Rs 15k per month, Rs 5k/day cooling period in the first 24 h, and the primary sees the secondary's transactions (OC-201, 13 Aug 2024). OC-201B extends this to IoT devices and software profiles (smart glasses, watch, TV, AI profiles in a closed user group), domestic P2M only, debits only by explicit user action. It adds purpose code 'BH' in the UPI raw file (back-office, not known to appear in consumer alerts). The earlier 'Merchant Identifier Code (MIC)' claim is not in the circular text. Useful for initiator/ownership labelling once notification formats are known.

upi-transaction-alerts.name: UPI transaction alerts (bank SMS and PSP app notifications with RRN/UTR)
upi-transaction-alerts.rationale: The fastest consumer-visible confirmation of UPI payments. The 12-digit RRN plus VPA/banking name is the strongest cross-source key. Under OC-215A, issuer banks must include the available balance in every successful UPI transaction communication. UPI Lite spends get only consolidated periodic SMS (OC-138). Delivered via the android-notification-listener / android-sms adapters. Android 15 redacts OTP-bearing notifications for untrusted listeners (all apps). Android 17 delays WebOTP-format OTP SMS by 3 h for non-recipient SMS readers; ordinary debit alerts are probably unaffected.

alipay-wechat-qr.name: Alipay / WeChat Pay / Alipay+ QR
alipay-wechat-qr.rationale: Proprietary opaque QR tokens (unverified) give at most a 'QR payment via Alipay/WeChat' hint with no amount or merchant. China is low priority.

paypay.name: PayPay (Japan)
paypay.rationale: The Open Payment API (dynamic QR codeId, merchantPaymentId <=64, paymentId, status COMPLETED/AUTHORIZED, 4-5 s polling) is merchant-side only. Consumers are observable only via notifications.

vipps-mobilepay.name: Vipps MobilePay
vipps-mobilepay.rationale: ePayment API (NOK/DKK/EUR; WEB_REDIRECT/QR/PUSH_MESSAGE/NATIVE_REDIRECT; states CREATED..TERMINATED; reference ^[a-zA-Z0-9-]{8,64}$; optional receipt lines) is merchant-side. One-time QRs are opaque. Consumers are observable via notifications and PSD2 feeds.

swish.name: Swish (Sweden)
swish.rationale: No consumer-side API or interceptable payload. Rail label only, observed via notifications/open banking. Details unverified.

bizum.name: Bizum (Spain)
bizum.rationale: Bank-integrated phone-number payments. Rail label only, observed via bank notifications/PSD2. Details unverified.

blik.name: BLIK (Poland)
blik.rationale: The 6-digit code is generated inside the bank app, so in-spend is invisible. Post-spend comes via bank notifications. Details unverified.

ideal-wero.name: iDEAL / Wero (EPI)
ideal-wero.rationale: Redirect-based web checkout is observable only as browser redirect/confirmation pages (via the extension). Migration timeline unverified.

sepa-instant.name: SEPA Instant Credit Transfer (IPR, Verification of Payee)
sepa-instant.rationale: Rail label. Seen via PSD2 account feeds with ISO 20022 EndToEndId. IPR/VoP dates unverified in this session.

fednow-rtp.name: FedNow / RTP (US instant rails)
fednow-rtp.rationale: No consumer-side observability. Appear as fast-posting transactions in Plaid/1033 feeds. Limits unverified.

mpesa-confirmation-sms.name: M-Pesa confirmation SMS
mpesa-confirmation-sms.rationale: Every M-Pesa transaction yields an SMS with a unique receipt code, amount, counterparty, time and balance (exact format unverified). Richest post-spend signal in Kenya. Subject to Play SMS policy.

mpesa-stk-push.name: M-Pesa Express / STK push (Daraja)
mpesa-stk-push.rationale: Merchant-side API (CustomerPayBillOnline; callback MerchantRequestID/CheckoutRequestID/ResultCode/ResultDesc). Not accessible to a consumer app without merchant partnerships.

payment-request-api.name: W3C Payment Request API (extension hook)
payment-request-api.rationale: Supported in Chrome 60+, Chrome Android 53+, Edge 15+, Safari 11.1+ and Android WebView 136+ (MDN BCD as of 2026-10-04); Firefox 55 only behind dom.payments.request.enabled/supportedRegions. Only the merchant page sees PaymentResponse. An extension could wrap PaymentRequest in the main world to read details.total, but that is invasive and brittle, and store acceptance is unknown.

secure-payment-confirmation.name: Secure Payment Confirmation (SPC)
secure-payment-confirmation.rationale: Browser-native passkey confirmation dialog (payee, amount, instrument). Chromium-only (Chrome/Chrome Android 95+, with Edge, Opera and Samsung Internet mirroring); not Firefox, Safari or Android WebView. Experimental. securePaymentConfirmationAvailability() from Chrome 139, getSecurePaymentConfirmationCapabilities() from Chrome 148. Not observable by third parties by design.

apple-pay-web.name: Apple Pay on the web (Apple Pay JS / Payment Request)
apple-pay-web.rationale: The native sheet is not observable. The page gets an encrypted token and contact data. Use DOM checkout context instead.

google-pay-web.name: Google Pay API for web
google-pay-web.rationale: The sheet is not observable. PaymentData goes only to the merchant (field list unverified). Use DOM checkout context instead.

browser-checkout-dom.name: Browser extension checkout DOM (cart total, Place-order click)
browser-checkout-dom.rationale: The main web pre-spend surface and counterpart to the QR scan. Works on desktop and iOS Safari Web Extensions, not Android Chrome. Restrict host permissions to commerce allowlists.

payment-confirmation-page.name: Payment confirmation pages and PSP redirects (incl. GA4 dataLayer purchase event)
payment-confirmation-page.rationale: Confirmation URLs, order numbers and redirect returns (iDEAL/Wero, 3DS, UPI/Pix web flows) confirm web spends and bridge to order e-mails. The dataLayer purchase schema is unverified.

payment-app-deeplink-handoff.name: Hand-off to the user's payment app (Android intents, iOS app-specific schemes/universal links)
payment-app-deeplink-handoff.rationale: Required plumbing so pre-spend checks do not add friction. Android: original URI via ACTION_VIEW/createChooser. In India this works only for verified/online merchants, because intents (mode 04/05) are disallowed for P2P and offline non-verified merchants (OC-76A/76C); otherwise 'open your UPI app and scan'. iOS: the generic upi scheme target is undefined. open() of an app-specific scheme (e.g. phonepe://pay, tez://upi/pay, paytmmp://pay; secondary) is not constrained by LSApplicationQueriesSchemes. Only canOpenURL detection is capped (50; 25 for apps linked on iOS 27+), so let the user pick their app once.
payment-app-deeplink-handoff.policy_constraints: NPCI OC-76A/76C initiation-mode rules; QR share & Pay <= Rs 2,000 for P2P and non-verified offline P2M; iOS canOpenURL query cap.

payment-string-share-paste.name: Shared/pasted payment strings (Pix copia e cola, upi:// links, payment links)
payment-string-share-paste.rationale: Explicit share/paste into BRAKE reuses the QR parsers. Avoid background clipboard reading (restricted on modern OSs; specifics unverified).

gmail-api.name: Gmail API (server-side, gmail.readonly + q filter)
gmail-api.rationale: Highest semantic value and widest coverage, but it needs restricted-scope verification, an annual security assessment for any server-side access, an app-type eligibility review whose 2026 wording is unverified, and a whole-mailbox consent. Start verification during the MVP phase and ship after the forwarding MVP has proven extraction quality.
gmail-api.access_requirements: Restricted-scope OAuth verification (brand, scope justification, demo video, app-type review). Annual CASA security assessment for apps that access, or can access, Gmail data from or through a server. Lab prices of ~$540-$1,800/yr (Tier 2) and ~$4.5k-$8k (Tier 3) come from 2024-25 rate cards compiled in a 2026 secondary source; 2026 prices are unverified. 100-new-user lifetime cap while unverified. In Testing mode, refresh tokens expire after 7 days (unless only name/email/profile scopes are requested). 100 refresh tokens per account per client ID.
gmail-api.policy_constraints: Google API Services User Data Policy, Limited Use (text last updated 15 Feb 2024): applies to raw, aggregated, anonymized and derived data; no transfer to ad platforms, data brokers or information resellers; no ads; no use to determine credit-worthiness or for lending; humans may not read the data without per-item affirmative agreement (or the security, legal or aggregated-internal-ops exceptions). The Workspace API User Data and Developer Policy additionally bars generalized AI/ML training beyond the user's personalized model (secondary sources). Also required: pre-consent in-product disclosure, a public Limited Use statement, encrypted tokens and incremental authorization.
data_fields: payload.headers (From, Subject, Date, Message-ID, List-Unsubscribe, Authentication-Results)
gmail-api.typical_latency: merchant send delay (seconds-minutes) + seconds with push, else poll interval

gmail-api.name: Transactional email (orders, receipts, refunds, subscriptions)
gmail-api.rationale: Main input for refund↔order links, trial/renewal/price-change events and disaggregating app-store billing. One order can produce several charges, so link candidates rather than merging them. Access cost is assessed in the Gmail stream.

gmail-api.name: Gmail API (OAuth)
gmail-api.rationale: Rich semantic context (line items, subscriptions, refunds), but the heaviest compliance burden. It needs Restricted scope verification and, for server-side access, an annual third-party security assessment. Limited Use covers derived data, with no ads, sale, credit use or non-personalised AI training. gmail.metadata cannot use q queries and returns no body, so it is not a lighter substitute. Ship after the forwarding route and on-device extraction are proven.
gmail-api.access_requirements: Google OAuth app verification. gmail.readonly and gmail.metadata are Restricted (secondary). Annual security assessment and Letter of Assessment from a Google-designated third party (verified via the Open Terms Archive copy of the policy). Testing mode: 100 test users and 7-day refresh tokens (secondary).
gmail-api.policy_constraints: Limited Use applies to raw, aggregated, anonymised and derived data (verified). Human reading only with affirmative agreement for specific messages (verified). No ads, sale, credit-worthiness or lending use (verified). No training of generalised/non-personalised AI/ML (secondary). Apple 5.1.2(i) requires explicit permission before any third-party AI processing (verified). q is unusable under gmail.metadata (verified, discovery rev. 20260928).

gmail-api.name: Email receipt and order parsing (Slice/Unroll.me, Paribus, Earny prior art)
gmail-api.rationale: Highest semantic value: items, order IDs, renewals, trials, refunds. Prior art failed on monetization (purchase-data panels; the Unroll.me case, unverified) and on over-broad scopes. Use sender allow-lists, local or ephemeral processing, and persist extracted facts only. Restricted-scope compliance cost is unverified here.

gmail-push-watch.name: Gmail users.watch + Cloud Pub/Sub + history.list
gmail-push-watch.rationale: A transport that cuts sync latency to seconds. The Pub/Sub notification carries only {emailAddress, historyId}, which enables an on-device design in which the server only relays a content-free push. watch must be re-called at least every 7 days (Google recommends daily). Notifications above 1 event/sec/user are dropped, so a periodic history.list reconciliation is required, and a stale startHistoryId returns 404 and forces a full sync.
gmail-push-watch.access_requirements: Same restricted scopes as gmail-api; a GCP Pub/Sub topic that already exists, with publish permission granted to Gmail; the topic must be in the same project as the caller.
gmail-push-watch.typical_latency: seconds (no published SLA); max 1 notification/sec/user, excess dropped

gmail-metadata-scope.name: Gmail gmail.metadata (headers and labels only)
gmail-metadata-scope.rationale: Still restricted, so it carries the same verification and CASA burden, yet it cannot use q or full/raw formats. It forces broader enumeration while yielding few amounts or items.

gmail-api-on-device.name: Gmail API called from the mobile app with local extraction (local-client variant)
gmail-api-on-device.rationale: Possibly the best long-run Gmail architecture for privacy: bodies and tokens never leave the device. The hoped-for CASA relief is weaker evidence than first stated. The 'local client applications ... may be exempt' sentence is verified only in 2022 policy text and is absent from the 15 Feb 2024 User Data Policy, so a 2026 exemption is unverified. OAuth verification is required regardless. Get Google's written position, including on syncing derived facts and on a server that only relays Pub/Sub {emailAddress, historyId}.
gmail-api-on-device.access_requirements: Restricted-scope OAuth verification; CASA exemption for local-only clients unconfirmed for 2026 (exemption sentence removed from the User Data Policy in the Feb 2024 revision).
gmail-api-on-device.policy_constraints: Limited Use covers derived data; any exemption likely requires that no restricted data transits a BRAKE server.
gmail-api-on-device.typical_latency: Android seconds-minutes via FCM relay (unverified); iOS minutes-hours (background limits)

gmail-workspace-addon.name: Gmail Workspace add-on (contextual, current message only)
gmail-workspace-addon.rationale: Its sensitive (not restricted) scopes cover only the open message and only on user action, so the burden is light and the privacy story is excellent, but coverage is low because it depends on user initiative. Mobile Gmail support for add-ons is unverified.
gmail-workspace-addon.access_requirements: Sensitive-scope verification; Workspace Marketplace listing review.

microsoft-graph-mail.name: Microsoft Graph mail (Mail.Read) with delta and change notifications
microsoft-graph-mail.rationale: Personal accounts can grant it without admin consent, it has no known CASA-style audit, and push notifications are documented at under 1 minute average and 3 minutes max. A good second provider after the forwarding MVP; the consumer Outlook base is smaller than Gmail's, especially in India.
microsoft-graph-mail.access_requirements: Entra app registration supporting personal accounts; publisher verification (CPP account) recommended and important for M365 tenants; no mandated third-party audit known as of 2026 (unverified).
microsoft-graph-mail.policy_constraints: Microsoft APIs terms; apply BRAKE's uniform Limited Use-style policy.
microsoft-graph-mail.typical_latency: <1 min avg, 3 min max (change notifications); subscriptions ≤10,080 min

microsoft-graph-mail-readbasic.name: Microsoft Graph Mail.ReadBasic (no body, preview or attachments)
microsoft-graph-mail-readbasic.rationale: A genuinely narrower grant that users can see, consentable by personal accounts and usable for change notifications. Good for merchant touchpoints and recurring-sender detection as an 'Outlook light' tier, but weak for amounts.
microsoft-graph-mail-readbasic.access_requirements: Entra app registration; delegated Mail.ReadBasic, no admin consent.

imap-generic.name: IMAP for iCloud and other providers (app-specific passwords / XOAUTH2)
imap-generic.rationale: Covers providers with no modern API, but app passwords are long-lived, full-mailbox secrets, so use them only on-device. Outlook.com basic auth and app passwords have been off since 16 Sep 2024 (use Graph). Gmail IMAP needs the broadest restricted scope (https://mail.google.com/), so prefer forwarding. Yahoo reportedly no longer accepts app-password login (OAuth only), so iCloud is the main remaining app-password case.
imap-generic.access_requirements: iCloud: imap.mail.me.com:993 with an app-specific password. Yahoo: OAuth only per a 2026 client FAQ; client approval believed required (unverified). Outlook.com: XOAUTH2 with IMAP.AccessAsUser.All (consentable by personal accounts). Gmail: XOAUTH2 with https://mail.google.com/ (restricted).
imap-generic.policy_constraints: Credential custody risk; possible provider ToS limits on automated access.

email-forwarding-inbox.name: User-configured forwarding to a per-user BRAKE inbound address
email-forwarding-inbox.rationale: No OAuth scope, verification or CASA, and it works with every provider today. The user's own filter enforces narrowness and doubles as the disconnect, and DKIM survives auto-forward for sender verification. Costs are onboarding friction, stale filters, and Microsoft 365 tenants that block external auto-forward by default.
email-forwarding-inbox.access_requirements: BRAKE inbound MX/SMTP, DKIM/ARC verification, per-user unguessable addresses, abuse controls; user completes the provider's forwarding-address confirmation.
email-forwarding-inbox.policy_constraints: Google Limited Use doesn't apply legally (no Google API), but BRAKE should apply it uniformly; GDPR/DPDP apply.

manual-email-share.name: Manual single-email forward, share sheet or .eml/PDF upload
manual-email-share.rationale: Universal, explicit per-message consent, cheap to build. It is also the clean consent path for human-assisted parsing improvements. Precision is high but recall is low.
data_fields: sender (original DKIM usually lost on manual forward)

mailbox-export-import.name: Mailbox export import (e.g., Google Takeout mbox of selected labels)
mailbox-export-import.rationale: A one-off historical backfill for subscription and recurring-merchant detection, with no ongoing access. Process locally (WASM) and discard the file. Provides no real-time signal.

email-api-aggregators.name: Email API aggregators (Nylas, Unipile and similar)
email-api-aggregators.rationale: A shared pre-verified OAuth client skips Google's queue, but the consent screen shows the vendor's brand, an extra processor holds tokens and content, and per-connection fees and lock-in follow. All of this conflicts with BRAKE's minimum-transmission and provenance principles.
email-api-aggregators.access_requirements: Commercial contract; vendor's verified GCP app (Nylas shared app, Unipile CASA Tier 2 client, per 2026 secondary sources).

bank-email-alerts.name: Bank/card transaction alert emails
bank-email-alerts.rationale: A near-real-time transaction sensor that also works on iOS. In India, HDFC reportedly emails every UPI transaction with the 12-digit UPI RRN, which is a strong fusion key. Coverage varies by bank (email is optional under RBI rules), and authentic alerts can still be wrong (RBL 2026), so treat them as pending or issuer-confirmed, not posted.
bank-email-alerts.policy_constraints: Match DKIM d= domains (incl. *.bank.in migration), never From; never mark posted from email alone.

merchant-receipt-emails.name: Merchant order confirmations, receipts, invoices, shipping/delivery emails
merchant-receipt-emails.rationale: The semantic richness that bank data lacks: items, order IDs, tax and shipping. It explains bank charges, but item-level presence per merchant is unverified for 2026 and order time often differs from charge time (Amazon charges per shipment; Subscribe & Save lands 14-19 days later).

subscription-lifecycle-emails.name: Subscription lifecycle emails (trial ending, renewal notice, price change, payment failed, cancelled)
subscription-lifecycle-emails.rationale: Directly powers 'renews tomorrow, keep or review?' pre-spend interventions. Legal reminder duties vary by jurisdiction, so combine these emails with transaction recurrence. Do not confuse them with newsletter subscriptions (List-Unsubscribe, Gmail's Manage subscriptions).

india-emandate-predebit-notification.name: India e-mandate pre-transaction (pre-debit) notifications
india-emandate-predebit-notification.rationale: A regulated PRE-SPEND signal at least 24 hours before every recurring e-mandate debit on cards, PPIs and UPI (RBI Digital Payments – E-mandate Framework, 2026, RBI/DPSS/2026-27/396, 21 Apr 2026). It states merchant, amount, date/time, mandate reference and reason, with an opt-out. Secondary sources also describe a mandatory post-debit notification, which is a POST-SPEND confirmation. The channel (SMS, email or app) varies by issuer and payment app.
india-emandate-predebit-notification.policy_constraints: Not required for FASTag/NCMC auto-replenish. AFA-free recurring debits up to ₹15,000 per transaction, or ₹1,00,000 for insurance premiums, mutual fund subscriptions and credit-card bill payments. AFA at registration and first debit. RBI primary text not fetched; corroborated by many secondary sources.

refund-cancellation-emails.name: Refund and order-cancellation emails
refund-cancellation-emails.rationale: Prevents refunds and cancelled orders from being counted as spending or income. Lets BRAKE track 'refund expected but not yet credited' by linking order IDs.

travel-reservation-emails.name: Travel bookings and reservations (flights, hotels, trains, restaurants, events)
travel-reservation-emails.rationale: POST-SPEND confirmation of large purchases plus contextual PRE-SPEND (an upcoming trip budget, an expected restaurant spend). These are the emails most likely to carry schema.org Reservation markup.

bill-statement-emails.name: Bills and statements (utility, telecom, credit-card statements)
bill-statement-emails.rationale: Gives upcoming known obligations (pre-spend) and monthly reconciliation, but Indian card statements are password-protected PDFs. Account Aggregator and open banking cover statements better. Card bill payments are transfers.

merchant-intent-marketing-emails.name: Merchant intent marketing (abandoned cart, price drop, back in stock)
merchant-intent-marketing-emails.rationale: The merchant itself signals likely purchase intent, which is a pre-spend reflection opportunity. But volume is high, precision low, and BRAKE must not amplify re-engagement. Opt-in only, and test behavioral value first.

payment-otp-emails.name: Payment OTP / authorization emails
payment-otp-emails.rationale: Email's only real IN-SPEND signal, but OTPs are authentication secrets: breach and fraud risk, and alarming to users and reviewers. Exclude OTP senders and subjects at query and filter level. Any future exploration should be on-device only, with the code dropped by the parser.

schema-org-email-markup.name: schema.org JSON-LD/microdata in email (Order, Invoice, ParcelDelivery, Reservation)
schema-org-email-markup.rationale: Deterministic, cheap, highest-confidence extraction when present and the sender is DKIM-verified. 2026 prevalence is unknown, so make it the first extractor layer and measure presence through aggregated telemetry.

email-template-parsers.name: Per-sender versioned template parsers (DKIM-gated)
email-template-parsers.rationale: High precision for the top senders per country (e.g., HDFC UPI alerts with an RRN regex). They break silently when merchants redesign emails, so they need sum-check validators and success-rate telemetry. Under Limited Use, templates must be built from test purchases or per-message donated emails, not from staff reading user mail.

on-device-llm-extraction.name: On-device schema-constrained LLM extraction (Android ML Kit GenAI Prompt API; Apple Foundation Models)
on-device-llm-extraction.rationale: Handles the long tail without sending bodies off-device. Android: the Prompt API requires at least 1.0.0-beta4 and minSdk 26, and structured output via @Generable needs genai-schema-compiler 1.0.0-alpha1; availability is per device (FeatureStatus), as of 2026-09-03. iOS: Foundation Models (iOS 26.0+, Apple Intelligence devices only) offers @Generable guided generation. The 2026 framework can also route to Private Cloud Compute or server models, so BRAKE must pin email extraction to the on-device model. Needs validators and prompt-injection defenses.

on-device-llm-extraction.name: On-device model extraction (Apple Foundation Models, Gemini Nano via AICore) - processing mechanism
on-device-llm-extraction.rationale: Content never leaves the device, which satisfies minimisation, Apple's 'not collected' and the interception arguments. AICore 'doesn't store any record of the input data or the resulting outputs' (verified). Use deterministic parsers first and the model as fallback. Private Cloud Compute or server providers change the analysis.

email-llm-extraction-server.name: Server-side LLM extraction of email content
email-llm-extraction-server.rationale: For Gmail-API data it adds CASA scope and Limited Use transfer obligations (consent, no training or retention) and weakens the privacy story. Only consider it for forwarded mail with explicit opt-in.
email-llm-extraction-server.policy_constraints: Limited Use: service-provider transfer only with consent, no generalized model training; Workspace policy expects prompt-injection protection.

gmail-purchases-category.name: Gmail category:purchases / category:reservations as a q pre-filter
gmail-purchases-category.rationale: Uses Gmail's own classifier to cut what BRAKE fetches (practical minimization). Requires gmail.readonly, since q is unusable with gmail.metadata. Recall on Indian bank alerts and regional-language receipts is unknown, so combine it with explicit sender lists.

microsoft-graph-mail-on-device.name: Microsoft Graph mail called from the mobile app with local extraction (local-client variant)
microsoft-graph-mail-on-device.rationale: The Outlook counterpart of gmail-api-on-device, which the doc had omitted. A public-client app (MSAL) holds delegated Mail.ReadBasic or Mail.Read tokens on the device and extracts locally. Push still needs a server, because Graph webhooks must be publicly accessible HTTPS endpoints. A basic (non-rich) notification carries only changeType, resource and message id, with no content, so BRAKE's server can relay a content-free push to the device. No CASA-style audit is known for Graph (unverified), so the gain is privacy rather than lower compliance cost.
microsoft-graph-mail-on-device.access_requirements: Entra app registration supporting personal accounts; delegated Mail.ReadBasic or Mail.Read (no admin consent for personal accounts); a public HTTPS webhook endpoint for change notifications.
microsoft-graph-mail-on-device.policy_constraints: Apply BRAKE's uniform Limited Use-style policy; tokens kept in Keychain/Keystore.
microsoft-graph-mail-on-device.typical_latency: notification <1 min avg / 3 min max + device wake latency (iOS minutes-hours, unverified)

sms-bank-alerts.name: Bank/card/UPI transaction SMS alerts (content, parsed by template packs)
sms-bank-alerts.rationale: The highest-value real-time POST-SPEND content in India and Nigeria. One on-device parser serves every capture path (SMS permission, notification listener, RCS, paste, Shortcuts). Verified-sender plus known-template parses reach ~0.95 confidence and carry RRN/UTR keys.
dedup_keys: masked tail + amount + minute timestamp + merchant
sms-bank-alerts.typical_latency: seconds to minutes after authorization (no published SLA; unverified)
sms-bank-alerts.access_requirements: Depends on capture path: Android SMS permission (Play-gated), Android notification listener, or user paste/Shortcuts on iOS.
sms-bank-alerts.policy_constraints: Parse on-device; persist only extracted facts plus a redacted, expiring excerpt; drop OTPs before persistence; never render links from alerts.

sms-bank-alerts.name: Bank SMS alerts (reconciliation keys)
sms-bank-alerts.rationale: Very high value for reconciliation (RRN, last4, Avl Bal, reversal and pre-debit notices; formats unverified), but platform-policy eligibility is decided in the SMS stream.

mobile-money-sms.name: Mobile-money confirmation SMS (M-Pesa, Mixx by Yas/ex-Tigo Pesa, Selcom, bKash)
mobile-money-sms.rationale: For mobile-money users this is the system of record, with a strong per-transaction code. It uses the same adapter as bank SMS, with extra template packs, and becomes MVP if BRAKE launches in East Africa or Bangladesh. Agent cash-in and cash-out are transfers, not spending. Brands drift: Tigo Pesa now sends as Mixx by Yas (MIXXBYYAS), with old and new templates on the same sender, and M-Pesa shares a sender across KE/TZ/MZ, so dispatch must look at content. Mixx sends twin messages (primary plus acknowledgement) that share a TxnID.
data_fields: transaction kind (send, pay, buy goods, withdraw, deposit)
dedup_keys: M-Pesa transaction code (10 chars KE/TZ; 11 chars in MZ fixtures; do not hard-code length)
Mixx by Yas / Tigo Pesa TxnId (shared by primary and ack twin messages)
mobile-money-sms.access_requirements: Android capture via SMS permission or notification listener; iOS only via paste.
mobile-money-sms.policy_constraints: Counterparty names and phone numbers are third-party personal data; keep them on-device.

sms-pre-debit-notifications.name: Mandate / UPI AutoPay pre-debit and bill-due SMS (India)
sms-pre-debit-notifications.rationale: One of the few real PRE-SPEND signals in messaging. RBI's Digital Payments – E-mandate Framework, 2026 (2026-04-21; secondary) requires a pre-transaction notice at least 24 h before each recurring debit on cards, PPIs and UPI. The notice must name the merchant, amount, debit date/time and e-mandate reference, and the customer can opt out. FASTag/NCMC auto-replenish is exempt. The signal comes cheaply with the SMS parser and directly powers renewal interventions. Transaction-only parsers drop these messages. PennyWise excludes them from transactions but extracts them into MandateInfo.
sms-pre-debit-notifications.typical_latency: >= 24 h before the debit (regulatory minimum, secondary)
sms-pre-debit-notifications.policy_constraints: Context only; never founds a spend candidate.

merchant-transactional-sms.name: Merchant order/delivery/refund SMS
merchant-transactional-sms.rationale: Adds order ids, refunds and merchant identity for users without connected email. Email is richer, and merchants are reportedly moving these messages to WhatsApp/RCS (unverified).

sms-balance-and-due-alerts.name: Balance, limit, statement and low-balance alerts (context)
sms-balance-and-due-alerts.rationale: Free with the parser. Powers balance-chain verification (detecting missed and forged alerts) and budget-cycle context. Never founds a transaction candidate.

sms-otp-messages.name: OTP SMS (incl. card e-commerce OTPs naming amount and merchant)
sms-otp-messages.rationale: Technically an in-spend signal, but an app that reads OTPs is indistinguishable from malware, and any leak is catastrophic. Android 15 redacts OTP notifications for untrusted listeners. SMS-Retriever-hash messages were already delayed 3 h for most apps before Android 17. Android 17 adds a 3 h delay for WebOTP messages to non-domain-verified apps (all apps) and for standard OTP SMS to apps targeting API 37+. RBI's 2025 authentication directions (in force 2026-04-01; secondary) allow alternatives to SMS OTP without abolishing it. Drop OTPs at capture, and never persist, log or send them to models.
sms-otp-messages.policy_constraints: Android 15 OTP notification redaction; Android 17 SMS OTP protection (WebOTP all apps; standard OTP SMS when targeting API 37); RECEIVE_SENSITIVE_NOTIFICATIONS is signature|role.
sms-otp-messages.typical_latency: real-time; withheld 3 h on Android 17 for non-recipient apps (WebOTP) or API-37-targeting apps (standard OTP)

rcs-mms-provider-read.name: Undocumented RCS read via content://mms rows (tr_id 'proto:' with ..._agent@rbm.goog)
rcs-mms-provider-read.rationale: Exposes the RBM agent id (strong sender verification) and history, but it is Google Messages implementation behaviour rather than an API, requires READ_SMS, and can break silently.

whatsapp-business-notifications.name: WhatsApp business/bank transactional messages via notification listener
whatsapp-business-notifications.rationale: There is no consumer read API (Meta's API is business-side only), so the notification listener with a per-sender opt-in is the only passive path. Previews and grouping make it unreliable. Shares a stream with E2E-encrypted personal chats.
data_fields: (in the business API, not readable by BRAKE: order_details total_amount, items, payment_type upi, reference_id)
whatsapp-business-notifications.access_requirements: Android notification listener; user-selected business senders.
whatsapp-business-notifications.policy_constraints: WhatsApp terms reportedly prohibit automated access/unofficial clients (unverified); never use accessibility scraping.

whatsapp-forward-to-brake.name: User forwards receipts/alerts to a BRAKE WhatsApp Business number
whatsapp-forward-to-brake.rationale: A user-initiated, cross-platform channel that also works on iOS in WhatsApp-first markets. Processing is server-side, so Meta and BRAKE both see the content, which conflicts with the local-processing preference. Cost is likely low: since 2025-07-01 Meta uses per-message pricing and charges only when a template message is delivered, so inbound forwards and free-form replies inside the service window are not billed (secondary; current rate cards unverified).
whatsapp-forward-to-brake.access_requirements: WhatsApp Business Platform (Cloud API) account, verified number, webhook endpoint.

ios-shortcuts-message-automation.name: iOS Shortcuts 'Message' personal automation passing text to a BRAKE App Intent
ios-shortcuts-message-automation.rationale: The only near-automatic iOS route to bank SMS: user-configured, sender-scoped and on-device. Whether it runs without confirmation, fires for alphanumeric senders and passes the full body is unverified. Prototype it.
data_fields: message text passed as App Intent String parameter
ios-shortcuts-message-automation.access_requirements: App Intents (iOS 16+); user creates the automation.

user-shared-message-text.name: User copy/paste or share of an alert message into BRAKE
user-shared-message-text.rationale: Nearly free, uses the same parser, and has the best consent posture. It is the honest fallback for iOS users in SMS markets. UIPasteControl pastes without the iOS 16+ prompt. There is no sender verification, so confidence comes from template match and corroboration (~0.7-0.85).

android-default-sms-handler.name: Becoming the default SMS app
android-default-sms-handler.rationale: Always permitted by Play, but BRAKE would have to be a full SMS/MMS/RCS client replacing the user's messaging app. That is the most invasive posture and out of scope.

android-sms-retriever-api.name: SMS Retriever / SMS User Consent APIs
android-sms-retriever-api.rationale: Built for an app to read its own single verification SMS: an 11-character app hash (per Google's AppSignatureHelper sample), one message, and a listen of up to five minutes. Android 17 directs OTP readers to these APIs. They do not apply to bank alerts.

in-dlt-header-registry.name: TRAI DLT SMS header register and category suffixes (India sender-verification reference data)
in-dlt-header-registry.rationale: Public reference data rather than user data. TRAI publishes a register mapping assigned SMS headers to entities (one open-source project uses a copy dated 2020-06-16) and the operator/circle prefix tables. The TCCCP Second Amendment 2025 adds category suffixes (-P/-S/-T/-G). Together these could seed BRAKE's OTA sender-entity allow-list and make spoof detection stronger than hand-curated per-bank regexes. Staleness is a risk, because headers assigned since the dated copy are missing. All of this is secondary; the primary TRAI pages were not reachable.
in-dlt-header-registry.access_requirements: Download of TRAI-published files; ship as a signed registry/template-pack update.
in-dlt-header-registry.policy_constraints: Public data; verify licence/terms of reuse (unverified).

manual-should-i-buy.name: "Should I buy this?" quick check (manual purchase intent)
manual-should-i-buy.rationale: Only universal pre-spend surface; zero permissions; anchors intent->purchased/abandoned outcome measurement; works for users with no connected accounts.

price-entry-widget.name: Quick-entry widgets, Controls, Action button, Quick Settings tile, app shortcuts
price-entry-widget.rationale: Cuts the main friction of the manual check to about two taps. iOS interactive widgets are buttons/toggles only ('should do more than open the app'; open the app via Link/widgetURL). Controls (iOS 18) work from Control Center, the Lock Screen and the Action button. Android widgets cannot take free text (Android 12 added only stateful CheckBox/Switch/RadioButton), so open a lightweight keypad activity.
price-entry-widget.policy_constraints: Redact amounts on the Lock Screen. Widget buttons/toggles are inactive on a locked device until the user authenticates. For Controls, authentication and locked-device redaction are developer opt-ins that BRAKE should enable.

cooling-off-wishlist.name: Cooling-off timer and wish list (Live Activity on iOS / scheduled notifications)
cooling-off-wishlist.rationale: Extends the intent horizon and marks intent outcomes. iOS Live Activities last up to 8 h active plus up to 4 h on the Lock Screen, and the HIG says to keep them under 8 h and avoid sensitive information, so show item and amount only on opt-in. Longer waits use local notifications. Android 16 Live Updates list timers/countdowns as an inappropriate primary use, so Android uses ordinary scheduled notifications.
cooling-off-wishlist.policy_constraints: Apple HIG: no ads, avoid sensitive info, at most 8 h. Android Live Updates not for timers/countdowns as primary use.

manual-transaction-entry.name: Manual transaction entry
manual-transaction-entry.rationale: Required for cash and for users with no connected accounts; accurate when entered but coverage decays with fatigue; must fuse with later bank records as possible duplicates. Design targets: <=4 taps, <=6 s median, amount the only required field.
dedup_keys: amount exact + date +/-1 day + merchant similarity

share-sheet.name: Share-to-BRAKE (share sheet: URL, text, image)
share-sheet.rationale: Cross-platform, policy-safe, works with app-first commerce (India); payloads usually carry URL+title but no price, so needs the on-device metadata resolver; URL reveals purchase intent, so resolve on-device and strip tracking params.
dedup_keys: order_id when shared from confirmation page
share-sheet.access_requirements: Android ACTION_SEND intent filter; iOS Share extension activation rules

ios-share-js-preprocessing.name: iOS/macOS Safari share extension with JavaScript preprocessing
ios-share-js-preprocessing.rationale: NSExtensionJavaScriptPreprocessingFile runs ExtensionPreprocessingJS in the live Safari page before the extension starts, so BRAKE can read JSON-LD, meta tags, cart totals and order numbers with no browser-extension permissions.

paste-product-url.name: Paste product URL
paste-product-url.rationale: Cheap field inside the quick check; use UIPasteControl on iOS 16+ to avoid paste alerts; Android 12+ shows a clipboard-access toast; never read the clipboard silently.

product-page-metadata.name: Product-page metadata resolver (schema.org JSON-LD, Meta product tags, Open Graph, DOM)
product-page-metadata.rationale: Shared on-device library for share, paste and extensions; JSON-LD Offer.price/priceCurrency is cleanest; core OGP has no price property; retailer affiliate APIs conflict with BRAKE's no-affiliate principle; server-side fetching leaks intent.

browser-extension-chromium.name: Chromium MV3 browser extension (Chrome, Edge, Brave)
browser-extension-chromium.rationale: Best web in-flow timing (cart, checkout, confirmation), but desktop-only reach, fragile DOM heuristics and store-policy overhead. Build activeTab-first with per-site optional host permissions. MV3 forbids remotely hosted code, so per-merchant detectors ship as data or remote configuration. Avoid for the India MVP.
browser-extension-chromium.access_requirements: Chrome Web Store developer account and review
browser-extension-chromium.policy_constraints: Limited Use (no personalised ads, data sale, or credit-worthiness/lending use; archived 2022 text verified). Affiliate links need related user action (archived 2022 text verified); the 2025-03-11 update and 2025-06-10 enforcement are secondary-only (unverified). Single purpose. MV3 remote-code ban (verified). Chrome on Android extensions unavailable (unverified).

safari-web-extension.name: Safari Web Extension (macOS, iOS, iPadOS, visionOS)
safari-web-extension.rationale: Reaches iPhone Safari shoppers (USA); per-site Ask/Allow/Deny grants; native messaging keeps data local; high enablement friction; do after Safari share preprocessing proves demand.
safari-web-extension.access_requirements: Shipped inside the iOS/macOS app; Safari 14+/iOS 15+
safari-web-extension.policy_constraints: App Review 4.4.2: no more website access than strictly necessary

firefox-extension.name: Firefox extension (desktop and Android)
firefox-extension.rationale: Cheap port of the WebExtension with a small share. Firefox for Android runs extensions. New extensions must declare data_collection_permissions (since 2025-11-03), with built-in consent UI in Firefox desktop 140+ and Android 142+. Policy 7.3 bans injecting affiliate tags into web content or redirects. BRAKE should declare required: ['none'] and make financialAndPaymentInfo/websiteContent optional.
firefox-extension.policy_constraints: Firefox built-in data consent (financialAndPaymentInfo, browsingActivity, websiteContent, websiteActivity categories); no deceptive consent flows (6.2.2); section 7.3 affiliate-tag injection ban

brake-qr-scanner.name: BRAKE in-app QR scanner (UPI URI, EMVCo MPM incl. Bharat QR, URL, GS1 Digital Link, fiscal QR)
brake-qr-scanner.rationale: In India the scan precedes payment and carries the payee VPA, name, MCC and sometimes amount and reference. BRAKE shows context, then hands off to the user's UPI app (Android ACTION_VIEW with a chooser). On iOS, upi:// hand-off is unpredictable: Apple says the target is undefined when several apps register a scheme, and app-specific schemes are capped by LSApplicationQueriesSchemes (25 entries for apps linked on iOS 27+), so iOS needs a curated app list or a 'scan again in your UPI app' fallback. Strong join to the later SMS/notification RRN. MVP for India (Android first); later for the USA.
data_fields: mc (MCC; 7407 = P2PM per NPCI OC-181, secondary)
brake-qr-scanner.access_requirements: Camera permission, or the Google code scanner without camera permission on Android (needs Play services). iOS: LSApplicationQueriesSchemes entries for each PSP app scheme (cap 50, or 25 when linked on iOS 27+).
brake-qr-scanner.policy_constraints: NPCI rules for non-PSP relay of UPI QR unverified; personal VPAs are personal data (store hashed)

barcode-gtin-lookup.name: Barcode / GTIN product lookup
barcode-gtin-lookup.rationale: A GTIN identifies the product, not the price. Open Food Facts covers food (ODbL; 15 product reads/min/IP and 10 searches/min/IP, applied per user when calls come from users' devices; custom User-Agent required; v2 deprecated, v3.6 current). Its value is 'bought before?' checks and category hints.
barcode-gtin-lookup.access_requirements: Product database terms (ODbL attribution/share-alike for OFF)

price-tag-ocr.name: Photo / live scan of price tag (OCR)
price-tag-ocr.rationale: Cheapest physical-store pre-spend input outside QR markets; iOS DataScannerViewController .currency (iOS 17); ML Kit Text Recognition v2 on Android; approximate amounts (tax-exclusive US prices, Indian MRP).

receipt-photo-ocr.name: Receipt photo OCR (incl. fiscal receipt QR)
receipt-photo-ocr.rationale: Post-spend semantic enrichment (line items, essentiality); ML Kit Document Scanner (no camera permission) + Text Recognition v2; iOS 26 RecognizeDocumentsRequest handles receipts/tables; iOS 27 Foundation Models image input; validate totals deterministically.

receipt-photo-ocr.name: Receipt photo capture with on-device OCR (Fetch/Ibotta/Expensify-style sensing)
receipt-photo-ocr.rationale: Rewards apps show users will photograph receipts for an immediate payoff (unverified). BRAKE's payoff should be splitting a mixed basket into essential and discretionary items, not points. Reject the brand-funded monetization; discard images after extraction.

fiscal-receipt-qr.name: Fiscal receipt / e-invoice QR codes (e.g. Brazil NFC-e, Saudi ZATCA, India B2C dynamic QR)
fiscal-receipt-qr.rationale: Would give exact totals and invoice ids without OCR where mandated; formats and coverage unverified in this stream.

screenshot-import.name: User-initiated screenshot import (cart, payment-success, order screens)
screenshot-import.rationale: Share-to-BRAKE of UPI payment-success or cart screenshots yields UTR/order ids and amounts; on-device OCR + template grammars + optional on-device LLM; cloud AI only with explicit consent (App Review 5.1.2(i)). MVP Android India, next iOS USA.
screenshot-import.policy_constraints: Disclose third-party AI; crop/redact unrelated PII

screenshot-auto-detection.name: Automatic detection of screenshots taken in other apps
screenshot-auto-detection.rationale: iOS userDidTakeScreenshotNotification has no userInfo or image and reaches the app only while it is running. Android 14 ScreenCaptureCallback (DETECT_SCREEN_CAPTURE) fires only while the app's own activity is visible, notifies the user, and provides no image. Detecting screenshots taken in other apps would need broad photo-library access, which is invasive and policy-restricted.

siri-app-intents.name: Siri / App Intents / App Shortcuts voice check
siri-app-intents.rationale: App Shortcut phrases with .applicationName and value prompts for amounts; same AppIntent powers Controls/Action button (MVP); voice is socially awkward in stores.

android-assistant-actions.name: Google Assistant App Actions / Android AppFunctions (Gemini)
android-assistant-actions.rationale: App Actions (shortcuts.xml BIIs, not on Android Go) status under Gemini unverified; AppFunctions is experimental, Android 16+, Gemini private preview as of May 2026.

ios-screen-time-shield.name: iOS Screen Time shields on user-selected shopping apps/web domains (FamilyControls + ManagedSettings + DeviceActivity)
ios-screen-time-shield.rationale: Earliest system-enforced interruption at app launch with tokenized privacy; iOS 26.5 openParentalControlsApp opens BRAKE directly and iOS 26.4 adds a submenu for 'open for 5/15 min'; schedule shields for personal high-regret windows; always allow one-tap bypass. Needs the Family Controls (Distribution) entitlement for the app and each extension; Guideline 4.10 bars monetizing Screen Time APIs.
ios-screen-time-shield.access_requirements: requestAuthorization(for: .individual) iOS 16+; Family Controls (Distribution) entitlement per bundle id and per Screen Time extension
ios-screen-time-shield.policy_constraints: App Review 4.10; shield extension sandbox (no network)

ios-shortcuts-app-automation.name: iOS Shortcuts personal automation on app open
ios-shortcuts-app-automation.rationale: No entitlement but heavy manual setup and re-trigger debouncing; superseded by shields + openParentalControlsApp; fallback for users declining Screen Time authorization (behaviour details unverified).

ios-family-activity-data.name: iOS FamilyActivityData (installed apps, visited domains) — EU only
ios-family-activity-data.rationale: iOS 26.4 approvedWithDataAccess + App and Website Usage entitlement exposes real bundle ids and domains, EU devices/accounts only, one app per device; surveillance-grade and unnecessary for shields.

merchant-partnership.name: Merchant checkout partnership
merchant-partnership.rationale: Cleanest order/checkout data but merchants optimise conversion and have little incentive to add friction; pursue structured post-spend e-receipts first.

payment-provider-partnership.name: Payment-provider partnership (issuer, BNPL, UPI app, wallet)
payment-provider-partnership.rationale: Exact real-time in-spend context inside the provider's own flow; requires commercial agreements and partner security review; UPI flow integration governed by NPCI (unverified).

manual-purchase-check.name: "Should I buy this?" manual purchase check (typed/shared/price-tag)
manual-purchase-check.rationale: User-initiated self-nudge with minimal reactance; the only pre-spend surface that works everywhere, including users with no connected source. Opportunity-cost framing (Frederick et al. 2009) fits here. Its labels are self-selected and must be tagged by surface.
manual-purchase-check.access_requirements: None; iOS share sheet/App Intents, Android ACTION_SEND
dedup_keys: purchase_intent observation id (forward-only join within 24 h, +/-15% amount)

manual-purchase-check.name: 'Should I buy this?' check via share sheet, URL, screenshot, voice or chat (Cleo/Starling-style chat; cooling-off wishlists)
manual-purchase-check.rationale: Universal across countries and platforms and a direct expression of BRAKE's purpose. Pair it with an optional 'remind me in N days' cooling-off. Frame AI answers as reflection, not advice.

cooling-off-hold.name: Cooling-off hold / wishlist with timed reminder
cooling-off-hold.rationale: Delay lets visceral cravings subside (Loewenstein 1996/2005). Asymmetric paternalism supports cooling-off (Camerer et al. 2003). Strong friction is allowed only when the user opted in, ad hoc or via their own rule. Default 24 h, with choices from 1 h to 7 d.
cooling-off-hold.access_requirements: Local notifications; iOS timeSensitive only for user-requested reminders
citations: Camerer et al. 2003 U Penn Law Rev 151(3)

app-launch-friction.name: One-sec-style pause on user-selected shopping apps (iOS FamilyControls/ManagedSettings shield; Android research)
app-launch-friction.rationale: The strongest evidence-backed pre-spend friction, legitimate only as opt-in. Evidence: one sec, a 10 s self-chosen delay with a dismiss option. 36% of opening attempts were dismissed (43% in week 1, then 32-34%), attempts fell 37%, and opens fell 57% after 6 weeks. N = 280 self-selected users, within-person; no shopping-specific data [S]. iOS 16+ needs Apple's approval of the FamilyControls entitlement. Android has no first-party API: UsageStats or Accessibility routes are policy-sensitive and research-only. Habituation must be monitored, since the dismissal rate fell after week 1.
app-launch-friction.access_requirements: iOS 16+ (FamilyControlsMember.individual, iOS 16.0): request the com.apple.developer.family-controls entitlement before App Store submission; device-owner approval with biometric confirmation (verified 2026-10-04). Android: Play policy review for UsageStats/Accessibility (unverified).
dedup_keys: none (app_context is context-only, never founds a candidate)
app-launch-friction.policy_constraints: Apple entitlement gating. iOS provides opaque ApplicationToken/WebDomainToken/ActivityCategoryToken, not app names; ShieldSettings covers applications, applicationCategories, webDomains and webDomainCategories (verified 2026-10-04). Google Play Accessibility/UsageStats policies (unverified).
citations: Gruning et al. 2023 PNAS 120(8) e2213114120 (figures via the authors' IC2S2 2023 extended abstract)

user-goals-and-rules.name: User goals, if-then rules and soft commitments (tighten now, loosen later)
user-goals-and-rules.rationale: Implementation intentions (94 tests, d about 0.65 [S]), voluntary commitments (SEED: 28.4% take-up, +81 pp savings [S]; SMarT 3.5% to 13.6% [S]), goal-salient reminders and fresh-start timing all converge here. User-authored triggers minimize reactance and are the only legitimate source of L3/L4 friction. Loosening follows the UK gambling RTS precedent: a 24 h cooling-off, then an explicit re-confirmation before a limit is relaxed [S]. Rules on contexts BRAKE cannot sense must be shown as inactive via the capability registry.
citations: UKGC Remote Technical Standards RTS 12 (via operator copy, unverified currency)

user-goals-and-rules.name: Budget cycle, savings goals and user-defined rules
user-goals-and-rules.rationale: User-authored context: the budget cycle start, goals, and rules written in a small rule language (for example, no food delivery after 10pm on weekdays). Includes categories the user marks as off-limits for nudges. It passes the justification test by construction and is the core context for users with no connected account. Goal progress can be derived from transfers to the user's own savings accounts.

time-of-day-context.name: Local time / weekday / late-night flag
time-of-day-context.rationale: Cheap, local regret-model feature. Evidence for a universal late-night effect is weak, and ego depletion failed replication, so use it per user, never as a universal trigger. Valid only when the timestamp comes from a real-time source, because ledger dates are often date-only.

payday-proximity.name: Payday proximity / liquidity cycle
payday-proximity.rationale: Strong evidence of spending spikes at income arrival (Stephens 2003; Gelman et al. 2014; Olafsson & Pagel 2018). Payday is also a fresh-start landmark for goal check-ins. Detection needs credit data, with manual payday entry as an MVP fallback. Breaks for irregular income.

spending-velocity-baseline.name: Per-category spending pace vs the user's own baseline
spending-velocity-baseline.rationale: The core of non-scolding post-spend insight: self-referenced (avoids peer-comparison boomerang and shame) and restores payment 'rehearsal' (Soman 2001). Needs at least 4 weeks of history and must state source coverage; suppress when coverage is partial and unknown.
spending-velocity-baseline.typical_latency: as fast as the fastest connected transaction source

notification-quick-action-labeling.name: One-tap transaction labeling via notification quick actions
notification-quick-action-labeling.rationale: Needed for transfer-vs-spend correctness and categories. Must be EVOI-driven, budgeted and one question per item. Platform limits (verified 2026-10-04): Android allows at most 3 action buttons plus RemoteInput (API 24+); iOS shows at most 2 actions when space is limited (up to 10 when unlimited; HIG detail view up to 4) plus UNTextInputNotificationAction. Android 16 auto-groups notifications (4+ ungrouped notifications from one app are grouped), so BRAKE should set explicit groups. Responses are noisy, and asking has a small question-behavior effect.
notification-quick-action-labeling.access_requirements: Android 13+ POST_NOTIFICATIONS (off by default for new installs; request in context); iOS notification authorization
notification-quick-action-labeling.typical_latency: seconds to minutes after candidate confirmed
notification-quick-action-labeling.policy_constraints: Apple 4.5.4: push notifications should not carry sensitive personal or confidential information. HIG: avoid sensitive info and never re-send for the same thing. Use VISIBILITY_PRIVATE + setPublicVersion. Android 15 cooldown dampens rapid repeats (user can disable).

notification-quick-action-labeling.name: One-tap labeling via notification actions
notification-quick-action-labeling.rationale: Android shows up to three actions, only in the expanded notification; a RemoteInput direct-reply action counts as one of the three. iOS banners show only the first two category actions (all in the expanded view). Use 'top-2 predictions + Other' on Android and 'top-2 predictions' on iOS banners, with Other via expansion or the app. Avoid YNAB-style exhaustive approval and Copilot-style queue fatigue (unverified) through uncertainty-driven asks and a daily cap.

weekly-review-session.name: Weekly batched review (at most 5 EVOI-ranked items plus one 'glad you bought' reflection)
weekly-review-session.rationale: Batching notifications improved wellbeing (Fitz et al. 2019) and turns many interruptions into one. It is also where expired questions and 'worth it' affirmations go. Scheduled on a fresh-start landmark day the user chooses.

retrospective-regret-prompt.name: Delayed satisfaction/regret check ('Glad you bought it?')
