retrospective-regret-prompt.rationale: Key per-user personalization signal, captured as remembering-self ratings. Limits: at most 1 per week, randomized selection with logged propensity, IPW estimation, delay by type (18-36 h for experiences, about 3 days after delivery for goods, before the return window ends), no totals or streaks, and stop rules. That such feedback improves personalization is a hypothesis to test.
retrospective-regret-prompt.typical_latency: 18 h to 14 days by purchase type
retrospective-regret-prompt.policy_constraints: Exclude sensitive categories (health, religion, etc.); keep the regret profile on-device

implicit-outcome-signals.name: Implicit outcomes: returns/refunds, early subscription cancellation, dropped holds, skipped checks
implicit-outcome-signals.rationale: Zero-burden revealed-preference labels that also enable remedies (return window still open). They are ambiguous: returns can mean fit or defect, so treat them as soft labels, occasionally disambiguated by one question. Depends on email and refund reconciliation adapters.

intervention-response-telemetry.name: Intervention decision and response log (including 'no intervention')
intervention-response-telemetry.rationale: Required for micro-randomized evaluation, habituation detection (proceed-through rate climbing) and a user-facing 'what BRAKE did' view. Downstream purchase is unknown, not 'no purchase', without a sensing source.
citations: Nahum-Shani et al. 2018 Ann Behav Med 52(6)

notification-engagement-telemetry.name: Notification engagement and fatigue telemetry (open/action/dismiss/channel mute)
notification-engagement-telemetry.rationale: Feeds the fatigue term in the asking cost and the adaptive budget. A muted channel is a strong negative signal, so that content moves to the digest. iOS customDismissAction reports explicit dismissals, and Android channel importance is user-controlled after creation.

mood-self-report.name: Optional 'why now?' self-report tag (planned/treat/bored/stressed/social)
mood-self-report.rationale: Mood effects on spending are real in lab studies (Lerner et al. 2004; Cryder et al. 2008), but some mood-driven spending is functional (Rick et al. 2014). Volunteered tags may help; keep them optional and local, and evaluate before shipping.

passive-emotion-inference.name: Passive emotion/mood inference (typing, voice, camera, messages, usage)
passive-emotion-inference.rationale: Surveillance-grade inference with low validity. It contradicts the brief's 'do not collect context merely because it is technically available', and emotion recognition is restricted under the EU AI Act.
passive-emotion-inference.policy_constraints: EU AI Act Art. 5(1)(f) bans emotion inference in workplaces and education (Art. 5 applies since 2 Feb 2025) [S]. Annex III lists emotion recognition as high-risk [L], with Annex III obligations reportedly deferred to 2 Dec 2027 by the Digital Omnibus on AI (in force 27 Jul 2026, reported) [S]. Art. 5(1)(a)-(b) also prohibits exploiting vulnerabilities from a specific social or economic situation.

app-usage-context.name: Cross-app usage timeline before purchase (e.g., social media then shopping app)
app-usage-context.rationale: Plausible trigger (Wilcox & Stephen 2013), but it builds a cross-app surveillance timeline. iOS exposes only opaque-token DeviceActivity thresholds. User-selected shielding (app-launch-friction) gets the benefit without the timeline.
app-usage-context.policy_constraints: Android special usage-access permission and Play policy; iOS opaque tokens only

dark-pattern-cue-detection.name: Checkout urgency/scarcity cue detection and neutral counter-messaging (browser extension)
dark-pattern-cue-detection.rationale: Mathur et al. 2019 found 1,818 dark-pattern instances across about 11K shopping sites. De-biasing urgency restores time for reflection. Detection is brittle, and claiming a merchant's timer is fake carries legal risk, so phrasing must be generic. Depends on the browser-extension adapter.
dark-pattern-cue-detection.access_requirements: Extension store review; host permissions on a shopping-domain allowlist
citations: Mathur et al. 2019 Proc ACM HCI 3(CSCW)
FTC 2022 Bringing Dark Patterns to Light

bnpl-usage-signal.name: BNPL usage and instalment schedule detection
bnpl-usage-signal.rationale: BNPL decouples payment from consumption and was linked to higher spending (Di Maggio et al. 2022; magnitude unverified). A 'BNPL due in the next 30 days' view is a high-value, non-judgmental insight. Instalment debits must link to the original purchase so they are not double-counted. Regulation as of 2026-10-04: UK deferred payment credit has been FCA-regulated since 15 Jul 2026 [S]; EU CCD2 applies from 20 Nov 2026 [S]; the US CFPB BNPL interpretive rule was withdrawn on 12 May 2025 [S].
bnpl-usage-signal.policy_constraints: None for BRAKE as an observer. UK regulated plans carry statutory disclosures that may appear in provider emails (unverified).
citations: Di Maggio, Katz & Williams 2022 NBER w30508

spending-style-self-assessment.name: Spending-style prior (Spendthrift-Tightwad scale or one plain question)
spending-style-self-assessment.rationale: Sets the direction of personalization. Tightwads already feel too much pain of paying (Rick et al. 2008), so adding friction can harm them. The plain single question can ship in the MVP.

financial-wellbeing-scale.name: CFPB Financial Well-Being Scale plus an autonomy item (outcome measure)
financial-wellbeing-scale.rationale: Anchors evaluation to wellbeing rather than engagement. Optional at onboarding and then quarterly (10-item or 5-item version; the CFPB site was not reachable to re-verify).
citations: CFPB Financial Well-Being Scale (consumerfinance.gov, not fetched)

location-geofence-context.name: Location / user-defined geofence context (e.g., at a mall)
location-geofence-context.rationale: Speculative behavioral value. Continuous location is invasive (avoid). At most, on-device geofences the user defines. Physical-store moments are better served by manual checks, QR scans and price-tag photos.

plaid-liabilities.name: Plaid Liabilities (credit card)
plaid-liabilities.rationale: Confirms card-bill payment matches (last_payment_amount/date) and gives due dates as upcoming known bills.

berlin-group-psd2-ais.name: Berlin Group NextGenPSD2 AIS (EU)
berlin-group-psd2-ais.rationale: SEPA mandateId + creditorId identify one recurring series exactly, and endToEndId is a strong key. Field population varies by ASPSP: Fineco documented endToEndId 'not used' in its v1.3 spec (2019-02-14), and BNP/Consorsbank v1.3.6 (2020) omits creditorId. These are historical snapshots, so capability facts are needed per bank, with dates.
berlin-group-psd2-ais.access_requirements: PSD2 AISP licence or licensed aggregator.
berlin-group-psd2-ais.policy_constraints: Per-ASPSP field facts above date from 2019–2020 copies in Yolt's archived provider repo; 2026 behaviour unverified.

australia-cdr-banking.name: Australia Consumer Data Right banking (CDS v1.36.0)
australia-cdr-banking.rationale: Not a launch market. It is an explicit example of no pending↔posted correlation. Its type enum (TRANSFER_OUTGOING/INCOMING, DIRECT_DEBIT) and instalmentPlanId (links transactions to an instalment plan) are useful models for transfers and EMI/BNPL.
data_fields: transactionId (mandatory unless justifiable technical reasons; not in required list)

merchant-descriptor-normalization.name: On-device merchant descriptor normalization
merchant-descriptor-normalization.rationale: Local-first merchant keys are needed for fusion and recurring grouping. Record intermediaries (PSP/POS/marketplace/app store) rather than discarding them, with a per-country dictionary plus per-user aliases.

mcc-iso-18245.name: Merchant category codes (ISO 18245)
mcc-iso-18245.rationale: Available on Plaid (beta), UK OB (optional), CDR, FinanceKit, AA credit card and UPI merchants. Cash (6010/6011), quasi-cash (6051), wires (4829), brokers (6211) and subscription (5968) codes drive type hints. The code describes the merchant, not the item bought. The cited code list is a community dataset with label errors, not ISO 18245 itself.

ntropy-enrichment.name: Ntropy transaction enrichment
ntropy-enrichment.rationale: Counterparty type person/organization answers P2P vs P2M for descriptor-only data. Recurrence types (recurring vs subscription) and groups (periodicity incl. semi-monthly since SDK 5.6.0, 2026-08-29) are a good model to copy. Coverage and pricing are unverified, and it sends data off-device.

ntropy-enrichment.name: Ntropy transaction enrichment API
ntropy-enrichment.rationale: Its model is a useful design reference: a counterparty with person or organization type plus separate intermediaries, a list of MCCs, structured location, and recurrence that distinguishes recurring (varying amount), subscription (fixed amount) and one-off. Coverage and pricing are unverified, and it is server-side.
ntropy-enrichment.policy_constraints: Raw descriptors including P2P names leave device

spade-enrichment.name: Spade card/transfer enrichment
spade-enrichment.rationale: Built for card issuers in the authorization path, and US-centric (unverified). Its transferType internal/external, isPeerToPeer, isDigitalWallet and recurrenceInfo fields are a useful reference design. Fields come from a third-party OpenAPI mirror.

visa-merchant-search.name: Visa Merchant Search
visa-merchant-search.rationale: Could not access developer.visa.com; fields, access terms and coverage are unverified. Do not plan around it.

heron-data.name: Heron Data
heron-data.rationale: Documentation not reachable; product focus and coverage unverified.

splitwise-api.name: Splitwise API
splitwise-api.rationale: paid_share/owed_share give the user's true share of shared expenses, and settle-ups explain incoming P2P credits. The self-serve API terms prohibit fee-based use, so a commercial licence is needed. Use in-app split labels until then.
splitwise-api.access_requirements: OAuth 2 or API key; commercial licence for fee-based services; explicit end-user consent.
splitwise-api.policy_constraints: 'The API is not intended for commercial use … may not be used in connection with any fee-based service'.

owned-instrument-registry.name: Owned-instrument registry (accounts, cards, wallets, handles)
owned-instrument-registry.rationale: Every transfer rule depends on 'is the other side mine?'. Build it from connections (Plaid masks are non-unique and account_id can change), alerts, self-names/tax IDs and user confirmation. Store masked identifiers only.

user-clarification-prompts.name: User clarification prompts (clerical-review zone)
user-clarification-prompts.rationale: The Fellegi–Sunter 'possible link' zone and uncertain transfer types become budgeted one-tap questions, ranked by value of information and asked once per counterparty. Answers are stored as assertions anchored to observation IDs.

probabilistic-record-linkage.name: Fellegi–Sunter fusion with TF-adjusted weights and complete linkage
probabilistic-record-linkage.rationale: Internal mechanism. Additive log-likelihood weights, term-frequency-adjusted amounts, neutral missing values, three decision zones, complete linkage, one-event-per-source and bridge-based retroactive splits prevent both over-merging and double counting.

pending-posted-supersession.name: Pending→posted supersession and retraction
pending-posted-supersession.rationale: Internal mechanism. No ecosystem guarantees the pending↔posted ID link. Handles tips, fuel/hotel/car holds, FX re-rating, descriptor and date shifts, mutable IDs and removed holds.

balance-continuity-check.name: Balance continuity / balance-after matching
balance-continuity-check.rationale: Internal mechanism. Equal balance-after on the same account is near-decisive evidence of the same event, and chain breaks reveal missing or duplicate events. AA currentBalance ('Available balance') is required in the XSD consulted, but Deposit v2.0.0 status is unverified. UK OB Balance is optional and typed (ITAV/ITBD). Plaid running_balance is hidden from public docs. Store a balanceType alongside balanceAfter.

transfer-pair-matching.name: Own-account transfer pair matching + single-leg transfer classification
transfer-pair-matching.rationale: Internal mechanism. Exact equal-and-opposite pairs between owned instruments, ranked one-to-one assignment, and an FX band only for ledger-linked legs (Sure: ±4 days auto, 30 days manual, 10% FX tolerance capped at 50%, AGPL-3.0, so re-implement, don't copy). Single-leg hints: PFC, ISO GP2P/MP2P/SWEP/TOPG (CCRD only weak), counterparty identity. Defaults to 'unclassified outflow'.

credit-card-payment-matching.name: Credit-card bill payment reconciliation
credit-card-payment-matching.rationale: Internal mechanism. Count card purchases, never the bill payment. Match the bank debit (issuer/biller descriptor, PFC LOAN_PAYMENTS_CREDIT_CARD_PAYMENT, transaction_code bill payment; ISO CCRD only as a weak hint because its semantics are ambiguous) with the card credit and liability/statement data. A payment for an unconnected card shows as 'unitemized card spending' outside discretionary pace.

p2p-p2m-classification.name: P2P vs P2M classification
p2p-p2m-classification.rationale: Internal mechanism, conservative by default. Evidence: QR/intent mc when BRAKE observed the payment, provider person-type flags, handle shape, behaviour and per-counterparty labels. Unknown-purpose P2P is excluded from discretionary pace until labelled.

transfer-type-heuristics.name: Wallet load, cash, investment, loan, rent, family and income heuristics
transfer-type-heuristics.rationale: Internal mechanism. A rules table over MCC, PFC, AA mode, ISO purpose codes and mandates, with learned answers. Wallet loads count as spending only while wallet spends are unobservable. Investment accounts are excluded from bill detection (Sure's documented failure).

refund-reversal-matching.name: Refund, reversal and chargeback matching
refund-reversal-matching.rationale: Internal mechanism. Merchant-key credits ≤ original within 120 days, with partial refunds allowed. order_id gives deterministic links. Failed-payment reversals (same RRN/OriginalRRN) become 'cancelled'. Chargebacks are provisional, and removed holds are cancellations, not refunds.

reimbursement-matching.name: Reimbursement and shared-expense matching
reimbursement-matching.rationale: Internal mechanism. Bounded subset-sum over incoming P2P credits within 45 days matching k/n of a purchase, confirmed by the user. Manual Split/Reimbursable labels in the MVP.

recurring-series-detection.name: On-device recurring-series detection
recurring-series-detection.rationale: Internal mechanism, needed to keep fixed obligations out of discretionary pace and to predict bills. Group by merchant/counterparty + currency. Use running-mean amount clusters at 7.5% (Sure's rule; Actual uses 7.5% of a reference amount, per account) and calendar-aware cadence (±2 days circular day-of-month). Statuses: EARLY/MATURE/LAPSED. Separate habits from obligations. Sure is AGPL-3.0 and Actual is MIT.

subscription-intelligence.name: Subscription intelligence (renewals, trials, price increases, duplicates, dormant)
subscription-intelligence.rationale: The MVP has only passive subscription labels plus upcoming bills. Trials and price changes need email or mandate signals, aggregator descriptors hide services, and 'dormant' needs usage data BRAKE lacks. India pre-debit notices are the early exception.

android-sms-bank-alerts.name: Android SMS bank/card/UPI alerts via READ_SMS / RECEIVE_SMS
android-sms-bank-alerts.rationale: Ubiquitous in India, and READ_SMS adds historical backfill for onboarding. Google Play lists an 'SMS-based money management' exception, but approval is discretionary. It needs sender-header allowlisting, OTP discard and on-device parsing. Android 17 delays OTP-bearing SMS by 3 hours: WebOTP SMS for all apps, and standard OTP SMS for apps targeting API 37+. Bank alerts that also carry OTP-like codes may arrive late, so targetSdk 37 needs testing. The notification listener is the fallback if Play rejects the declaration.
android-sms-bank-alerts.access_requirements: Google Play SMS/Call Log permission declaration under the 'SMS-based money management' exception (READ_SMS, RECEIVE_SMS, RECEIVE_MMS, RECEIVE_WAP_PUSH); secondary, as support.google.com was blocked. The feature must be core and promoted in the store listing. In India, Play Protect blocks sideloaded APKs requesting SMS permissions (secondary).
android-sms-bank-alerts.policy_constraints: Android 17: WebOTP SMS withheld for 3 h from non-recipient apps, all target SDKs (verified). For targetSdk 37+, standard OTP-bearing SMS are also withheld for 3 h (verified). Exposes all personal SMS, so parse only allowlisted bank headers. The TRAI suffix is a hint only: bank alerts are mostly -S, -T is mostly OTP, -P is promotional (secondary). Not available on iOS.

outlook-microsoft-graph.name: Outlook / Microsoft 365 mail via Microsoft Graph
outlook-microsoft-graph.rationale: Same value and extraction pipeline as Gmail. Publisher verification and tenant consent policies apply (unverified). Default to personal accounts to avoid employer-data issues.
outlook-microsoft-graph.access_requirements: Delegated Mail.Read or Mail.ReadBasic; Microsoft APIs Terms of Use; publisher verification; possible admin consent for work tenants (all unverified).
outlook-microsoft-graph.policy_constraints: Third-party data in mailboxes; work mailboxes contain employer data.

email-forwarding.name: User-configured email forwarding to a BRAKE inbound address
email-forwarding.rationale: Best legal profile of any email route. Consent is per message or rule, only the data the user selected flows, and no Google restricted-scope assessment applies (secondary). BRAKE is the intended recipient, which weakens the CCPA SPI and interception concerns (unverified). The server receives content, so the raw MIME must be deleted within 24 h.
email-forwarding.access_requirements: Inbound mail infrastructure; SPF/DKIM/ARC checks to accept only verified forwarding by the user.
email-forwarding.policy_constraints: Raw MIME deleted after extraction (max 24 h); no human access; encryption at rest.

imap-app-password.name: IMAP polling with stored credentials or app passwords
imap-app-password.rationale: Requires holding mailbox credentials, bypasses provider consent and Limited Use frameworks, and major providers have moved away from basic and less-secure authentication (unverified). High breach impact.

card-linked-transaction-feeds.name: Card network / issuer real-time transaction feeds (card-linked programs)
card-linked-transaction-feeds.rationale: Partnership-gated. Network program rules typically restrict data use to the program's purpose (unverified), which may exclude budgeting. Must be token-only to stay out of PCI scope.
card-linked-transaction-feeds.policy_constraints: Never handle full PAN (PCI DSS, unverified details).

qr-code-scan.name: Payment / merchant QR scan inside BRAKE
qr-code-scan.rationale: User-initiated, needs only camera permission, minimal legal risk. Payee data is third-party personal data and is only shown on the device.

receipt-ocr.name: Receipt photos / screenshots with OCR on the device
receipt-ocr.rationale: User-initiated and low risk if OCR runs on the device, Luhn-valid PANs are redacted before persistence (PCI), and images are discarded after extraction. Apple prefers out-of-process pickers and share sheets over full photo access (verified).
receipt-ocr.policy_constraints: Mandatory PAN detection/redaction; discard images unless the user pins them.

manual-entry.name: Manual transaction entry and 'Should I buy this?'
manual-entry.rationale: The graceful-degradation floor with no permissions. Apple 5.1.1(ii) bars making paid functionality depend on data access, 5.1.1(iv) asks for alternatives 'where possible', and 5.1.2(i) bars requiring system functionalities (verified). Together they support, but do not literally mandate, a fully functional manual mode. Still screen free text for PANs.

manual-entry.name: Manual transaction entry (YNAB, Spendee, Money Manager, Actual Budget)
manual-entry.rationale: The floor of graceful degradation and the only route for cash. Prior art shows only committed users sustain it, so make it fast and never required.

chrome-extension.name: Browser extension on allowlisted checkout and order pages
chrome-extension.rationale: Strong pre-spend surface with no OAuth restricted-scope gate. The Chrome Web Store single-purpose rule and Limited Use cover all data the extension handles. From 1 Aug 2026, collected data must be 'strictly necessary to the extension's disclosed single purpose' and all collection must be prominently disclosed (secondary, primary blog not fetched). Needs narrow host permissions and must never capture form fields.
chrome-extension.access_requirements: Chrome Web Store review; public Limited Use compliance statement; prominent disclosure of all collection (secondary).
chrome-extension.policy_constraints: Collection strictly necessary for the disclosed single purpose; no cross-purpose use; prominent disclosure of every collection, regardless of how close it is to the purpose (secondary).

bank-credential-scraping.name: Storing bank credentials and screen-scraping
bank-credential-scraping.rationale: Breaches bank terms (CFAA risk in the US, unverified). PSD2 SCA and 1033 move the industry away from it. Holding credentials has a large breach impact.

ios-screen-time-api.name: iOS Screen Time API (FamilyControls / ManagedSettings / DeviceActivity)
ios-screen-time-api.rationale: Private by design (opaque tokens, unverified here; stream 04 owns the details). Legal risk lies in coercive or third-party use, so use individual authorisation only, with user-configured and overridable shields.

device-location.name: Device location / geofencing
device-location.rationale: Precise geolocation is sensitive personal information under CCPA and several state laws (unverified), and background location carries platform restrictions. Coarse and user-initiated only, if ever.

calendar-events.name: Calendar events (travel, bills, occasions)
calendar-events.rationale: Contains third-party data and invites surveillance creep. Only with a narrow, user-selected scope and a clear value case.

cloud-llm-extraction.name: Cloud LLM extraction of message content - processing mechanism
cloud-llm-extraction.rationale: Avoid by default; 'later' only as a per-feature explicit opt-in. Apple 5.1.2(i) requires explicit permission before data goes to third-party AI (verified). The Workspace policy bars non-personalised training (secondary). The tier also needs GDPR processor and transfer terms, zero-retention and no-training contracts, pre-redaction, schema-constrained output with no tool use, and must never touch Gmail-derived data unless every Workspace condition is met.
cloud-llm-extraction.policy_constraints: Prompt injection: emails are attacker-controlled input.

federated-learning-dp.name: Cross-user learning via federated learning / differential privacy - processing mechanism
federated-learning-dp.rationale: Improves merchant normalisation and categorisation across users without centralising raw data; mature DP libraries exist (verified). Eligibility is set by source policy. Gmail- and Google-API-derived data is ineligible (Limited Use covers derived data), as are special-category inferences. The MVP uses per-user on-device personalisation.

india-dpdp-consent-manager.name: India DPDP Consent Manager integration
india-dpdp-consent-manager.rationale: Rule 4 Consent Manager registration commences on 13 Nov 2026, one year after G.S.R. 846(E) of 13 Nov 2025 (secondary, verbatim mirror). No registered operators were verified as of 2026-10-04. Design BRAKE's per-source consent receipts to be exportable to a Consent Manager later.

india-sms-bank-alerts.name: Android READ_SMS bank-alert parsing (Walnut/axio, Money View, early ET Money)
india-sms-bank-alerts.rationale: Excellent data: zero setup, all banks, near-real-time. But Play still requires the default SMS handler or an approved exception (confirmed current as of 2026-02-26), and the 'SMS-based money management' exception is unverified for 2026. The permission exposes the whole inbox. Android 17 delays OTP-bearing SMS by 3 h for non-exempt readers (WebOTP for all apps; standard OTP SMS when targeting API 37), so OTP-style card-authorization SMS cannot give in-spend timing. Indian prior art drifted into lending (search summaries only). Capture the same alerts via the notification listener; consider READ_SMS only as an opt-in historical backfill if the Play exception is confirmed.
india-sms-bank-alerts.typical_latency: seconds to minutes after debit; OTP-bearing SMS delayed 3 h on Android 17 for non-exempt apps
india-sms-bank-alerts.access_requirements: Google Play Permissions Declaration; default SMS handler or approved Play Console exception (rule confirmed as of 2026-02-26; 'SMS-based money management' exception name unverified)
india-sms-bank-alerts.policy_constraints: Play SMS/Call Log policy (since Jan 2019; 2019-03-09 deadline per search summaries); Android 17 SMS OTP protection (3 h delay; default SMS app and companion apps exempt)

upi-payment-app-analytics.name: PhonePe / Paytm / Google Pay India in-app payment history and spend summaries
upi-payment-app-analytics.rationale: No third-party read API (unverified). BRAKE can only reach this data through payment notifications or user-shared screenshots. These incumbents own the Indian in-spend moment with incentives tied to volume and credit, which makes them a competitive risk to watch rather than a source.

simplefin-bridge.name: SimpleFIN Bridge (user-paid aggregation bridge)
simplefin-bridge.rationale: User-held aggregator relationship ($1.50/month or $15/year, ≤90 days, ~daily updates via MX, one-time setup token) aligns incentives and keeps BRAKE out of credential custody, but setup is too technical for mainstream users. Possible 'bring your own aggregator' adapter for power users.

open-banking-ais.name: UK/EU open-banking account information (Emma, Snoop, Plum, Moneyhub, Yolt prior art)
open-banking-ais.rationale: Primary financial source for EU users and a complement to FinanceKit in the UK. Prior art shows that standalone PFMs struggle (Yolt closed, Snoop sold to a lender; both unverified) and that providers exit (GoCardless Bank Account Data closed to new accounts in July 2025), so build on multiple providers.

bank-native-spend-insights.name: Neobank in-app insights (Monzo Trends/Pots, Revolut Analytics, Starling Spaces/Spending Intelligence)
bank-native-spend-insights.rationale: No general third-party API. Verified: Monzo's developer API 'is not suitable for building public applications' and connects only to your own account or a small allow-listed set. BRAKE reaches these banks via notifications, open banking and FinanceKit (which includes Monzo in the UK). Use them as UX benchmarks (instant notifications, pots, gambling blocks; feature details unverified), not as integrations.

card-linked-offers-network.name: Visa/Mastercard card-linked offer platforms (Cardlytics, Dosh-style)
card-linked-offers-network.rationale: Provides card events only for participating merchants, and merchants fund it to increase spending, which is structurally opposed to BRAKE's mission (all details unverified).

issuer-card-controls.name: Issuer card controls: gambling blocks, category/merchant blocks, card toggles, virtual cards
issuer-card-controls.rationale: The only true in-spend hard stop (at authorization), and users opt into gambling blocks with delayed reversal (unverified). Only issuers can apply them, so a real integration requires an issuer or BaaS partnership. In MVP, BRAKE should offer 'assisted controls' that explain, deep-link and record the user's own bank controls.

ios-familycontrols-managedsettings.name: iOS Screen Time API shields (FamilyControls + ManagedSettings/ManagedSettingsUI + DeviceActivity), as used by one sec, Opal and ScreenZen
ios-familycontrols-managedsettings.rationale: The prior-art-validated pre-spend mechanism (a skippable pause at app launch). It works with no financial data and in every country. Individual authorization is available on iOS 16+. The shield action handler and the main app get only opaque tokens. The sandboxed shield-configuration extension receives display names and bundle IDs for rendering but cannot export them. From iOS 26.5, ShieldActionResponse.openParentalControlsApp lets the shield open BRAKE directly; earlier versions need a notification workaround (one sec, March 2026). Requires Apple's distribution entitlement; whether a spending-friction use case is accepted is unverified. Guideline 4.10 forbids monetizing Screen Time APIs.
ios-familycontrols-managedsettings.policy_constraints: App Review 4.10 (no monetizing Screen Time APIs); entitlement approval discretionary

android-app-launch-detection.name: Android app-launch interception via UsageStatsManager or AccessibilityService
android-app-launch-detection.rationale: Same friction mechanic as one sec and ScreenZen on Android. Prefer the usage-access route (PACKAGE_USAGE_STATS granted by the user in Settings; UsageEvents ACTIVITY_RESUMED, API 29+). For apps targeting Android 15+, an overlay holder can start a foreground service from the background only while a TYPE_APPLICATION_OVERLAY window is visible, and dataSync foreground services are capped at 6 h/24 h, which constrains continuous polling. The Accessibility route carries Play policy risk (unverified) and very broad screen access.
android-app-launch-detection.access_requirements: PACKAGE_USAGE_STATS via Settings > Usage access (ACTION_USAGE_ACCESS_SETTINGS); optional SYSTEM_ALERT_WINDOW for overlay
android-app-launch-detection.policy_constraints: Android 15 SYSTEM_ALERT_WINDOW foreground-service restriction and dataSync 6 h/24 h timeout (apps targeting 15+)

ios-shortcuts-app-open-automation.name: iOS Shortcuts personal automation 'when app opened' (one sec's original approach)
ios-shortcuts-app-open-automation.rationale: Needs no entitlement, but the user must set up each app by hand and can silently remove the automation (unverified). Keep it as a fallback if the FamilyControls entitlement is delayed or denied.

browser-extension-checkout.name: Browser extension checkout detection and purchase delay (Icebox-style; Honey as a trust cautionary tale)
browser-extension-checkout.rationale: The only mechanism with true in-spend timing for online purchases outside UPI (cart, checkout and confirmation pages). Shopping extensions proved detection works across merchants, and also produced major trust incidents (Honey, Avast; unverified). Use host permissions limited to an allow-list, process on-device, and never inject affiliate links or coupons.

merchant-order-history-import.name: Retailer order-history import (Amazon/Target-style matching)
merchant-order-history-import.rationale: Useful for splitting large marketplace charges by item. Some US PFMs reportedly added this (unverified). Retailer terms of service and page fragility need checking.

regret-feedback-prompt.name: Sparse post-purchase satisfaction/regret check-ins
regret-feedback-prompt.rationale: No mainstream PFM verified in this session does this systematically. It is BRAKE's key personalization input for the friction ladder. Limit it to a few prompts per week with neutral wording to avoid guilt loops.

subscription-detection.name: Recurring/subscription detection and renewal alerts (Rocket Money, Emma, Snoop, Copilot prior art)
subscription-detection.rationale: Derived from fused transactions, email and mandate notices with no new sensor needed. Prior art shows it is a strong engagement driver. Avoid success-fee monetization and cancellation dark patterns (Cleo FTC case; unverified).

iso-18245-mcc.name: ISO 18245 Merchant Category Code (cross-source field)
iso-18245-mcc.rationale: The most widely available merchant-level category prior. It arrives post-spend on card feeds and pre-spend through QR codes (EMV tag 52 is mandatory; UPI mc is optional). The acquirer assigns it per merchant account, so it is ambiguous for supercenters, marketplaces and payment facilitators. Normalize the format, and ship it with a comprehensive sensitive-code deny-list. The originally proposed list was incomplete.
iso-18245-mcc.access_requirements: Arrives inside other connected sources. The ISO standard itself is paywalled, and whether the 2003 edition is current is unverified (iso.org blocked). The community greggles table (981 rows) lacks newer codes such as 5552 and 5723.

card-network-merchant-apis.name: Card-network merchant lookup APIs (Visa Merchant Search, Mastercard Merchant Identifier)
card-network-merchant-apis.rationale: These APIs map descriptors to cleansed merchant names, addresses and MCCs. Access is likely limited to partners, and fields and terms are unverified because the developer portals were unreachable. Open brand data plus aggregator enrichment cover the MVP.

eu-nextgenpsd2-card-accounts.name: Berlin Group NextGenPSD2 card account transactions
eu-nextgenpsd2-card-accounts.rationale: The richest merchant record among the open-banking standards: card-acceptor ID, address and phone, terminal ID, a timestamp from the merchant's acceptance system, and a 4-character MCC. Card-account endpoints are not offered by every bank (unverified).

au-cdr-banking.name: Australia Consumer Data Right banking transactions
au-cdr-banking.rationale: BankingTransactionV2 includes merchantName and merchantCategoryCode for outgoing merchant payments, BPAY billerCode, billerName and crn, and a DIRECT_DEBIT type, which are good signals for upcoming bills. The standard does not guarantee that a pending transaction can be matched to its posted version.

br-open-finance-credit-cards.name: Open Finance Brasil credit-card transactions
br-open-finance-credit-cards.rationale: Exposes payeeMCC as type number, format integer, which loses leading zeros, and supports filtering by MCC (creditCardPayeeMCC). Version 2.3.1 exists alongside 2.3.0 with the same field. It is the main category source in Brazil, because Pix QR codes commonly carry MCC 0000.

upi-qr-scan.name: UPI QR / intent merchant fields read by BRAKE
upi-qr-scan.rationale: The only source in India that can give the merchant's VPA, name and, when present, MCC before the user pays. Per the v1.6 spec (secondary transcription), mc is optional, while pa and pn are mandatory and tr is mandatory for merchant and dynamic links. A missing mc must be treated as unknown. The scan is user-initiated, so privacy cost is low. tr, pa and mid/msid/mtid later join the bank alert or RRN.
upi-qr-scan.access_requirements: None for reading a user-scanned QR

emvco-merchant-qr.name: EMVCo merchant-presented QR (incl. Pix, SGQR-type schemes)
emvco-merchant-qr.rationale: One TLV parser covers many national QR schemes. Mandatory tags give the MCC (52), merchant name (59) and city (60), which provides location without a location permission. Optional tags give postal code (61), static vs dynamic (01: 11 or 12, so it may be absent) and reference, bill and terminal labels (62). Pix generators commonly set MCC 0000 (a BCB mandate is unverified). Tags were checked against an open-source parser because emvco.com was blocked.

google-places-api.name: Google Places API (New)
google-places-api.rationale: Rich place data, including primary_type, types and price_level, but per-user lookups leak purchases or locations to Google. Under the non-EEA Service Specific Terms (last modified 2026-06-10), content must not be used with a non-Google map (14.2). Under the separate EEA terms (same date), it must not be used with any map apart from lat/lng and place_id (§15.1), and only for the 'EEA Permitted Uses' (§15.2). Both cap lat/lng caching at 30 days, while place_id may be cached. Open data covers store type without these costs.
google-places-api.access_requirements: Google Maps Platform billing account (pricing unverified); the applicable terms depend on whether the billing address is in the EEA
google-places-api.policy_constraints: Non-EEA Service Specific Terms 14.1-14.3; EEA Service Specific Terms 15.1-15.4; General Service Terms §3 (place_id cacheable)

apple-mapkit-poi.name: Apple MapKit POI search
apple-mapkit-poi.rationale: iOS-only and its categories are coarse: a single 'store' category covers all retail. Queries go to Apple, so it is useful only as a user-initiated 'what is this place' fallback.
data_fields: MKPointOfInterestCategory (store, foodMarket, restaurant, cafe, pharmacy, gasStation, hotel, nightlife, ...)
apple-mapkit-poi.policy_constraints: App Review 5.1.5 for any location use

osm-name-suggestion-index.name: OpenStreetMap name-suggestion-index brand dictionary
osm-name-suggestion-index.rationale: BSD-3 licensed brand dictionary that can be bundled on-device. Entries have Wikidata IDs, country-scoped locationSet and matchNames, and an OSM category tag, for example Starbucks Q37158 amenity=cafe and DMart Q5203271 shop=supermarket (India only). Its Wikidata IDs make a good stable merchant key, and nothing leaves the device.

overture-maps-places.name: Overture Maps Places
overture-maps-places.rationale: About 81.5M places in the September 2026 release (81,455,423 across nine sources), licensed CDLA-Permissive-2.0, Apache-2.0 or CC0, with no OSM data. Joining it to OSM data may still create an ODbL derivative. Offers basic_category (about 280 labels), taxonomy (about 2,300 categories), brand Wikidata IDs, confidence and operating_status. Places is released monthly and the taxonomy is revised quarterly. categories was removed in September 2026, and the July 2026 re-matching caused one-time GERS ID churn. Pin the release, and remap stored keys through bridge files.
dedup_keys: GERS id (stable across releases subject to conflation; remap via bridge files)
overture-maps-places.access_requirements: Open bulk download from S3/Azure; releases discoverable through the STAC catalog (file format not stated on the guide page)

channel-indicators.name: Online vs physical / card-present indicators (derived)
channel-indicators.rationale: Fuses several indicators into channel and p_online: Plaid payment_channel, Plaid location presence (absent location does not mean online), UK Open Banking AuthorisationType, Berlin Group terminal ID and acceptor address, static vs dynamic QR, direct-marketing and digital-goods MCCs, and receipts. Channel decides the type of intervention: online purchases allow a pause, in-store ones need speed.

recurring-detection-on-device.name: On-device recurring merchant and subscription detector
recurring-detection-on-device.rationale: Users without Plaid or Ntropy need recurring and subscription detection too. The detector groups transactions by merchant and amount band, finds the cadence from the median gap with a regularity check, and uses Plaid-style early, mature and tombstoned status. MCC and dictionary priors raise subscription probability, and price changes are flagged.

per-user-merchant-history.name: Per-user merchant history aggregates
per-user-merchant-history.rationale: Per-merchant aggregates: visit counts, median ticket, label distribution, regret counts and typical channel. Drives the personal pre-spend context ('6th time this month'), unusual-ticket alerts and fewer clarifying questions. Kept on-device as aggregates only.

brake-merchant-resolver.name: BRAKE on-device merchant resolution pipeline
brake-merchant-resolver.rationale: Pipeline: clean the descriptor, split off any intermediary, look up aliases (provider IDs, VPA), match the brand dictionary (NSI) and the local POI file (Overture), apply MCC and PFC priors, then user history, with server enrichment only by opt-in. Output is a stable key (a Wikidata ID, an Overture ID or a salted hash) with store type, channel, sensitive flag and the steps used for provenance.

device-clock-context.name: Device clock: time of day, day of week, holidays
device-clock-context.rationale: Needs no permission and is derived. Purchase-time features need minute-precision timestamps: Plaid authorized_datetime may contain default 00:00:00 values and the AA card txnDate is date-only, so features must abstain when precision is coarse. Use it as a personal pattern, not a moral rule.

payday-detection.name: Payday / income-cycle detection from inflows
payday-detection.rationale: Derived from data already consented to: Plaid inflow streams with income categories and income_source counterparties, AA or SMS credits, and Open Banking purpose codes. Feeds pacing and free-to-spend. Activate only when income confidence is at least 0.7 after 2 or more cycles. Income stays on-device and is used only to protect the user, never for offers.

upcoming-obligations.name: Upcoming known bills and recurring obligations
upcoming-obligations.rationale: Merges recurring series, the AA credit-card summary (due date and minimum due), Australia CDR BPAY and direct-debit entries, mandates and renewal emails. From these it computes money already committed before the next payday and free-to-spend, which must abstain when the balance is more than 24 hours old.

spending-velocity.name: Spending velocity and burst detection
spending-velocity.rationale: Rolling spend over 24 hours, 7 days and the cycle to date, a robust z-score against the user's own baseline, and burst detection over 2 hours. It must exclude transfers, card-bill payments, refunds and likely duplicates. Feeds the brief's 'above your usual pace' insights.

regret-feedback-history.name: Prior regret patterns (retrospective feedback)
regret-feedback-history.rationale: Sparse feedback asked 24-72 hours after a purchase, stored as regret rates per segment and per merchant. Personalizes friction once a segment has at least 5 ratings. Cap prompts at 2 per week, never prompt on sensitive or essential categories, and let the user reset what was learned.

travel-context-derived.name: Travel context derived from foreign transactions and travel MCCs
travel-context-derived.rationale: Infers travel without GPS or calendar access. Signals: foreign currency or country (Plaid location.country, FinanceKit foreignCurrencyAmount, Berlin Group currencyExchange) and bookings with airline, lodging or travel-agency MCCs. Switches to travel mode, which offers a trip budget and suppresses unusual-merchant alerts.

timezone-change-signal.name: OS time-zone change broadcast / notification
timezone-change-signal.rationale: Android's ACTION_TIMEZONE_CHANGED is exempt from the implicit-broadcast limits, so a manifest receiver still gets it, and it needs no permission. On iOS, NSNotification.Name.NSSystemTimeZoneDidChange is posted when the time zone changes, but through NotificationCenter to a running app only, so iOS should also compare the time zone on each launch or resume. It is a coarse, permission-free travel signal that also keeps local-time features correct after a flight.
timezone-change-signal.typical_latency: 0 s (Android); on next launch or resume (iOS)

email-booking-extraction.name: Travel and reservation extraction from email bookings
email-booking-extraction.rationale: Uses the schema.org Reservation types (Flight, Lodging, RentalCar, Train, FoodEstablishment; properties reservationId, reservationFor, totalPrice, reservationStatus) to know trip dates and explain charges. Use it only if email is already connected for receipts; never request email access for travel context alone.
email-booking-extraction.access_requirements: Email adapter (Gmail restricted scopes, covered by email stream)

background-location-geofencing.name: Background location, geofencing and visit monitoring
background-location-geofencing.rationale: Fails the Context Justification Test: purchase location can be derived after the fact, the lift is unproven, users don't expect it, and it reveals sensitive places. It also needs ACCESS_BACKGROUND_LOCATION (a settings-page grant on Android 11+), is limited to 100 geofences per app with 2-6 minute latency on Android and 20 monitored conditions on iOS, and iOS visit monitoring (CLVisit) is effectively a place-history log. At most, research an opt-in, user-named, on-device, expiring 'trouble spots' mode.
background-location-geofencing.policy_constraints: Google Play background-location declaration (unverified details); Apple App Review 5.1.5

user-initiated-location.name: Session-scoped, user-initiated location (Android 17 location button, approximate location)
user-initiated-location.rationale: Android 17 (API 37) adds a location button that grants precise location for the current session only. Google Play requires it for apps targeting Android 17 whose location features are all session-based, and it is still experimental. Approximate location is about 3 km² on Android, and iOS offers a reduced-accuracy mode. These pass the user-expectation check, but the lift is questionable versus the merchant city from a QR scan or simply asking the user.
data_fields: approximate or precise location for one session
user-initiated-location.policy_constraints: Play policy for session-only location apps targeting Android 17

calendar-read-access.name: Calendar read access (EventKit full, READ_CALENDAR, Google Calendar, Microsoft Graph)
calendar-read-access.rationale: Fails the Context Justification Test: travel and bills can be derived from other data, calendars are a social and professional context users don't expect a spending app to read, and they reveal medical and religious events and other people's names. Let users enter events themselves instead.

calendar-write-only-reminders.name: Write-only calendar reminders for renewals and bills
calendar-write-only-reminders.rationale: BRAKE adds renewal and bill reminders without reading the calendar. Options: iOS 17 write-only access ('Don't request full access if your app's features only need write-only access'); EventKitUI, which needs no permission; Android ACTION_INSERT, which needs no WRITE_CALENDAR; and Google calendar.app.created, limited to an app-owned calendar.

ambient-sensors.name: Other ambient signals (weather, activity recognition, health/sleep, Wi-Fi/BLE, contacts, installed apps)
ambient-sensors.rationale: Fails the derive-first, user-expectation and sensitive-inference checks; time of day plus personal regret history is a better proxy for 'tired'. Apple 5.1.2(iii) forbids secretly building a user profile, and 5.1.2(iv) forbids collecting installed-app data for analytics.

alltheplaces.name: All the Places brand store-location dataset
alltheplaces.rationale: CC-0 point-of-interest data scraped weekly from brands' own store-locator pages, published as per-spider GeoJSON with brand and brand:wikidata, address, phone, opening_hours and OSM-style tags. It joins to NSI keys and gives fresher chain-branch locations for store-level merchant keys and QR-city matching. It covers chains only, and spiders break when sites change. Overture already ingests it (1.8M places in September 2026), so compare coverage before adding a separate pack.
alltheplaces.policy_constraints: CC-0 data, MIT code; no attribution required, though attribution is courteous
